jobs.title: Cymer Field Service Engineer
jobs.description:
Introduction to the job

ASML /Cymer is one of the world’s leading manufacturers of lithography systems that help enable Moore’s Law and the creation of increasingly powerful and capable electronic devices. Our San Diego-based light source division, Cymer, is renowned for developing both deep ultraviolet (DUV) lithography light sources and next generation extreme ultraviolet (EUV) light sources. As the world’s leading semiconductor equipment manufacturer, ASML enables chipmakers to produce cheaper, speedier chips – and to produce them faster – thereby enabling all the technology you use today. The systems we produce integrate several large and sophisticated machines, themselves each a feat of engineering innovation, precision, and speed.

We are a multinational company with over 70 locations in 16 countries, headquartered in Veldhoven, the Netherlands. We have 18 office locations around the United States including main offices in Wilton, CT, Chandler, AZ, San Jose, CA and San Diego, CA (EUV laser source creation).

In the Cymer Light Source (CLS) division in San Diego, we design and manufacture Deep Ultraviolet (DUV) lasers, used directly in the chipmaking process. Far from a basic “consumer” laser, these machines are complex, powerful, and flexible. The lasers we make require: durable and high-speed precise motion-controlled optics to maintain wavelength to femtometer accuracy under high laser powers; advanced materials to endure the harsh Fluorine-rich environments and high powers; clever mechanical designs to allow high performance and fit all the parts within a confined space, but still allow easy manufacturing and servicing.

If you have a passion for technology and innovation you’ll want to check us out. Be a part of progress.

One Company, One Goal, Limitless Innovation. It's our people that make the difference.

Role and responsibilities

The Field Service Engineer provides onsite field service support through the performance of installations, upgrades, repairs, and maintenance of complex capital equipment and systems. Troubleshoots either to resolve issues directly or through referring advanced issues to technical support resources. Acts as a customer service advocate, instructing customers in the operation and maintenance of the system.

This is a shift position,12 hrs. per day. Shift consists of both days and nights. , 3 – 4 – 4 – 3 compressed work week. Must be flexible to train during day shift for 3 – 6 months after scheduled new hire laser training.

Analyzes, diagnoses, and troubleshoots Cymer equipment problems via telephone or at customer site.
Performs installation, repair, retrofits, upgrades and preventive maintenance on Cymer equipment installed at customer sites.
Maintains an assigned installation equipment base. This includes providing primary support, forecasting, conducting customer support meetings, and ensuring regular communication with the customer.
Assists customers in the receipt, installation, and testing of company equipment.
Conducts equipment troubleshooting, analysis, and debugging in support of installation or operating activities.
May provide service education to customer’s service and operations staff.
Ensures that parts are available and as specified for service requirements.
Maintains appropriate tools are on hand and as required.
Travels as required for the purposes of performing service activities at customer sites or backfilling for other Cymer Field Service Engineers.
Completes service, expense reports, and other administrative responsibilities in accordance with Cymer’s procedures and with supervisor’s approval.
Uses company technical documentation and provides feedback for improvement.
Performs other duties as assigned.

Education and experience

Minimum High School diploma or equivalent required. Associates Degree or higher preferred, Similar Military / vocational experiences is a plus.
Minimum of two (2) years of field service engineering experience required or relevant work related experience is required.
Minimum of one (1) year experience in optics, laser, and/or semiconductor manufacturing equipment experience is preferred.
Laser and vacuum experience preferred.
Has led one installation or significantly contributed to the successful installation of products at multiple sites.

Skills

Working at the cutting edge of tech, you’ll always have new challenges and new problems to solve – and working together is the only way to do that. You won’t work in a silo. Instead, you’ll be part of a creative, dynamic work environment where you’ll collaborate with supportive colleagues. There is always space for creative and unique points of view. You’ll have the flexibility and trust to choose how best to tackle tasks and solve problems.
To thrive in this job, you’ll need the following skills:

Ability to apply advanced knowledge of installation, maintenance/repair, and troubleshooting at both the module and system level, while seeking expertise of more senior field service engineers where required.
Ability to read and analyze opto-mechanical and electronic schematics.
Protocol, and Computer Networking.
Effective communication, perseverance, problem solving, customer support focus and team oriented.
Must be able to successfully meet customer site access requirements such as: background checks, safety training, and cleanroom access (gowning and breathing apparatus).
Excellent written and verbal communications skills.

Onsite field service support, troubleshooting and resolving issues. Customer support advocate, guiding customers in operation and maintenance of the system.

jobs.description:
Summary
#LI-Hybrid
Location: Dublin, Ireland

This role is based in Dublin, Ireland. Novartis is unable to offer relocation support for this role. Please only apply if this location is accessible for you.

Complex data are integral to our work in clinical studies. This position is part of the Advanced Quantitative Sciences (AQS) Technology & AI function at Novartis. Our mission is to use automation and artificial intelligence to unlock the potential of complex scientific data, speed up quantitative decision-making in clinical trials, and bring innovative medicines to patients faster.

Our new Statistical Computing Environment (SCE) is changing how AQS works, from how programming and QC are done in the SCE to how outputs flow across the AQS Digital workflow. The AI & Automation Catalyst turns that technology into lasting changes in daily practice. You will co-lead, with engineering and business partners, the rollout of AI and automation into the how we generate evidence. That covers redesigning processes, being a technical champion, bringing stakeholders along, and making sure new ways of working are adopted, compliant and deliver measurable value.

This is a technical role and a change role, not one or the other. You are credible enough with engineers and programmers to shape solutions and challenge designs. You are also skilled enough with people to move senior stakeholders, line functions and skeptical end users from pilot to standard practice.
About the Role

Major accountabilities:

Leads translation of AI and automation into production. Owns the adoption roadmap for AI/automation that includes tools that span from the current-state process baseline, through future-state design and pilots, to scaled rollout.
Connects technology and business. Translates needs into clear requirements, user stories and acceptance criteria. Works hand in hand with AI & Data Engineering, SCE platform teams and IT to shape solutions. Makes informed technical trade-offs across build vs. configure, human-in-the-loop design and validation effort.
Manages stakeholders and influences without authority. Builds strong relationships across statistical programming, biostatistics, QA, line leadership and governance forums. Gets sponsors aligned, handles resistance, and turns different priorities into agreed decisions in a matrix organisation.
Redesigns processes and operating models. Redesigns QC and review workflows so AI and automation inform the standard process, and are not a bolt on. Updates SOPs, work instructions, RACI and role definitions with process owners.
Drives adoption and builds capability. Designs and runs change plans covering communications, training, champion networks, office hours and feedback loops. Tracks adoption and sentiment, and adjusts the approach based on the evidence.
Keeps change safe, compliant and inspection-ready. Understands GxP, computerised system validation and data integrity in drug development. Makes sure AI-assisted steps have the right risk assessment, human oversight, traceability and documentation. Works with QA and Compliance so the change holds up in audit.
Stays hands-on where it matters. Prototypes, reviews code and runs proofs of concept when that speeds up a decision or unblocks adoption. Offers expert guidance on complex data and automation problems.
Remains current with industry trends, and brings in external good practice on AI adoption in regulated environments through industry consortia, conferences and publications.
Fosters a culture of continuous learning, constructive challenge and innovation. Role-models transparent, responsible use of AI.

Essential Requirements:
MSc or PhD in Computer Science, Data Science, AI/ML, Biostatistics, Bioinformatics or another quantitative discipline. Equivalent experience considered.
Extensive experience in technology delivery in life sciences or another regulated industry, with at least 3 years leading technology-enabled business change or transformation.
Proven record of taking AI/automation or digital solutions from pilot to scaled, sustained adoption, with measured business impact.
Working knowledge of clinical data flows and statistical programming (e.g. SDTM/ADaM, TFLs, double programming/QC), statistical computing environments, and GxP/CSV expectations.
Solid technical foundation: can read and write R and/or Python, and understands software engineering practices (version control, testing, CI/CD, release management). Practical understanding of LLM/agentic AI applications and their limits, including evaluation, human-in-the-loop design and risk.
Excellent stakeholder management and influencing skills at all levels, including senior leadership. Comfortable challenging and handling resistance in a matrix environment.
Fluent English, verbal and written. Can tell a clear, evidence-led story to both technical and non-technical audiences.

Desirable Requirements:
Change management certification, Lean/Six Sigma, or product owner/agile certification or experience.
Experience with Domino or similar analytics platforms, and with CDISC initiatives / metadata-driven automation.
External profile through publications, industry working groups or conference talks.

The only way to ignite change is to build the best team. We believe unifying software, intelligent automation, and data is the answer to delivering quality and flexibility at scale. jobs.title: Junior Materials Engineer
jobs.description:
Junior Materials Engineer

We are seeking a proactive and detail-oriented Junior Materials Engineer to join our Manufacturing team. This is an exciting opportunity to develop your expertise in materials selection, testing, analysis and product development within a fast-paced manufacturing environment. Working closely with Engineering, Quality, Purchasing and Production teams, you will support the evaluation of materials, investigate material-related issues and contribute to continuous improvement initiatives that enhance product performance, quality, sustainability and manufacturing efficiency. This role is ideal for someone with a qualification in Engineering or a related discipline who is looking to build a successful career in engineering and innovation.

Duties Include:

· Support the selection, evaluation and specification of materials for new and existing products, ensuring suitability for intended applications.

· Conduct material testing, inspections and analysis to assess performance, durability, reliability and compliance with product specifications and quality standards.

· Investigate material failures, product defects and quality concerns, identifying root causes and contributing to corrective and preventive actions.

· Provide material-related technical input and recommendations to support product development and innovation projects.

· Collaborate with manufacturing, quality, design and engineering teams to improve product performance, manufacturability and production efficiency.

· Analyse test data and prepare technical reports, presentations and recommendations for internal stakeholders.

· Support supplier assessments, material approvals and the qualification of new materials and components.

· Maintain accurate records of material specifications, test results and engineering documentation.

· Ensure compliance with relevant industry standards, regulatory requirements and internal quality management systems.

· Participate in continuous improvement initiatives focused on material performance, sustainability, quality enhancement and cost reduction.

· Research emerging materials, technologies and manufacturing processes to support product innovation and business objectives.

· Assist in resolving production and customer-related technical issues involving materials and product performance.

· Contribute to environmental and sustainability initiatives relating to materials, manufacturing processes and product development.

· Adhere to all health, safety and environmental procedures while carrying out engineering activities.

· Participate in team meetings, project reviews and engineering problem-solving activities.

· Undertake any other duties and responsibilities reasonably assigned by management.

Skills and Characteristics

· Bachelor’s Degree in Science or Engineering

· Excellent attention to detail and ability to analyse data effectively.

· Strong communication and interpersonal skills.

· Excellent attention to detail

· Effective teamwork skills are essential

What do we offer?

At Tricel, we care about you and your progression. As well as a competitive salary and benefits package, we offer:

· Excellent development and growth opportunities

· A supportive and collaborative culture

· Opportunities to Travel

· A fun and dynamic work environment

· Team oriented atmosphere

· Good work, life balance

· Opportunity to work across countries and cultures

· Employee Assistance Programme

· Tax-free vouchers up to the value of €1,500

· Sports and Social club

· Health and Wellbeing initiatives

· Enhanced Maternity leave

· Health Insurance Contribution

· Free onsite parking

About Tricel

Tricel, a family-run business, was founded in 1973 by Anne Stack and Con Stack. This year marks the company’s 50th year in business. The company began by producing

products from glass-reinforced plastics (GRP). It expanded its exports and established manufacturing facilities throughout the UK and Europe by implementing a comprehensive growth strategy in the 1990s and 2000s. The Stack family leads Tricel, which provides market-leading solutions in over 50 countries. Among the markets served by the company are storage tanks, pumps, sewage treatment tanks, construction products, and lubricant and composite distribution. With its headquarters in Killarney, the Tricel Group consists of 15 companies across Europe, including seven manufacturing facilities. The company employs more than 600 people at these locations. The company has grown domestically and internationally by manufacturing locally, exporting, partnering with local distributors, and acquiring companies that enhance its product capabilities and geographical reach. In the next five years, the company’s roadmap for growth will continue to be based on three main pillars: Customer Excellence, Innovation & Sustainability.

If you are interested in joining Tricel please email HR@tricel.ie today with your CV and cover letter. We look forward to hearing from you.

Financial Accountant (Newly Qualified)

Finance | Dublin | Permanent

About Life Scientific

Life Scientific operates in a $250 billion global crop protection market.

We reverse-engineer off-patent products and deliver them with the same quality, safety and performance as the original - operating across multiple countries, currencies and regulatory environments.

As we scale internationally, complexity increases.

More entities.
More intercompany.
More inventory.
More moving parts.

Our Finance team is not a reporting function.

It is an enabling function.

And we are growing it deliberately.

The Opportunity

This role exists because we are expanding.

Not replacing. Building.

As a financial accountant, you will join a high-performing, commercially engaged finance team supporting a multi-entity, multi-currency business.

This is not a narrow ledger role.

You will gain exposure across:

Group reporting

Technical accounting

Audit

Tax compliance

Budgeting & forecasting

Cross-functional business partnering

You will work closely with senior leadership and operational teams - embedding financial clarity into a business that is moving quickly.

We are open to candidates from 1–5 years PQE.

What matters most is not just experience - but mindset.

This role is for you if you…

You enjoy structure - but don’t hide behind it.

You care about the integrity of the general ledger.

You instinctively question reconciling items that don’t feel right.

You can explain complex accounting clearly to non-finance colleagues.

You want to understand the business behind the numbers.

You’re comfortable operating in a multi-entity environment where intercompany and consolidation matter.

You don’t wait to be told what’s wrong - you go looking for it.

You are ambitious - and see this as a stepping stone into broader finance leadership.

You prefer building something in a scaling company over maintaining something static.

What You’ll Own

Financial Reporting & Ledger Integrity

Lead preparation of monthly and quarterly management reporting packs

Maintain general ledger integrity across multiple entities (accruals, deferrals, intercompany, reclasses)

Support group consolidation activities in a multi-currency environment

Ensure reporting is accurate, structured and delivered on time

Audit & Compliance

Own key elements of statutory audit preparation

Liaise directly with external auditors

Manage VAT, Intrastat and related compliance filings

Ensure adherence to IFRS / FRS 102 accounting standards

Commercial & Operational Support

Partner with Supply Chain, R&D and Commercial teams

Provide financial insight supporting operational decision-making

Contribute to budgeting and forecasting cycles

Support analysis that informs growth and investment decisions

Process & Scale

Contribute to automation and process improvement initiatives

Strengthen controls as the business grows

Support and mentor junior finance colleagues

What You Bring

You are a fully qualified accountant (ACA, ACCA or equivalent).

You bring:

1–5 years’ PQE

Strong grounding in technical accounting principles (IFRS / FRS 102)

Experience in multi-entity, multi-currency environments (group consolidation exposure is highly valuable)

Comfort operating in a deadline-driven, fast-paced setting

Clear communication skills - able to explain financial matters simply

Highly beneficial:

Audit training from a recognised practice

Exposure to manufacturing, stock or inventory environments

Experience working within ERP systems

But more important than background:

You are curious.
Structured.
Commercially aware.
And motivated to grow beyond traditional accounting boundaries.

What Success Looks Like

Within 18–36 months, you will have:

Strengthened ledger control and reporting clarity across entities

Built credibility with senior leadership and operational teams

Played a visible role in audit and compliance cycles

Contributed meaningfully to budgeting and forecasting

Positioned yourself for broader responsibility within Finance

Why Join Life Scientific?

Because this is not a static reporting role.

It is a growth role.

You will:

Gain exposure across technical, operational and commercial finance

Work in a flat, fast-moving structure

Have visibility with senior leadership

Help shape processes in a scaling international business

Life Scientific is building deliberately.

And this role is part of that build.

If you want early-career breadth, real responsibility and the chance to grow within a business that is scaling internationally - this is your platform.

The Fresh Breath Clinic is hiring a dental nurse to lead our decontamination unit and support our clinical team chairside.

The Fresh Breath Clinic is a busy, well-established practice with four surgeries and a skilled, supportive team. We’re a growing practice, and we put our people first.

*The role*

This role is primarily LDU, with the remainder of your time chairside. You’ll keep our instruments safe, sterile and ready for four surgeries, and help us maintain very high infection control standards. We value this work, which is why we’re creating a dedicated role for it.

*A typical day*

You’ll start by checking and preparing the LDU and machines, then process instruments as they come through from the surgeries, completing records as you go. When the LDU is up to date, you’ll support the clinical team chairside or help turn over surgeries, finishing the day with end-of-day checks and everything set up for tomorrow.

* Keep all surgeries supplied with sterile instrument sets

_Nursing_

* Chairside assistance and surgery turnaround when required
* Taking medical histories and entering notes accurately on Exact
* Welcoming patients and keeping your allocated surgery clean and stocked

*What we’re looking for*

* Qualified (desirable) dental nurse, registered with the Dental Council of Ireland [or eligible to register]
* Dental experience; LDU/decontamination experience strongly preferred
* Good knowledge of decontamination and IPC standards
* Experience with Exact dental software (desirable)
* Organised, methodical, reliable and detail-focused

jobs.title: Psychologist - Irish Prison Service, Castlerea
jobs.description:
Clinical or Counselling Psychologist - Irish Prison Service

Locum role - Castlerea Prison, Co. Roscommon

Clinical or Counselling Psychologist required for locum assignment in Castlerea Prison, a closed, medium security prison for adult males. It is the committal prison for remand and sentenced prisoners in Connacht and also takes committals from counties Cavan, Donegal and Longford.

The IPS Psychology Service is a national, public psychological service. Psychologists work as part of broad multi-disciplinary teams (MDTs) within all prisons across the country. The Service holds the principle of equivalence of care as its foundation. Its integrated model of care is bio-psycho-social, strengths-based and recovery focused and balances this with the principles of Risk, Need and Responsivity (RNR). Services are organised within a layered care model.

As the IPS Psychology Service provides an integrated care model, it accepts referrals for a broad range of mental health and criminogenic needs. The Service prides itself on thorough, individualised, evidence-based assessment and interventions with clients, and to this end, there are excellent Continuing Professional Development opportunities for all staff members.

Castlerea Prison is a closed, medium security prison for adult males. The population profile is otherwise heterogeneous, consisting of men from across the adult age profile, who may be on remand or serving a broad spectrum of sentence lengths.

At any one time it accommodates approximately 300 men. As a locum Psychologist, you will support the Senior Psychologist and the multi-disciplinary team (MDT) to assess and intervene with people who have been referred to the IPS Psychology Service in relation to any, or a combination of the following: a) mental health difficulties including, but not exclusive to: Mood and Anxiety Disorders, Disorders of Personality and Behaviour, complex-Post Traumatic Stress Disorder, Self-Harm and Suicidal Behaviour, Eating Disorders, Psychosis and Schizophrenia, Addiction, and b) offence-specific needs, including the need for formal offence related risk assessments, preparation of Parole Board reports, offence related group and individual work, complex case consultation and risk management work. In addition to the above presentations, the Service works with people presenting with developmental disorders, intellectual difficulties, cognitive decline, traumatic brain injuries, people with limited literacy, and people from a wide variety of cultural (national and international) backgrounds.

Interventions include a variety of evidence based group and 1:1 interventions.

Prison-based Psychologists have regular contact with community agencies involved in the support and resettlement of people leaving custody.

They also work with the families and carers of those in custody. Where clinically appropriate, IPS Psychologists provide time-limited community intervention(s) to support a client’s transition from custody to community.

The Service plays a critical role in supporting the broader IPS organisation (and Criminal Justice Agency partners, as required) through consultation, training and education.

Placements are available for psychologists-in-training and the Service provides regular input to training programmes. Psychologists are also involved in research in conjunction with various Universities.

Essential qualifications and competencies

Candidates must:

(a) Be eligible for graduate membership of the Psychological Society of Ireland (PSI) or the British Psychological Society (BPS).

and

(b) (i) Hold a postgraduate professional qualification in Clinical Psychology recognised by PSI. (Applicants with qualifications obtained outside of Ireland must obtain a statement of equivalence in Clinical Psychology from the Department of Health);

or

(b) (ii) Hold a postgraduate professional qualification in Counselling Psychology recognised by PSI. (Applicants with qualifications obtained outside of Ireland must obtain a statement of equivalence in Counselling Psychology from the Department of Health);

(Potential applicants who are considering relocating to Ireland and may have queries or concerns relating to the current Irish validation process should feel free to contact the IPS Psychology Service through CPL Healthcare to discuss and seek support on the process).

In addition to the above, the following are desirable but not essential requirements:

-Experience in addressing emotional, mental health and / or offence-related difficulties with a forensic or inpatient population

-Experience of providing consultation, education, guidance and support to multidisciplinary colleagues.

-Further therapeutic or research qualifications

For further information, please contact Brian Murray on +353 1 482 5421 / +353 872226752 or email brian.murray@cplhealthcare.com

jobs.title: Designated Support Engineer
jobs.description:
As a Designated Support Engineer (DSE) at Asana, you'll be the named technical support partner for a set of our enterprise customers. This is a hands-on role focused on delivering high quality, customer centric service to our most engaged users, ensuring that entitled customers receive responsive, thoughtful, and proactive support.

In addition to owning support for your assigned accounts, you'll also contribute to broader case queues, working cross-functionally with teams across Customer Support (including Technical Account Managers), Customer Success, and Product to help drive resolution and share insights. You'll thrive in this role if you're detail oriented, collaborative, and passionate about helping customers succeed.

This role is based in our Dublin office with an office-centric hybrid schedule. The standard in-office days are Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday. Most Asanas have the option to work from home on Wednesdays. Working from home on Fridays depends on the type of work you do and the teams with which you partner. What you'll achieve

Serve as the named support partner for designated customers, providing guidance on issues, features, and best practices to accelerate adoption, optimize usage, and build long-term trusted customer relationships.

Manage the full lifecycle of product cases for your assigned customers—triaging, troubleshooting, providing deep product knowledge, and resolving issues in partnership with internal teams.

Provide live, scheduled video support upon request, delivering high-touch service when it matters most.

Proactively identify and document product bugs with clear reproduction steps, offering customer success perspectives on case volumes and trends.

Gain a strong understanding of where Support can assist your named customers, developing a positive, consultative relationship to help them transform the way they work with Asana.

Collaborate closely with Customer Success Managers (CSMs) and Technical Account Managers (TAMs) to align on account strategy and ensure a seamless customer experience, raising issue areas or trends to your Manager.

Monitor case volumes and SLAs across varying complexity levels, ensuring timely and premium resolution.

Update and maintain Support's internal knowledge base with insights from customer engagements to ensure information is up-to-date.

Provide assistance to colleagues in Customer Support by responding to questions and requests about complex cases for other customers.

Meet team standards for key metrics such as response time to new cases, customer satisfaction score, and number of cases resolved.

Act as a liaison between the Product team and your customers, contributing to support documentation and product feedback sessions to help scale knowledge and inform product improvements.

Flag potential risks or upsell opportunities based on customer signals, usage patterns, or engagement behavior.

About you

Demonstrates curiosity about AI tools and emerging technologies, with a willingness to learn and leverage them to enhance productivity, collaboration, or decision-making.

5+ years in a technical support role (Product Support Analyst, Technical Support Engineer, Product Support Engineer, Implementation Consultant, or similar customer-facing technical troubleshooting role) in a SaaS or tech environment.

Technical proficiency troubleshooting common SaaS issues, including authentication (SSO/SAML/native), browser behavior (extensions, cache), API & integrations, and user access management.

Empathetic, curious, and committed to helping customers feel heard and supported.

Strong critical thinking and problem-solving skills with the ability to break down complex topics into clear, actionable steps.

Proactive and transparent written and verbal English communication skills, with the ability to convey complex technical concepts across all organizational levels from operations to executives.

Comfortable operating in ambiguous environments while maintaining a consultative approach with customers.

Commitment to continuous learning and adopting new technical and non-technical skills to deliver optimal solutions.

At Asana, we're committed to building teams that include a variety of backgrounds, perspectives, and skills, as this is critical to helping us achieve our mission. If you're interested in this role and don't meet every listed requirement, we still encourage you to apply.

What we'll offer

Our comprehensive compensation package plays a big part in how we recognize you for the impact you have on our path to achieving our mission. We believe that compensation should be reflective of the value you create relative to the market value of your role. To ensure pay is fair and not impacted by biases, we're committed to looking at market value which is why we check ourselves and conduct a yearly pay equity audit.

For this role, the estimated base salary range is between €57,000 - €75,000. The actual base salary will vary based on various factors, including market and individual qualifications objectively assessed during the interview process. The listed range above is a guideline, and the base salary range for this role may be modified.

In addition to base salary, your compensation package may include additional components such as equity, sales incentive pay (for most sales roles), and benefits. If you're interviewing for this role, speak with your recruiter to learn more about the total compensation and benefits for this role.

NeoDyne is a leading engineering company specialising in industrial automation, digital manufacturing, and electrical engineering solutions. From our offices in Ireland, the UK, Romania, and the US, we operate on a global scale, combining technical expertise with local delivery. We support customers across Europe, North America, and Asia, delivering tailored engineering services that drive long-term success.


Position summary

NeoDyne are recruiting a Graduate Automation Engineer to join our expanding System Integration team. Our graduate programme is all about learning new and developing your existing skills. Over a two-year period, you will be placed in projects where you get to do meaningful work and contribute to the business.

This Graduate opportunity is offered as a full-time permanent contract, based at our Galway Office, with an excellent salary and benefits package. What's on offer?

  • Income Protection

  • PRSA pension with employer contribution

Apply today!

So why wait? Apply Today!

*Main Purpose and Objectives of Position*

The Graduate Utilities Engineer is an entry-level engineering role, designed to build the knowledge, skills and confidence needed to support the reliable operation and qualified state of clean utility systems and supporting grey systems within Biotech manufacturing. Working closely with mentors and experienced engineers, the Graduate Utilities Engineer will progressively develop the technical and professional capability to help ensure processes are in-control and compliant, while contributing to process continuous improvement as part of a structured development programme.

● Develop a strong safety mindset by following safety rules and actively contributing to improving the safety culture.

● Build clean system engineering knowledge as a developing member of the area team, supported by experienced colleagues.

● Learn how clean system unit operations and equipment are maintained in a qualified and reliable state.

● Gain exposure to establishing and monitoring critical parameters for clean systems, to support processes remaining in control.

● Support troubleshooting of unit operations, equipment and operational issues, building problem-solving skills under guidance.

● Learn to evaluate activities for their impact on the qualified state of equipment, and to use the appropriate tools and processes.

● Actively participate in safety-related activities (audits, hazard reviews, pre-start-up safety reviews) to build safety awareness and drive ongoing improvement.

*Bio-process Technical Support*

● Develop into a competent point of contact for equipment and processes in an assigned area of responsibility, building a clear understanding of unit operations and associated equipment.

● Learn to monitor clean utility systems and support the optimisation of unit operations and equipment performance.

● Support troubleshooting efforts relating to unit operations, equipment and operational issues, working alongside experienced engineers.

● Identify and support improvement opportunities (procedural changes, upgrades, projects etc.) associated with unit operations/equipment within the area.

jobs.title: SHEQ Advisor
jobs.description:
Job Title: SHEQ Advisor

Reporting to: SHEQ Manager

Business Unit: Ireland

Role purpose

Within Omexom Ireland’s Business Unit (BU), there is a requirement for a SHEQ Advisor to oversee and enhance project delivery standards related to Safety, Health, Environment, and Quality (SHEQ). Reporting directly to the BU SHEQ Manager, the SHEQ Advisor will play a pivotal role in ensuring that all Omexom projects uphold the highest standards of safety and environmental stewardship. The role involves promoting and advising on all SHEQ matters, as well as driving continuous improvement in quality practices across project sites, supporting Omexom's commitment to operational excellence.

Responsibilities & Duties

Including but not limited to the following:

Safety Management and Compliance

• Develop, implement, and monitor safety policies, procedures, and practices in alignment with Omexom’s health and safety standards and Irish regulations.

• Conduct regular safety audits, risk assessments, and safety inspections at various project sites to ensure compliance and identify potential hazards.

Ensure compliance with Irish health and safety legislation, including statutory requirements, codes of practice, and relevant guidelines.

Incident Investigation and Reporting

• Lead investigations of incidents, near-misses, and accidents, identifying root causes and recommending corrective actions to prevent recurrence.

• Prepare and maintain accurate safety records, including incident reports, inspection findings, and corrective action tracking.

• Develop reports for senior management, highlighting safety performance metrics and recommending improvements.

Risk Assessment and Hazard Control

• Conduct risk assessments and provide recommendations for control measures to mitigate identified hazards.

• Advise project teams on appropriate safety measures, including personal protective equipment (PPE), safe work practices, and emergency procedures.

• Collaborate with engineers and project managers to implement risk mitigation strategies specific to energy and infrastructure projects.

Training and Development

• Deliver health and safety training to site personnel, including induction, toolbox talks, and refresher courses on safety protocols and procedures.

• Identify training needs and coordinate ongoing safety training and development programs to ensure a high level of safety awareness.

• Maintain records of all training provided and ensure site personnel are fully aware of their health and safety responsibilities.

Promoting Safety Culture

• Actively promote a culture of safety and continuous improvement across all levels of the organization.

• Serve as a visible safety leader on-site, fostering a proactive approach to health and safety.

• Engage with site teams to encourage safe behaviours, provide guidance, and promote health and well-being initiatives.

Emergency Preparedness

• Coordinate emergency response planning and drills to ensure preparedness in case of accidents, environmental incidents, or other emergencies.

• Assist in the development of emergency response procedures tailored to the specific needs of each project.

• Ensure all personnel are familiar with emergency response protocols and maintain emergency equipment.

• Co-ordinate the COSHH, Calibration & Inspection databases.

• Support the statutory inspections of equipment and tools for the BU.

• Assist in training relating to Omexom safety procedures and practices. Support the BU in ensuring any safety related required training is in place and is up to date.

• Develop and compile Construction Stage Safety Plans, Safety Files,

• Assist with the SHEQ support of project PQQ and tendering activities.

• Undertaken any additional duties which fall under the remit of a SHEQ Manager, where the business needs support.

Values

In line with Omexom’s values, the jobholder must have the following qualities:

Team Spirit & Generosity – able to work effectively within and contribute to the Omexom team to deliver results, provide support and drive performance.

Trust and Empowerment – enjoy managing their responsibilities and time to ensure work is completed efficiently and professionally.

Integrity and Responsibility – enjoy taking responsibility for their duties and managing these effectively to ensure efficient high quality results.

Innovation & Entrepreneurship – continually strive to improve processes and introduce new initiatives to improve efficiency.

jobs.description:
Company Description

Are you ready to be a trusted presence in a dynamic and vital environment? At Securitas, our mission goes beyond securing premises — we protect people, property, and peace of mind. As a Corporate Security Officer, you’ll be instrumental in maintaining a safe, professional, and welcoming atmosphere for clients, employees, and visitors.

This role offers the chance to work with a prestigious client.

Dublin 18

Fully Flexible, Monday to Sunday, minimum 36 hours per week

€17.76 per hour plus €20.00 night allowance and Sunday premium

Why Join Us?

Be part of a company that lives by its values: Integrity, Vigilance, and Helpfulness

Career development opportunities and industry-recognised training

A supportive team environment

Competitive salary and benefits package

Make a meaningful impact every day

Join Securitas and help us “See a Different World.” Apply now and become a key player in delivering safety and peace of mind.

Job Description

 As a Security Officer, you will be critical in ensuring the safety and security of the organisation's premises, assets, and personnel.

Your primary responsibility will be to respond swiftly and effectively to any security incidents or emergencies that may arise, including but not limited to breaches, alarms, disturbances, and medical emergencies.

You will be tasked with maintaining a vigilant presence, monitoring surveillance systems, and promptly intervening to mitigate risks and resolve situations as they occur.

Responsibilities:

Emergency Response: Respond promptly to security incidents, alarms, and emergencies, including but not limited to breaches, disturbances, medical situations, and fire alarms. Take decisive action to contain and resolve the problem while minimising risk to personnel and property.

Patrol and Inspection: Conduct regular patrols of assigned areas to deter criminal activity, enforce security policies, and ensure the integrity of physical barriers and access points. Perform thorough inspections to identify vulnerabilities and address potential security risks.
Access Control: Control access to restricted areas, ensuring that only authorised individuals are permitted entry. Verify identification credentials, issue access badges to new starters and temporary badges for existing employees, verify approvals, issue keys upon request, and enforce any other access protocols in accordance with company policies and procedures.
Reporting: Document all security incidents, observations, and actions in detailed and accurate reports. Provide timely and comprehensive written accounts to aid in investigations, compliance efforts, and risk assessment,
Collaboration: Coordinate effectively with other security personnel, law enforcement agencies, emergency responders, and relevant stakeholders to address safety & security concerns, share information, and implement coordinated responses to incidents
Training and Education: Stay informed about security best practices, emerging threats, and
relevant regulations. Participate in training programs to enhance your knowledge and skills in security procedures, crisis management, and emergency response techniques.
Parking management: Ensure compliance by overseeing all parking activities, issuing and checking parking permits, managing visitor parking, and guiding and instructing vendors to facilitate smooth traffic flow.
Admin tasks: Monitor security email box & respond to queries, manage lost property including safe storage and log keeping, provide occasional security support during company events, and provide escort upon request.
Other: Conduct thorough screening of incoming mail and packages using X-ray machines and other specialized equipment to ensure safety and security within the organization.
Your site Security Supervisor or equivalent may assign you additional tasks to ensure the smooth operation and security of the facility, which you will be expected to support with.

Qualifications:

Experience: Previous experience in security, law enforcement, or a related field is preferred.
Expertise in emergency response, crisis management, or security operations is highly desirable.
Physical Fitness: Must be physically fit and able to perform the essential duties of the job, including standing, walking, and responding swiftly to emergencies. CPR and first aid certification may be required.
Communication Skills: Excellent verbal and written communication skills are essential for effectively interacting with colleagues, stakeholders, and the public. The ability to remain calm and articulate during stressful situations is crucial.
Critical Thinking: Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to think quickly and analytically are
necessary to assess security threats, make sound judgments, and implement effective response strategies.
Team Player: Ability to work collaboratively as part of a team and independently with minimal supervision. Willingness to support colleagues and adapt to changing priorities in a dynamic security environment.
Integrity: Demonstrated honesty, integrity, and a commitment to upholding ethical standards in
all aspects of security operations. Must adhere to confidentiality requirements and maintain the trust and confidence of stakeholders.

jobs.description:
Indra is one of the leading global technology and consulting companies and the technological partner for the core business operations of its customers worldwide. It is a world leader in providing proprietary solutions in specific segments in Transport and Defence markets, and the leading firm in Digital Transformation Consultancy and Information Technologies in Spain and Latin America through its affiliate Minsait. Its business model is based on a comprehensive range of proprietary products, with a high-value focus and with a high innovation component. In the 2023 financial year, Indra achieved revenue of € 4.34 billion, employing over 58,000 people across 46+ countries, with business operations in over 140 countries.

At Indra, Innovation is in our DNA. We promote the digitalization of transport to achieve more sustainable, safe, reliable, resilient, and accessible mobility and infrastructure. We strive towards a reduction of accidents, to an improvement of safety, and the protection of travellers and infrastructure. We facilitate more efficient and less polluting transport management, optimizing the use of public resources, reducing the carbon footprint, promoting sustainable mobility policies and improving air quality.

Leadership - Generating real impact through tangible results

Flexibility - Enhancing proximity to the customer and differentiating Indra from its competitors

As part of a recently awarded ticketing project, Indra has a requirement for a Financial Accountant (Fixed Assets) to play a key role in the financial management of the NGT Fixed Assets and the establishment of robust financial governance and control and to provide strategic financial insights to senior management and project stakeholders.

Maintain and reconcile the fixed asset register.
Manage asset additions, disposals, transfers, depreciation, and impairments.
Ensure accurate capitalisation of project and technology expenditure.
Support month-end, year-end, and statutory reporting processes.
Monitor and report on capital expenditure against approved budgets.

Support internal and external audits, providing required documentation and analysis.

Requirements

The role requires the individual to have demonstratable experience across change control, incident management, exception management, and high-volume transactions management.

Essential requirements

A professional accountancy qualification and be admitted to membership of a recognised professional body of accountants
2+ years’ experience working in a finance role, (Finance Business, Finance Analyst, Financial Accountant) with demonstrable experience With Fixed Asset accounting
Well-developed communication skills, both written and verbal
Demonstrated commercial acumen, and knowledge of project financial management
Knowledge of data analytics and financial modelling
Strong Excel skills
Flexible and adaptable with experience working within a fast paced, dynamic work environment.

Desirable attributes

An understanding of public sector accounting, public transport ticketing technology or the ability to quickly acquire such understanding
Have demonstrable experience working in a high-volume transaction environment
Experience with Maximo or other asset management software,
Have experience in contract management.

Benefits

Comprehensive Employee Benefits Package

Annual Leave: 24 days per annum + Irish bank holidays (options to buy/sell days)
Pension – 7% employee and 7% employer
Private medical insurance (including dental & optical)
Flexible/hybrid working options
Charitable initiatives
Learning and development programs
Travel & expense allowances
Innovative & collaborative work environment

Must be eligible to work in Ireland; and must be willing to travel (5%), depending on busi

jobs.title: Physiotherapist - 12 month Fixed Term Contract
jobs.description:
Marymount University Hospital & Hospice provides specialist palliative care services and services to care for dependent older people. Its origins date back to 1870 with its foundation by the Religious Sisters of Charity in Cork. The original hospital was built on the north side of the city, but the service relocated in 2011 to purpose-built, modern, high-quality facilities in Curraheen, Cork.

An independent voluntary hospital, Marymount works closely with the statutory health services and is a section 38 organisation under the Health Act 2004 and a registered charity. It is governed by a voluntary Board of Directors and staffed by a CEO and a multi-disciplinary team who provide clinical and care services, education, and research.

Its services comprise a 44-bed in-patient specialist palliative care unit, a Day Care service (Day hospice), an out-patient department, community-based services, and bereavement & family support services. For older people, Marymount Hospital provides a 63-bed long-term care unit, and palliative care support services. Both services have a reputation for excellence in care.

Purpose of the Post

The provision of a quality Physiotherapy service in line with standards of Physiotherapy practice. To provide quality, client centered Physiotherapy assessment and treatment to identified client groups as directed by the Physiotherapy Manager.

Principal Duties and Responsibilities

The post holder is responsible for:

Carry a clinical caseload appropriate to the post
Be responsible for client assessment, development and implementation of individualised treatment plans that are client centered and in line with best practice.
Be responsible for goal setting in partnership with the client, family and other team members as appropriate.
Communicate and work in co-operation with other team members
Develop effective communication with and provide instruction, guidance and support to service users, family, carers etc.
Document client records in accordance with professional standards and departmental policies
Provide a service in varied locations in line with local policy / guidelines and within appropriate time allocation (e.g. clinic).
Participate in review meetings, case conferences, ward rounds etc. as appropriate
Maintain professional standards of practice
Maintain quality standards of work and co-operate with quality assurance programmes
Work within own scope of professional competence in line with principles of best practice, professional conduct and clinical governance.
Seek the advice of relevant personnel when appropriate / as required
Operate within the scope of practice of the Irish Society of Chartered Physiotherapists

Education & Training

Participate in mandatory training programmes
Take responsibility for, and keep up to date with Physiotherapy practice by participating in continuing professional development such as reflective practice, in service, self directed learning, research, clinical audit etc.
Engage in performance review processes including personal development planning
Participate in the practice education of student therapists. Take part in teaching / training / supervision of staff / others as appropriate (once sufficient clinical experience has been attained) and attend practice educator courses as relevant to role and needs.

Quality, Safety & Risk

Develop and monitor implementation of agreed policies, procedures and safe professional practice by adhering to relevant legislation, regulations and standards
Ensure the safety of self and others, and the maintenance of safe environments and equipment used in Physiotherapy in accordance with legislation
Assess and manage risk in their assigned area(s) of responsibility
Take the appropriate timely action to manage any incidents or near misses within their assigned area(s)
Be responsible for the safe and competent use of all equipment, aids and appliances both by clients and staff under their supervision
Be responsible for the safe and competent use of all equipment, aids and appliances both by clients and staff under their supervision
Comply with the Safety, Health and Welfare at Work Act, 2005
Comply with relevant Health and Safety responsibilities as outlined in Hospital Policies, Protocols and Procedures relevant to their area
Take reasonable care to protect her/his own safety, health and welfare and that of any other person who may be affected by her/his acts or omissions at work
Adhere to Departmental and Hospice policies at all times
Ensure confidentiality in all matters of information obtained during the course of employment
Report any malfunctions or defects in equipment or any such suspicions immediately to the Senior Physiotherapist / Physiotherapy Manager
Have a working knowledge of Marymount policies

Administrative

Actively participate in the improvement and development of Physiotherapy services by liaising with the Senior Physiotherapist / Physiotherapy Manager.
Gather and analyse statistics and participate in audits as directed by the Senior Physiotherapist / Physiotherapy Manager.
Represent the department at meetings and conferences as designated
Assist in ensuring that the Physiotherapy service makes the most efficient and effective use of developments in IT
Promote a culture that values diversity and respect in the workplace
Keep up to date with organisational developments within the Irish Health Service
Carry out other duties appropriate to the post as required from time to time by the Physiotherapy Manager

Teamwork

Communicate oral and written information in a clear, concise and well structured manner appropriate to the content and the target audience.
Manage communications in a professionalism manner.
Facilitate and maintain communication within own department, across multi-disciplinary and practice education teams
Promote and improve communication in their area of responsibility
Present lectures and research projects at local and national level

jobs.title: QA Compliance Specialist (Part Time)
jobs.description:
Company Description


About AbbVie

AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at www.abbvie.com. Follow @abbvie on LinkedIn, Facebook, Instagram, X and YouTube.


Job Description


The Quality Compliance Specialist is responsible for supporting and maintaining the site's Quality Management System (QMS) to ensure compliance with AbbVie standards, cGMP requirements, and applicable regulatory guidelines. The role plays a key part in ensuring that products manufactured at AbbVie consistently meet the expectations of patients, regulatory authorities, and the company.

Key Responsibilities

  • Coordinate and maintain the site Quality Management System, ensuring compliance with AbbVie policies and applicable regulatory requirements.
  • Lead and support Product Quality Review (PQR) activities.
  • Manage technical agreements, including initiation, review, approval, implementation, and document control.
  • Coordinate quality metrics, track-and-trend activities, and performance reporting to support Manufacturing and Quality Control operations.
  • Drive the application of Quality Risk Management (QRM) principles across site activities, including Risk Control Strategies (RCS) and FMEA processes.
  • Support investigations of customer complaints, deviations, and non-conformances, ensuring robust CAPA implementation and effectiveness verification.
  • Provide quality oversight and approval for validation activities, including systems, processes, and equipment.
  • Support New Product Introduction (NPI) projects and collaborate closely with Manufacturing, Technical Operations, and Laboratory functions.
  • Monitor quality system performance and present key metrics during management review and site performance meetings.
  • Coordinate change control activities and assess quality impact associated with proposed changes.
  • Provide guidance to site personnel on cGMP, quality system requirements, and regulatory expectations.
  • Act as a key liaison with corporate quality functions and regulatory agencies, including HPRA, FDA, and other regulatory authorities.
  • Perform regulatory assessments and policy reviews to ensure ongoing compliance.
  • Initiate and manage quality event records, investigations, and CAPA activities as required.
  • Support supplier quality activities, including vendor qualification, supplier performance monitoring, notifications, and audits.
  • Participate in and support internal audits, regulatory inspections, customer audits, and inspection readiness activities, including audit responses and evidence management.
  • Contribute to continuous improvement and compliance initiatives across the site.
  • Ensure adherence to all Environmental, Health & Safety (EHS) standards, procedures, and policies.

Qualifications


Required

  • Third-level qualification in Science, Quality, Engineering, or a related discipline.
  • Minimum of 2 years' experience in a Quality Assurance, Quality Compliance, or related GMP environment.
  • Strong knowledge of cGMP requirements and pharmaceutical regulatory expectations.
  • Experience working within a Quality Management System in a regulated manufacturing environment.

Preferred

  • Experience supporting regulatory inspections and audits.
  • Knowledge of quality risk management, change control, CAPA, supplier quality, and validation processes.
  • Experience within the pharmaceutical, biologics, or medical device industry.

Skills & Competencies

  • Strong attention to detail with a commitment to quality and compliance.
  • Excellent problem-solving and analytical skills.
  • Ability to assess and interpret regulatory requirements and implement effective solutions.
  • Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, both written and verbal.
  • Proven ability to work independently while collaborating effectively across cross-functional teams.
  • Results-driven mindset with a focus on continuous improvement and Right First Time principles.
  • High level of integrity, accountability, and professionalism.
  • Ability to influence stakeholders and drive compliance-focused outcomes.

Additional Information


Deadlines for applications is the 15th October 2026

PLEASE NOTE THIS POSITION IS TO START IN SEPTEMBER 2027

Our Critical Systems teams at Cundall play a key role in making buildings more energy efficient, cost effective to run and, ultimately, more sustainable. To do this, we’re looking for graduates who have a desire and enthusiasm to make a difference: in our homes, offices, projects, industry and community.

Working across a variety of sectors, our building services engineers are a source of world leading expertise, producing innovative and award-winning sustainable engineering solutions throughout the lifecycle of any building project.

With 29 locations globally, we offer a pro-active and collaborative approach to skill development, professional excellence and knowledge sharing.

Our Critical Systems teams have worked on a range of amazing projects, from data centres for large tech companies to headquarters of companies such as Deutsche Bank and Diageo. As a graduate in the team, you could play a key part in our next big project.
The Role You'll Play:
In this Graduate Electrical Critical Systems Engineer role, you’ll join a team who specialise in the design of some of the most exciting construction projects in Ireland and worldwide.

Working closely with colleagues across our multi-disciplinary practice, you’ll provide specialist consultancy input on projects across a wide range of sectors including education, healthcare, workplace, retail and critical systems (data centres).

Under the guidance of our team of experienced engineers, we’ll equip you to undertake detailed electrical building services engineering design and analysis, defining and translating clients’ needs into designs for buildings, facilities and services (electrical distribution and power generation, lighting design, security systems etc) - all with sustainability at the forefront of the design.

You’ll have the opportunity over time to assume greater levels of responsibility and autonomy as your professional skills develop and with accredited professional development programmes from CIBSE and IET, you’ll be fully supported towards achieving chartership.

  • On target to achieve at least a 2:2 degree.
  • Desirable if accredited with or on course to achieve a BEng/MEng degree level (or equivalent) in Electrical Engineering.
  • Have a keen interest in Electrical Engineering, particularly withing Building Design or Critical Systems
  • Possessing a desire for personal and professional development, you’ll have the proven ability to work effectively as part of a team, be organised and methodical when managing tasks, priorities and deadlines.
  • Digital engineering is a big focus at Cundall, so ideally, you’ll have an understanding of Parametric Modelling Techniques (Grasshopper or Dynamo), or at least one modern programming language (e.g. Python, C#, VB).
  • Collaborative in nature, you’ll be able to empathise with your clients’ needs and utilise excellent communication skills, both in writing and verbally, with internal and external stakeholders. You’re used to using your initiative to overcome challenges and have a positive, can-do attitude.

What’s in it for you?


We offer a competitive starting salary which grows as you develop, as well as many training and development opportunities to make sure you keep progressing.

Aside from this, those who successfully join our graduate scheme also enjoy:

  • A €2,000 bonus on gaining chartered status with a relevant professional body
  • 22 days' holiday per annum (plus statutory holidays)
  • A flexible benefits package which enables you to select additional benefits to suit your personal circumstances

jobs.description:
Closing Date: 14th October, 12pm (Ireland)

Apple is a place where extraordinary people gather to do their best work. Together we build products and experiences people once couldn’t have envisioned - and now can’t imagine living without. Are you excited by the idea of making a real impact? Are you prepared to dream big? Then a career with Apple might be your dream job.

Apple, Cork has a fantastic graduate opportunity to work within our AppleCare department, this position will give the you excellent development opportunities within a global company to build the career you always wanted! AppleCare, Cork is responsible for managing customer service and support for the entire EMEIA region.

The goal of the AppleCare organisation is to provide world-class technical support and service to the extensive installed base of Mac & iOS products and associated services. We are looking for astute, energetic graduates to work across a number of AppleCare Departments undertaking 5 rotations during a 23 month period.

The departments you will work in may include Product Repair and Service management, Customer support, Service Channel Management, Materials and Planning, Business Process Re-engineering, Data Analytics, Engineering & Quality.

This is an outstanding opportunity to gain valuable experience across a highly matrixed organisation. Graduates of Business Information Systems, Supply Chain, Engineering, Computer Science, Data Science/Analytics or any similar business disciplines are of particular interest. If you feel you have the critical skills required, we would love to hear from you.

Description
You will rotate through 5 AppleCare departments some of which are outlined below to assist in the ongoing management and development of the extensive AppleCare operations functions supporting our customer base.

Duties will include providing support functions to the various teams, developing and presenting business reports, investigating and solving technical and process problems, managing projects etc. There will likely be an opportunity to travel to various customer support and service partner operations within Europe at various points in the programme.

This role will involve extensive multi-functional teamwork and challenge your array of hard and soft skills daily. The AppleCare environment is a dynamic, fast-paced and complex operation, so the opportunity to learn and develop is immense.

Below is a brief description of each of the participating departments :

- Product Repair and Service Management - Responsible for managing the extensive range of service providers and repair factories across the EMEIA region. These providers generally are the partners to AppleCare who provide hardware repair services for our customers.

- Customer Support - A number of departments in AppleCare provide the management and support to ensure our customers get outstanding technical support for our products and services.

- Service Channel Management - This team provides extensive management and oversight to the different channels that our customers have for service, either directly with Apple or through our partner network.

- Service Supply Chain Operations (SSCO) - All of the parts and components required to keep the extensive service repairs network going are planned and procured by this department.

- Business Process Reengineering - This group provides the project and programme management services to develop our comprehensive systems and process network supporting the different AppleCare business groups.

- Data Analytics - Data analysis is a critical part of ensuring that our business functions are operating as effectively and efficiently as possible. This team develops the tools and perform the essential services to analyse big data for all business groups within AppleCare.

Preferred Qualifications
Highly motivated self-starter with consistent record of delivering results through team work.
Strong data analytics skills & a data driven approach
Good knowledge of any of SQL, Excel, Tableau or Power BI
Excellent time management and prioritisation skills
Outstanding interpersonal skills
Superb communication skills both verbal & written
Be able to function comfortably in a fast-paced, pressurised & highly information sensitive environment
Good problem-solving skills, being able to make informed & timely decisions.

Minimum Qualifications
Will have achieved or expected to achieve a 2:1 or higher overall grade in undergraduate degree programme or MSc.

jobs.title: Controls Engineer

Our colleagues across the globe love innovating with science and technology to enrich people’s lives with our solutions in Healthcare, Life Science, and Electronics. Together, we dream big and are passionate about caring for our rich mix of people, customers, patients, and planet. That`s why we are always looking for curious minds that see themselves imagining the unimaginable with us.

The Role

The Automation and Controls Specialist is responsible for designing, programming, and implementing control strategies to optimize manufacturing processes using advanced automation technologies. This role requires proficiency in configuring and troubleshooting systems such as PLCs, SCADA, DCS, and HMI.
While the role focuses on Smart Manufacturing and CapEx projects implementation, on a day-to-day it may also support diagnosis and resolution of issues related to control systems.

Duties

• Design, develop, install, modify and test the programming of PLC's, Robotics, vision systems as well as supporting the sites SCADA systems.
• Responsible for repairing, fault finding, and troubleshooting automation issues on production equipment as part of a team working in a live production environment.
• Collaborate with team members to implement effective repairs and improvements.
• Develop knowledge of on-site systems and equipment such as PLC's, Servo motors, vision systems and robotics to become the Site SME for these technologies. Lead or manage the development of GAMP documentation with the project team e.g. URS, FDS, FAT, SAT etc...
• Participate and in some cases lead projects, provide technical support and make informed decisions on hardware and architecture selection.
• Monitor and analyze opportunities for the development of new or improved tools for process improvement activities. Define the equipment and technologies to be used in the department based on experience in the area.
• Support the site during out of hours with automation issues as part of the Automation Oncall service as part of the Automation On-call team rota.
• Have a keen ability to fault find complex automation equipment including interrogation ofprogram code to identify issues.
• Coach area technicians and junior control engineers as required and support problemsolving and continuous improvement efforts across all areas of Biotools.
• Carry out justification for capital projects for the site and lead all elements of the projectwithin schedule and costs
• Manage all Requisitions and financial needs to ensure site discretionary budgets and capitalbudgets are met.
• Give input to the budgeting process for controls automation needs to allow the correctfinance to be put in place for execution.
• Ensure project design and installations meet the requirement of EU directives such as the Machinery Directive and CE compliance.
• Ensure Electrical Control Panels are built to standard and adhere to Safety of Machinery –EN60204-1.
• Develop critical spares list for site controls and automation hardware & ensure that criticalspares are in stock or are readily available at all times. Ensure that an effective program is then maintained.
• Investigate EHS incidents, lead RCAs and complete EHS actions as appropriate.
• Perform all tasks with due recognition of safety, environment, GMP & plant procedures.

Who You Are

• BEng degree in electrical/electronic/automation engineering or equivalent, with particularemphasis in the automation discipline.

• Minimum of 7 years + industry experience in an FDA or GMP environment as an automation controls engineer. Electrician experience and qualification is desirable.

• Experience with Robotic/pick &place Machines with high speed assembly operations required.
• Knowledge of interfacing with and controlling of servo drive and Motion Control systems.
• Knowledge of Vision Systems is preferable. [Cognex and other Vendors]
• Experienced with Rockwell, Siemens S7, Telemecanique and other types of PLC Controllers.
• In depth knowledge of automation network protocols including EtherNet IP, DeviceNet,ControlNet, Modbus and Profibus.
• Knowledge of control systems integration with plant MES (Manufacturing Execution System).
• Excellent problem solving and analytical ability and the ability to work as part of a team.
• Be familiar with planned preventative maintenance approaches.

jobs.description:
Position: Data Protection/Freedom of Information Officer

Contract: Permanent Part-time - Onsite

Hours: 21 hours per week

Salary range: HSE Consolidated pay-scale (Current Applicable Scale)

Reporting to: Chief Executive Officer

Closing date: 19 October 2026

Organisational Context

Clontarf Hospital is a 160-bed Voluntary Hospital providing rehabilitation Services under Section 38 of the Health Act 2004 for Adults and Older Persons. At Clontarf Hospital, our committed, expert and compassionate staff provide excellent care to patients on their rehabilitation journey. Our goal is to work in partnership with patients, providing care that is tailored to their unique needs, empowering them to achieve their optimum level of independence at home and in their communities. The patient pathways include:

Older Persons Rehabilitation
Step-up beds and hospital avoidance pathways with the Integrated Care Team for Older Persons (ICPOP Team)
Specialist Rehabilitation Services including neuro-rehabilitation and rehabilitation after trauma for adults and older persons
Orthopaedic Rehabilitation

The Hospital has close links with the Mater Hospital, Beaumont Hospital, The National Orthopaedic Hospital, HSE Services and our Community Partners.

Role Summary

The Data Protection / Freedom of Information Officer holds primary operational and statutory responsibility for overseeing Clontarf Hospitals adherence to data protection laws and the Freedom of Information (FOI) Act 2014. The post holder reports directly to the Chief Executive Officer, maintaining the professional independence required to act as the formal statutory Data Protection Officer (DPO) and formal Information Decision Maker.

Essential Criteria

Hold a 3rd Level qualification in a relevant field e.g., Data Protection, Information Compliance, Law, Records Management or a related discipline.
Have a minimum of 2 years experience in the area of Data Protection, Information Management and/or Records Management or similar role.
Experience managing GDPR and FOI processes.
Strong knowledge of Irish and EU Data Protection legislation.
Excellent organisational, analytical and decision-making skills.
High standard of integrity, professional judgement and communication skills.
Ability to work with multiple internal and external stakeholders.
Fluent command and understanding of the English language to include spoken and written word.

Duties and Responsibilities

Data Protection Advisory & Compliance

Act as the principal point of contact for the Data Protection Commission (DPC) on all data protection issues and monitor all ongoing responses to regulatory requests.
Serve as the formal point of contact for internal and external regulatory organisations, patients, and staff regarding the processing of personal data.
Act as the first point of contact for data subjects wishing to make a formal complaint in relation to their rights and freedoms.
Work with the hospitals ICT manager to develop ICT policies and procedures as they relate to GDPR, privacy laws, and data protection.
Assist and advise on corporate business decisions that carry data protection implications, ensuring that decisions are designed with data protection and privacy in mind.
Provide structured GDPR and Data Protection Act compliance planning and advisory support to Heads of Services/Departments in the hospital as necessary.
Assist and advise on the development, enhancement, and revision of Hospital policies, procedures, standards, guidelines, best practices, templates, and checklists. Ensure materials reflect changes in laws, regulatory mandates, or Hospital standards to drive operational consistency.
Prepare and communicate comprehensive reports regarding data protection compliance breaches and other relevant compliance updates to the CEO, the Executive Management Team, the Hospital Board and the Data Protection Commissioner.
Provide structured monthly updates directly to the CEO on all matters relating to data protection and GDPR compliance.
Ensure the timely adoption and execution of all GDPR and data privacy compliance requirements across all hospital departments.

Data Governance Operations & Registers

Centralise, maintain, and formally audit the organisational Record of Processing Activities (RoPA) under Article 30 of the GDPR.
Maintain a centralised register of signed Clontarf Hospital Data Sharing Agreements (DSAs)
Provide ongoing advice to Heads of Departments regarding GDPR compliance to ensure that formal agreements are actively in place for all existing and new contracts with third parties who process (view, access, store, or process) identifiable patient or employee data.
Actively review and assess any reported data protection incidents recorded on the Hospitals Data Breach Log. Direct notifications to the Data Protection Commission as appropriate, and provide technical advice alongside letter templates to departments for formal breach notifications to affected data subjects.
Act as an advocate for data protection and privacy within Clontarf Hospital. Promote compliance by designing, updating, and delivering GDPR awareness and education training courses to hospital staff regarding the foundational importance of data protection in a rehabilitation hospital environment.

Data Protection Impact Assessments (DPIAs)

Undertake and systematically review completed Data Protection Impact Assessments (DPIAs) submitted by internal departments and external stakeholders.
Audit all newly proposed data processing activities, including new ICT systems, new mobile applications, research ethics applications, and new Electronic Referral Systems etc.
Recommend clear mitigating steps to reduce data risks if they are not initially identified by stakeholders. Risks must be deemed entirely acceptable under statutory frameworks for the post holder to formally sign off on the activity from a GDPR perspective.

Freedom of Information (FOI) Decision Maker

Responsibility for the end-to-end management
