jobs.description:
Getty Images is looking for a NOC Operator who enjoys working with a diverse set of technologies and takes pride in their attention to detail. Someone who is looking to develop new skills and strengthen existing ones as they prepare for the next steps in their career.
The mission of the NOC at Getty Images is to provide 24x7 support of our production systems, minimizing customer impact by identifying, resolving, and (when vital) escalating issues as quickly as possible. This support is not limited to technical restoration; we also advise, coordinate resources, and provide leadership via strict adherence to our Incident Management process.
When not actively responding to alerts or running incidents, you are encouraged to spend your time working on projects that improve your team's responsiveness and sharpen your technical skills.

Your next challenge:

You will join a team of highly collaborative and curious NOC operators who are as comfortable working with a wide range of tools as they are willing to take the initiative on an incident bridge. As a team member you respond quickly to new alerts; triaging, resolving, or escalating as needed. From within the NOC you will have the opportunity to interact with and build relationships with the entirety of Getty Images; examples include:
  • Working with the Sales Ops team to dig into a website issue
  • Advising the App Dev team while performing a code rollback
  • Advising the DBAs that you identified and resolved SQL blocking on a critical system
  • Reporting to Security that you disabled an account after investigating suspicious activity
  • Coordinating with Facilities, Network, Storage, and local Service Desk teams to shut down and power up remote office equipment during planned or unexpected power outages
  • Assisting with core system patching
Some of the ways that you will contribute to Getty's success are by shortening the duration of customer-impacting incidents or, better yet, preventing impact entirely by resolving issues. You will also play a pivotal role in incident triage, helping our engineers focus on project work during the day and getting uninterrupted sleep at night by only escalating issues that need immediate attention. You have taken the time to thoroughly learn how our systems are interconnected; allowing you to quickly craft a notification that details the incident's full scope and impact.

About the team The Platform Responsibility team is responsible for building, optimizing, and maintaining machine learning models and operational processes that support TikTok's Trust & Safety systems. We ensure that automated safety models perform effectively in identifying harmful content, mitigating risks, and maintaining a safe user environment across regions. The Platform Responsibility team is bringing disruptive innovation to content safety through the deep application of AI. We are building next-generation infrastructure that leverages advanced LLMs to reshape risk detection and governance. By engineering high-quality data pipelines and integrating AI into core decision-making, we drive exponential efficiency gains and precision. Working at the intersection of scalable engineering and technology, we empower global business growth while serving as the foundation of user trust. We are looking for talented individuals to join us for an internship. Our internship program offers students hands-on experience, industry exposure, and opportunities to apply their knowledge to real-world challenges while building a strong foundation for personal and professional growth. Interns will gain practical experience, explore potential career paths, and participate in social events, learning programs, and development workshops alongside industry professionals. Candidates may apply to a maximum of two positions across Our Company and its affiliates globally. Applications will be considered in the order they are submitted. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, so we encourage you to apply early. Please clearly state your availability in your resume, including your start and end dates. Responsibilities - For large-model training and evaluation scenarios, participate in formulating and continuously iterating data quality standards, judgement rules, and acceptance criteria; - Review and assess data outputs against quality standards, identify issues and close the loop on corrections to ensure accuracy and consistency; - Participate deeply in the assessment and discussion of complex, ambiguous, and edge cases, turning findings into reusable judgement rules and knowledge assets; - Track quality performance, identify root causes, and drive improvements in production processes and execution; - Collaborate with production, product, algorithm, strategy, and other teams to align quality standards and connect the “standards—production—acceptance—feedback” loop. - Be patient with foundational and repetitive work, and adept at identifying problems;

Qualifications

Preferred Qualification(s) - Internship or project experience in data quality, content moderation, compliance, content operations, AI data/annotation, or related areas. - Extensive experience using mainstream large-model products such as ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and Doubao.

About TikTok

TikTok is the leading destination for short-form mobile video. At TikTok, our mission is to inspire creativity and bring joy. TikTok's global headquarters are in Los Angeles and Singapore, and we also have offices in New York City, London, Dublin, Paris, Berlin, Dubai, Jakarta, Seoul, and Tokyo. ​

When we create and grow together, the possibilities are limitless. Join us. ​

Great training

jobs.title: Dedicated Emergency Responder Team
jobs.description:
Job Details:

Job Description:

The Role and Impact
As a Manufacturing Safety Technician, you will play a critical role in ensuring the safety and readiness of Intel's factory operations. You will be responsible for responding promptly to safety incidents and emergencies, conducting thorough investigations, and providing technical guidance on emergency response protocols. Your work will directly contribute to a safer, more efficient manufacturing environment, ensuring compliance with safety standards and fostering continuous improvement across the site.

Business group
Intel Foundry is at the forefront of innovation, enabling cutting-edge manufacturing and advancing Intel's mission to create world-changing technology. The team is dedicated to supporting factory operations by embedding safety and emergency response expertise across the site. Joining this group provides an opportunity to work in a collaborative environment committed to operational excellence and employee well-being.

Key Responsibilities
- Respond promptly to safety incidents, accidents, and alarms, including hazardous material leaks, odors, spills, and medical concerns.
- Investigate incidents to determine root causes and recommend corrective actions to prevent recurrence.
- Document all safety reports, incidents, and activities occurring during shifts, maintaining accurate and detailed records.
- Conduct regular site walkthroughs to identify potential hazards and ensure a physical presence across the factory.
- Collaborate with project teams to ensure safety compliance during equipment installations, startups, and retirements.
- Provide technical expertise on emergency response protocols and actively participate in planning safety initiatives.
- Lead, mentor, and coach shift safety and emergency response teams, ensuring alignment with safety goals and readiness for emergencies.
- Develop and deliver safety training sessions, drills, and scenario updates to team members as needed.
- Perform preventative maintenance and upgrades on safety equipment, supplies, and emergency resources to ensure optimal functionality.
- Monitor and maintain inventory levels of safety equipment and emergency supplies, ensuring their availability when needed.
- Partner with other departments to implement safety initiatives and drive continuous improvement measures.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications
- Bachelor's degree in a relevant field with 2+ years of hands-on experience in safety, emergency response, or a related domain OR an Associate degree in a relevant field with 3-6 years of applicable experience.
- Proficiency in incident investigation procedures, root cause analysis, and safety documentation.
- Familiarity with safety standards, regulations, and protocols, including Hazardous Production Materials.
- Experience conducting safety audits, inspections, or walkthroughs in manufacturing environments.
- Technical aptitude for maintaining and performing preventative maintenance on safety equipment and supplies.

Preferred Qualifications
- Strong communication skills with the ability to lead and mentor teams effectively.
- Experience delivering safety training sessions, drills, or scenario updates.
- Demonstrated ability to collaborate across departments and drive safety initiatives.
- Familiarity with continuous improvement processes and safety-related project planning.
- Passion for fostering a safe workplace and contributing to team development.

Take the next step in your career by joining Intel Foundry's dedicated safety team. Be part of an environment where your expertise will make a tangible impact on factory operations and employee well-being.

jobs.title: Maintenance Technician- Mechanical & Electrical
jobs.description:
Sheraton Athlone Hotel is seeking an experienced Maintenance Technician to carry out planned and reactive maintenance across the property.

Reporting to the Facilities Manager, you will play a key role in maintaining a safe, efficient and welcoming environment for our guests, associates and visitors. As part of the globally recognised Marriott International family, you will have the opportunity to develop your career within one of the world's leading hospitality brands while contributing to the smooth day-to-day operation of a busy four-star hotel.

Key Responsibilities

Complete planned preventative maintenance (PPM), reactive and emergency maintenance throughout the hotel, including guest bedrooms, public areas, meeting and event spaces, plant rooms and external grounds.
Carry out routine inspections, plant checks and meter readings, identifying potential issues before equipment failure occurs.
Diagnose faults and undertake first-line mechanical and electrical repairs.
Maintain and troubleshoot pumps, motors, boilers, heating and hot water systems, HVAC equipment, BMS controls, lighting, plumbing systems and hotel operational equipment.
Respond promptly and professionally to maintenance requests and breakdowns, prioritising issues effectively in a busy hotel environment.
Support energy-efficiency and sustainability initiatives across the property.
Maintain accurate maintenance records, work orders, PPM documentation and compliance logs.
Liaise with specialist contractors and suppliers as required.
Ensure appropriate stock levels of tools, consumables, spare parts and maintenance materials are maintained.
Carry out all work in compliance with health and safety requirements and support the wider facilities team with additional operational projects as required.
Participate in an on-call or out-of-hours rota when necessary.

The Ideal Candidate

Previous experience in a hands-on maintenance, facilities, engineering or technical role, ideally within hospitality, leisure or a similar commercial environment.
A relevant qualification in a mechanical or electrical trade is essential.
Strong practical knowledge of mechanical and/or electrical systems, including HVAC, heating systems, pumps, motors, plumbing and building services equipment.
Excellent fault-finding, preventative maintenance and problem-solving skills.
Ability to read technical manuals, equipment documentation and basic mechanical or electrical schematics.
Strong awareness of safe working practices and compliance requirements.
Good communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work independently and collaboratively with colleagues and contractors.
Flexible, practical and solutions-focused approach to work.
Full clean driving licence desirable.

What We Offer

Competitive salary and benefits package.
Complimentary use of the hotel leisure facilities.
Meals provided while on duty.
Free on-site parking.
Marriott Explore Associate Rate and Friends & Family discounts worldwide.
Learning and development opportunities through Marriott International and Hodson Bay Group.
Employee recognition and reward programmes.
Health and wellbeing initiatives.
Active Sports & Social Club.
Opportunities for career progression within Sheraton Athlone Hotel, Hodson Bay Group and Marriott International.

As part of the Hodson Bay Group-proudly holding Gold certification in Failte Ireland's Employer Excellence Programme, Silver accreditation from Investors in Diversity, and recently recognised as one of Ireland's Happiest Workplaces for 2025 in association with The Sunday Times-the Sheraton Athlone Hotel is committed to fostering a culture of growth, opportunity, and continuous development for driven and ambitious team members.

We prioritise fostering a people-centric culture where mutual respect and trust create a thriving work atmosphere.

jobs.description:
*Post* 	Migrant Mentor

*Location* 	Letterkenny & Buncrana

*Reporting to*	\*\*Programme Manager

*Salary*	TBC

*Working hours* 	35 hours

*6 months fixed term contract*

*Application Closing Date *	12 noon 20th November 2026

*Are you passionate about supporting migrants to overcome challenges and access new opportunities? Do you enjoy working with people from diverse cultural backgrounds, building meaningful relationships, and helping individuals take positive steps towards employment? If so, a Migrant Mentor role with People 1st could be your perfect next step.*

As a Migrant Mentor working on the Fáilte Project, you'll play a key role in supporting economically inactive migrants across Donegal to address the barriers that may be preventing them from entering the labour market. Through a flexible, person-centred approach, you'll provide tailored mentoring, employability guidance, and practical support to help participants develop the skills, knowledge, and confidence needed to progress towards employment.

You'll work closely with participants to understand their individual circumstances, identify their strengths, and develop personalised progression plans that reflect their goals and aspirations. You'll also collaborate with employers, training providers, community organisations, and statutory services to connect participants with suitable employment, education, training, and community opportunities, helping them achieve positive and sustainable outcomes.

*PERSONAL SPECIFICATION*

*Essential Criteria*

* Fluent in English, with excellent verbal and written communication skills.
* Educated to Leaving Certificate standard or equivalent as a minimum. A third-level qualification in in Social Care, Community Development, Education, Employment Support, or a related field is desirable but not essential.
* Minimum of one year’s experience in mentoring, employability, recruitment, training, customer service, advice and guidance, or another relevant people-facing role.
* Good understanding of the challenges facing migrants living in Ireland, including language barriers, cultural differences, social integration, and accessing employment, education, and support services.
* Experience working in a target-driven environment, with the ability to manage caseloads and achieve individual and team performance targets (KPIs).
* Strong interpersonal and relationship-building skills, with the ability to engage effectively with individuals from diverse cultural backgrounds and communicate sensitively and respectfully.
* Competent IT user with experience using Microsoft Office applications, databases, and CRM/case management systems.
* Ability to work independently as well as collaboratively within a team environment, with an understanding of confidentiality, safeguarding, equality, diversity, and professional boundaries.
* Hold a current clean driving licence and have access to a car.

*Desirable Criteria*

* Fluency in additional languages, particularly those commonly spoken within migrant communities in Donegal.
* Knowledge of local employment opportunities, education and training provision, community organisations, and migrant support services across Donegal.
* Experience delivering one-to-one mentoring, coaching, employability guidance, or group-based workshops.
* Experience supporting migrants, refugees, or individuals facing barriers to employment, including language difficulties, social isolation, low confidence, or unfamiliarity with the Irish labour market.
* Experience supporting cultural awareness activities, conversational English sessions, or community integration initiatives.
* Willingness to travel to different locations across Donegal and surrounding areas as required.

*PROFESSIONAL BEHAVIOURS AND CORE CAPABILITIES*

*Key Duties and Responsibilities*

As an Migrant Mentor, your responsibilities will include:

* Manage a caseload of participants on the Fáilte Project, providing personalised mentoring and practical support to help individuals progress towards employment, education, training, and greater independence.
* Support participant recruitment, induction, and initial assessments, identifying individual needs, strengths, aspirations, and potential barriers to employment.
* Develop and regularly review Personalised Progression Plans, agreeing achievable goals and actions that support positive participant outcomes.
* Deliver one-to-one mentoring and group-based employability interventions, including job-search support, CV preparation, interview skills, confidence-building, cultural awareness, and conversational English activities.
* Support participants to understand and navigate the Irish labour market, including recruitment processes, workplace expectations, employment opportunities, and access to relevant services.
* Identify barriers to progression, including language difficulties, cultural differences, social isolation, and additional or complex support needs, providing appropriate guidance and referrals to specialist services where required.
* Build and maintain effective relationships with employers, training providers, statutory bodies, community groups, voluntary organisations, and other relevant stakeholders, attending meetings where necessary to identify employment vacancies, work placements, and volunteering opportunities.
* Support participants to access suitable employment, education, training, work placements, and volunteering opportunities that align with their individual goals.
* Liaise with employers and participants to identify and provide appropriate in-work support, helping individuals settle into employment and achieve sustainable outcomes.
* Coordinate access to relevant training, resources, and support services to enable participants to develop their skills, confidence, and employability.
* Maintain regular participant engagement, monitor progress, and contribute towards achieving agreed individual and team performance targets, KPIs, and programme outcomes.

We currently have an exciting opportunity for a Supervising Pharmacist to join the team in our McCauleys Fairgreen Pharmacy, in Carlow.

This is a 45 hour permanent position.

The team currently comprises a Store Manager, an Assistant Store Manager, 2 Support Pharmacists, and 6 Pharmacy Technicians.

This store has manageable items and services.

What we offer:

Reimbursement PSI fees annually
Funding of vaccination training.
A Pension Scheme with a company contribution of up to 7% of the annual salary
CPD hours allowance annually
Premium Rate on Sunday Shifts (1.5 x Normal Rate)

Employee Assistance Programme with Spectrum Life Wellbeing Platform

Qualifications, Experience & Skills Required

Excellent attention to detail
Strong communication, Interpersonal and leadership skills
Highly organized with a proven ability to work on multiple tasks accurately in a busy environment

Since Uniphar became a publicly listed company in 2019, the Group has grown organically and through a series of strategic acquisitions, which continue to strengthen Uniphar’s international reach. Uniphar Pharma

Pharma is a global division operating across US, Europe, APAC and MENA, bringing a range of pharma services to manufacturers across the product life cycle. We leverage this platform to provide unlicensed medicines, or medicines that are otherwise difficult to source. In addition, we commercialise launch and established brands to HCPs on behalf of pharmaceutical clients across the globe. The core to this division is providing equitable access to medicines globally.

Culture at Uniphar

From our leadership team and across all of our divisions, Uniphar lives and breathes four key culture pillars:

We have a People First approach, we do the right thing and take a stand for our people
We foster a strong Entrepreneurial Spirit where Adaptability, Commitment & Resilience is embodied in our way of working

Analyst, Investment Operations | iRisk Data Integrity | PGIM Global Services

(Letterkenny, Ireland / Hybrid 2 days onsite a week)

A GLOBAL FIRM WITH A DIVERSE & INCLUSIVE CULTURE

As the Global Asset Management business of Prudential, we’re always looking for ways to improve financial services. We’re passionate about making a meaningful impact, touching the lives of millions and solving financial challenges in an ever-changing world.

We also believe talent is key to achieving our vision and are intentional about building a culture built upon respect and collaboration. When you join PGIM, you’ll unlock a motivating and impactful career – all while growing your skills and advancing your profession at one of the world’s leading global asset managers!

If you’re not afraid to think differently and challenge the status quo, come and be a part of a dedicated team that’s investing in your future by shaping tomorrow today.

At PGIM, You Can!

What you will do:

In this staff-level role, you’ll have the opportunity to build experience in investment operations, data quality and financial reporting while supporting PGIM’s iRisk Data Integrity Group. You’ll work with financial data from Prudential’s accounting and trading systems to help ensure that information used across investment and risk reporting is accurate, complete and reliable.

You’ll partner with experienced team members across the firm including PGIM Global Services, Finance and the Chief Investment Office to learn how investment data supports decision-making across a global investment management business.

Reliable data is essential to how PGIM manages investments, monitors risk and supports business decisions. In this role, your work will help strengthen data quality controls and ensure teams have the information they need to operate with confidence.

Responsibilities include:

Monitor a variety of financial and accounting data (such as prices, ratings, analytics, yields, positions) via daily data integrity controls across the iRisk platform and related investment systems
Help identify and research production issues by reviewing data, analyzing trends, and partnering with the right teams to resolve them
Build experience working with financial instruments, investment data, and reporting tools used across PGIM and Prudential
Assist with reporting requests and ad hoc inquiries using tools such as iRisk, Excel, Tableau, Cognos and related systems
Partner with team members to streamline existing processes, test new enhancements and support project work
Contribute to the quality and accuracy of data used to support investment risk, reporting and business decision-making

You’ll work in a collaborative, hands-on environment where you’ll learn from experienced colleagues and partner with teams across PGIM Global Services, Finance and the Chief Investment Office. This role offers exposure to investment operations, data integrity, reporting, and process improvement, giving you a strong foundation to grow your career in financial services.

What You Bring:

Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Business, Economics, Accounting, Information Systems or a related field
Interest in investment operations, financial data, risk reporting or asset management
Strong analytical, problem-solving and organizational skills
Comfort working with data and tools such as Microsoft Excel
Ability to manage priorities, meet deadlines and communicate clearly with team members and stakeholders

What Will Set You Apart:

Exposure to investment security types, financial reporting or investment operations through coursework, internships or early career experience
Experience with tools such as Aladdin, Cognos, Tableau, PAM for Investments or similar reporting systems
Curiosity about how financial data flows across investment, accounting and risk platforms

*PGIM welcomes all applicants, even if you don't meet every requirement. If your skills align with the role, we encourage you to apply.

What we offer you:

jobs.title: FP&A Specialist
jobs.description:
FP&A Specialist/Group FP&A Lead: Build Our Forecasting Function from Scratch

Remote (Ireland or UK) | Reporting to the Group CFO | Yomali

Why This Role Exists

Yomali has never had a formal forecasting capability, and that's about to change.

We're a privately-held group of e-commerce businesses (HelpGrid, BuyGoods, MaxWeb and more). Today our leaders don't have a consistent way to forecast revenue and costs, understand variance, or be held accountable to their numbers. We're building that capability from the ground up. The forecasting model will be built in Excel and loaded into Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central for reporting against actuals. We need someone who has built models like this before to lead the build.

This isn't a role where you inherit a working model and keep the lights on. You're building the model.

What You'll Own

Design, build and maintain our driver-based Excel forecasting and budgeting model, starting with HelpGrid, BuyGoods and MaxWeb

Load the outputs into Business Central and report forecast versus actual

Own the accountability loop, making sure business leaders understand, use and stand behind their forecasts

Build visibility of the cost base down to supplier level, working with our Financial Controllers

Run what-if and scenario analysis for leadership

Evolve the model as we grow, so it scales and can move into a dedicated planning platform when the time is right

You'll work directly with our Group CFO, Financial Controllers and business unit leaders, with real autonomy and real visibility into how the business runs.

What Success Looks Like

First 3–6 months: The foundations of the Excel forecasting model are in place. The revenue and cost drivers for HelpGrid, BuyGoods and MaxWeb are built and tested, and the outputs are loading into Business Central.

12 months: A full 12-month budget is built and loaded. There's a regular rhythm of forecast-versus-actual conversations between Finance and business leaders, who use Finance's numbers in their own performance reviews. Supplier-level spend reporting is live.

What We're Looking For

Substantial hands-on FP&A experience , including having personally built a driver-based forecasting or budgeting model in Excel from scratch, not just maintained or administered one that already existed

Advanced Excel financial modelling: scenario analysis, clear model structure and integrity checks. You should also be comfortable reviewing and improving a model someone else built

Comfortable owning forecast-vs-actual conversations directly with business stakeholders, including pushing back when the numbers don't add up

Able to explain the numbers clearly to non-finance leaders

Genuinely energised by complex "what-if" modelling, not just running the base forecast but exploring what a new market or acquisition could look like

Able to work autonomously, without a team beneath you or an established playbook to follow

Experience loading budget or forecast data into an ERP and reporting against actuals is helpful. Business Central or NAV is a plus, but any ERP (Oracle, SAP, Sage, Workday, NetSuite or similar) is fine

Experience with a dedicated planning platform (Anaplan, Vena, Planful, Adaptive, Datarails, Pigment or similar) is a bonus, not a requirement

Professional finance qualification (CIMA/CGMA, ACCA, ACA or equivalent) preferred, not required

Who Thrives Here

You'll do well here if you're the kind of person who gets excited by ambiguity rather than overwhelmed by it. There's no existing FP&A team to lean on. You'll be it, with our CFO backing you up. You'll need to be strategic about sequencing (one business at a time, not all three at once) and comfortable holding your ground with senior stakeholders who are new to forecasting.

This role won't suit someone who needs an established process, a team of analysts to delegate to, or quick, fully-validated wins in the first few months. It will suit someone who wants to point at a forecasting capability in a year's time and say "I built that."

Why People Stay / Love Working Here

Our finance team spans Malta, Switzerland, the Philippines and the UK & Ireland, around 11 people in Finance and roughly 600 across the wider Group. The culture is genuinely open: people want to evolve how things are done, there's no bureaucracy slowing you down, and our CFO leads by trusting people to own their remit rather than micromanaging it.

What's In It For You

Genuine ownership: you're not maintaining someone else's model, you're building the Group's forecasting capability from day one

Direct access and visibility: you'll work closely with the Group CFO and business unit leaders, not buried in a large finance function

Fully remote, 9am–5pm UK/Ireland time

Competitive salary: Ireland: €68,000–€92,000 base | UK: £62,000–£82,000 base

A rare chance to shape how an entire Group forecasts and makes decisions. This isn't a role you'll find advertised often

Interview Process

Initial conversation with Talent

Interview with Group CFO, e.g. a forecasting scenario or model walk-through

Final stakeholder conversation with CEO and Group CFO

We move quickly and keep candidates informed at every stage.

About Yomali

Yomali is a privately-held group of e-commerce businesses, including HelpGrid, BuyGoods and MaxWeb, operating fully remotely across the globe. We're a lean, close-knit organisation where finance, operations and leadership work closely together — and where the person who builds something owns it.

Permanent capital model — no outside investor pressure for a quick exit, which lets the business plan long-term and protect culture rather than chase short-term numbers

600+ team members across 42 countries, driving $1B+ in online sales volume

10+ autonomous businesses, each with its own CEO, management team and brand — decentralized, not a single monolithic company

Founded 2019 with a "Build, Buy, Grow" philosophy, hands-on operator experience rather than pure capital

On Site

About us

The Fidelis Partnership is a leading privately-owned, Bermuda-based Managing General Underwriter, which, through its subsidiaries, is a global underwriter of property, bespoke and specialty insurance and reinsurance products. The Fidelis Partnership is one of the largest Managing General Underwriters globally and its operations also include outwards reinsurance, claims handling, exposure management and portfolio analytics. The Fidelis Partnership also sponsors and incubates specialist MGAs through its Pine Walk platform. The Fidelis Partnership is separately owned and managed from the ownership and management of Fidelis Insurance Group.

Across product lines and geographies, we focus on three diversified pillars: reinsurance, specialty and bespoke solutions. We are truly diversified. Our long-standing partnerships with capital providers and quota share partners make us nimble. Our breadth of expertise and capabilities deliver outstanding market returns.

The role

We are looking for an experienced Third-Party Risk Management Specialist to support the end-to-end assessment and oversight of third-party suppliers within a regulated environment.

You will be responsible for understanding supplier services and dependencies, assessing the quality of supporting evidence, coordinating specialist reviews, and maintaining clear and defensible records of risks, decisions, conditions and actions.

This role would suit an evidence-led risk professional who combines strong analytical judgement with disciplined case management and has experience working within third-party risk, operational risk, supplier risk, compliance or a related area.

Key accountabilities
Deliver proportionate, evidence-based third-party risk assessments from initial intake through approval, ongoing monitoring, reassessment and exit.
Understand supplier services, ownership structures, delivery models, legal entities, locations, data use, technology dependencies and potential business impact.
Coordinate corporate due diligence and supplier screening, including company registration, ownership and control information and supporting evidence.
Assess inherent risk and service criticality based on the nature of each arrangement, documenting the rationale and triggering reassessment following material changes.
Review questionnaires, policies, certifications and other supporting evidence for completeness, consistency and relevance.
Identify unsupported claims, inconsistencies, control gaps, remediation requirements and overdue actions.
Coordinate input from Information Security, Privacy, Compliance, Legal, Risk, Finance, Resilience and Technology specialists.
Track findings, remediation activity, approval conditions, exceptions, risk acceptance and outstanding actions through to completion.

Produce concise risk summaries and management information using Excel, TPRM/GRC platforms and other reporting tools.
Support the continued development and improvement of third-party onboarding and due diligence processes.
Maintain clear and auditable records of classifications, findings, decisions, conditions, owners and key dates.
Third-Party Risk Assessment: Ability to understand a service, identify key dependencies and apply proportionate due diligence throughout the third-party lifecycle.
Evidence Evaluation: Strong ability to assess questionnaires, policies, SOC reports, ISO certifications, resilience testing and remediation evidence, identifying gaps or inconsistencies.
Risk & Control Judgement: Good understanding of inherent risk, controls, residual risk, remediation, risk acceptance and escalation.
Regulatory & Resilience Awareness: Understanding of third-party risk, outsourcing, ICT risk and operational resilience requirements within regulated environments, including exposure to DORA, FCA/PRA outsourcing requirements, EBA guidance or comparable frameworks.
Technology & Data Literacy: Comfortable discussing SaaS, cloud, managed services, system access, data processing and cyber dependencies with relevant specialists.
Corporate Due Diligence: Ability to interpret company identity, registration, ownership and control information, supplier screening and related evidence.
Case Management & Auditability: Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage multiple assessments, actions, owners, deadlines and supporting evidence.
Analysis & Communication: Ability to turn complex information into clear findings, risk summaries, management information and reporting.

Previous experience within third-party risk management, vendor risk, operational risk, supplier due diligence, compliance, information security, resilience or a related discipline.
Experience completing supplier onboarding, inherent risk assessments, due diligence, ongoing monitoring or reassessments.
Experience within insurance, reinsurance, banking, payments or another regulated sector would be beneficial.
Practical exposure to DORA, ICT third-party risk, outsourcing or operational resilience would be advantageous.
Experience assessing cloud, SaaS, managed services, data, AI or other technology suppliers.
Experience using TPRM/GRC platforms such as ServiceNow, Archer, OneTrust, Coupa Risk Assess, ProcessUnity or similar systems would be beneficial.
Strong Excel skills, with Power BI or comparable reporting experience advantageous.
Relevant qualifications in operational risk, compliance, information security, resilience, procurement or financial services would be beneficial.
Experience of process improvement, particularly across supplier onboarding and due diligence processes, would be valued.

Job Summary:

In view of the continued growth of Bon Secours Hospital Dublin (BSHD) and the recent merger with Bon Secours Mercy Health, BSHD is now recruiting a permanent experienced and professional Sonographer/Radiographer to provide high-quality, patient-focused services. You will be required to perform a range of ultrasound examinations ensuring high-quality imaging and a comfortable, professional experience for every patient (exams include Abdominal, Gynae, Thyroid, Testes, Musculoskeletal and some Vascular scans to include both upper and lower limb DVTs).

The Dublin Diagnostic Imaging department is a busy multidisciplinary department incorporating US, MRI, CT, Cardiac Catheterization Laboratories, Interventional Radiology, DEXA and General Radiography. This is an opportunity for you to join a well-motivated and enthusiastic team providing a high quality of patient care and play a crucial part in delivering access to care and patient experience that are consistent with the Bon Secours Mission, Vision and Values.

This role applies value-based pricing, market insight, data, and Microchip tools to improve quote quality, conversion, profitability, decision speed, and ease of doing business. The team member will influence important commercial decisions, resolve complex opportunities, lead cross-functional improvements, strengthen pricing governance, and own key annual operating plan initiatives through measurable completion.

CMT offers broad commercial exposure and the opportunity to work with global leaders, influence high-value decisions, solve complex business challenges, and drive initiatives with visible impact. The team is modernizing how Microchip approaches pricing, quoting, analytics, systems, and commercial execution, and is seeking high-caliber talent ready to help lead that transformation.

Key Responsibilities

• Quote to Win: Recommend competitive, value-based pricing that balances profitable growth, customer value, commercial judgment, and speed.

• Pricing and Market Analysis: Use customer, product, cost, quote, backlog, market, and competitive data to improve decisions, quote quality, and organizational responsiveness.

• Cross-Functional Partnership: Collaborate globally across Sales, Business Units, Finance, Channel, Distribution, Inside Sales, Global Sales Support, Operations, and CMT to resolve complex opportunities and align stakeholders on the best business outcome.

• Process, Tools, and Governance: Execute approved workflows, maintain accurate data, apply pricing guardrails, and manage exceptions and escalations with urgency and accountability.

• Operational Excellence: Advance process simplification, automation, training, performance monitoring, and modern tools to reduce friction, improve quote response time, and strengthen customer experience.

• Strategic and AOP Initiatives: Own strategic projects and annual operating plan initiatives from problem identification through execution, delivering measurable improvements in organizational effectiveness and operational efficiency.

• Knowledge and Insight Sharing: Share market, pricing, and business insights; build capability across the organization; and contribute to a high-performing culture of ownership, collaboration, learning, and continuous improvement.

Requirements/Qualifications:

Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Business, Finance, Marketing, or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience.

• Demonstrated experience in pricing, quoting, product marketing, business analysis, sales operations, or a related commercial function.

• Strong analytical, problem-solving, and business acumen, with the ability to interpret complex data and make clear, defensible recommendations.

• Excellent written and verbal communication, stakeholder management, and influencing skills, including the ability to explain pricing decisions and train varied audiences.

• Proven ownership and accountability, combining strategic thinking with disciplined and timely execution through measurable completion.

• Demonstrated ability to work across functions, regions, leadership levels, and time zones; manage competing priorities; and remain adaptable in a fast-moving environment.

• Proficiency with Microsoft Excel and business systems, with the willingness and ability to learn Microchip pricing, quoting, reporting, and automation tools quickly.

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience in the semiconductor industry, including pricing, distribution, negotiating customer agreements, or product lifecycle management.

0% - 25%

Glanua is a leading provider of innovative and sustainable engineering solutions for water, wastewater and bioresources infrastructure. We design, build, operate and maintain critical infrastructure for municipal and industrial clients, combining engineering expertise, specialist technologies and off-site manufacturing to deliver efficient, sustainable solutions.

Our clients include major water utilities such as Uisce Eireann, Thames Water, Yorkshire Water and Affinity Water, alongside leading organisations in the pharmaceutical, life sciences, food and beverage and manufacturing sectors. Through our expertise in water and wastewater treatment, bioresources and resource recovery, we help protect the environment, safeguard water resources and support the transition to a circular economy.

Guided by our values of Respect, Collaboration, Accountability, Integrity, Excellence and Safety, we empower our people to innovate, develop their skills and reach their full potential while helping to create a cleaner, more sustainable planet.

As a Chemical or Environmental Engineering Intern, you will support multidisciplinary teams on water and wastewater projects from design through commissioning and operation, building practical skills in treatment processes, data analysis, environmental performance, energy efficiency and sustainability.

This is a formal internship opportunity undertaken as part of relevant Chemical Engineering, Environmental Engineering, Environmental Science, Energy Engineering or related studies. Under the guidance of senior staff, you will develop practical and professional skills, learn how treatment infrastructure is designed, delivered, commissioned and improved, and complete or return to your studies with stronger industry experience.

Graduate Programme Pathway

Final-year students graduating in 2027 who successfully complete the internship will, if they wish to continue with Glanua, be entitled to an immediate offer for the Glanua Chemical, Environmental or Energy Engineering Graduate Programme starting in September 2027, with no further interviews required.

The two-year Chemical, Environmental or Energy Engineering Graduate Programme combines live project experience with structured mentoring, training, one 12-month rotation and two six-month rotations. A six-month rotation may be available in Portugal or the UK, subject to business requirements and suitability, and graduates receive support towards future professional accreditation.

Maintain accurate project, process and environmental records and communicate progress clearly to colleagues.

Research relevant technologies, standards and regulatory developments and share findings through reports, case studies or presentations.
Communicate clearly with colleagues and contribute positively to multidisciplinary project and site teams.
Take part in mentoring, continuous learning and feedback.

Our Values

At Glanua, our values shape how we work together and how we serve our clients. We act with Respect towards our colleagues, clients and communities, and believe in the power of Collaboration to deliver the best outcomes for our teams and projects. We hold ourselves to a high standard of Accountability, taking ownership of our commitments, and act with Integrity in every decision we make. We pursue Excellence in everything we do, continuously improving how we design, build and operate, and we place Safety at the centre of our culture, ensuring the wellbeing of our people is never compromised. As a Chemical or Environmental Engineering Intern, you will be expected to demonstrate these values in your day-to-day work and learning.

Currently enrolled in Chemical Engineering, Environmental Engineering, Environmental Science, Energy Engineering or a closely related degree programme.
Able to complete the internship as a formal placement or work-based learning opportunity connected to your studies. Final-yea

jobs.title: Sustainability Graduate
jobs.description:
Sustainability Graduate Programme

Two year structured development programme

Programme Highlights

Build your sustainability career through a two-year programme that combines an in-depth placement with wider exposure to Glanua's water and wastewater business.

Structured rotations Complete one in-depth 12-month rotation followed by two additional six-month rotations across other areas of the business.
International opportunity One six-month rotation may be available in Portugal or the UK, subject to business requirements and individual suitability.
Training and development Learn through live projects, mentoring and structured training, with support towards future professional accreditation.

About Glanua

Glanua is an industry leader in providing innovative and sustainable engineering solutions to design, build, operate and maintain critical water and wastewater infrastructure across Ireland and the UK. We are a trusted provider to the municipal and industrial sectors, working with some of Ireland's and the UK's largest water utilities.

We are passionate about solving environmental challenges and contributing to a decarbonised and sustainable world. We provide an inclusive environment where people have the freedom to develop and reach their full potential, guided by our values of Safety and Well-being, Innovation, Integrity, Collaboration, Courage, Agility, Accountability, Diversity and Inclusion.

The Programme

The Sustainability Graduate Programme is designed for recent graduates beginning careers in corporate and project sustainability within the water and wastewater sector. Through practical experience, structured rotations, mentoring and professional development, you will learn how sustainability objectives are translated into measurable action across Glanua's operations, projects and value chain.

There will be one 12-month in-depth rotation, as well as another two 6-month rotations across other areas of the business. Potential rotation areas include group sustainability, project delivery, design and innovation, operations and maintenance, HSQE, energy management, procurement and supply chain, pre-contracts or commercial functions.

Depending on business requirements and suitable opportunities, graduates may have the opportunity to complete one of the six-month rotations in Portugal or the UK. International placements are not guaranteed and will be subject to operational requirements, individual suitability and any applicable travel or work eligibility requirements.

The Role

As a Sustainability Graduate, you will support the delivery of Glanua's sustainability priorities across the business, helping teams measure performance, identify improvements and embed practical environmental, social and governance considerations into projects and operations.

Main Duties and Responsibilities

Collect, validate and analyse sustainability data, including carbon, energy, water, waste, resource efficiency and other environmental, social and governance performance indicators.
Support sustainability reporting, performance dashboards, target tracking and evidence gathering for internal, client and regulatory requirements.
Contribute to carbon reduction, circular-economy, biodiversity, social-value and responsible procurement initiatives across projects, operations and the supply chain.
Research emerging sustainability legislation, standards and good practice, and help translate findings into practical guidance and improvement actions.
Collaborate with project, design, operations, HSQE, procurement and commercial teams, engaging clearly with colleagues, clients, suppliers and other stakeholders.

What We Are Looking For

A bachelor's degree in Sustainability, Environmental Science, Environmental Management, Energy, Engineering, Finance, Accounting, Business Sustainability or a closely related discipline, or expected completion before the programme begins.
A genuine interest in climate action, resource efficiency, the circular economy, biodiversity, social value and sustainable water and wastewater infrastructure.
Strong analytical, research, communication, teamwork and problem-solving skills, with the ability to present data and recommendations clearly.
A proactive approach, willingness to learn and flexibility to work across office, site and rotation locations.
Good working knowledge of Microsoft Word, Excel and PowerPoint. Experience with data visualisation or sustainability reporting tools is beneficial but not essential.
A full driving licence and access to your own vehicle. Both are essential due to project locations and programme travel requirements.
Previous sustainability, environmental, engineering, infrastructure or water-sector experience gained through an internship, work placement, summer role or university project is beneficial but not essential.

What We Offer

A structured two-year programme comprising one in-depth 12-month rotation and two additional six-month rotations.
The potential opportunity to complete one six-month rotation in Portugal or the UK.
Hands-on experience supporting sustainability across significant water and wastewater infrastructure projects, operations and corporate functions.
Mentoring, structured learning and support in developing the competencies required for future professional accreditation.
A competitive graduate salary with annual reviews, a company laptop and phone, 22 days' annual leave plus applicable public holidays, and access to a confidential Employee Assistance Programme.

On successful completion of the programme, graduates may be considered for permanent roles within Glanua, subject to individual performance, suitable vacancies and business requirements.

Equal Opportunities

Glanua Limited is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to creating an inclusive workplace and welcome applications from suitably qualified candidates from all backgrounds.

 Equal Opportunity Statement and Benefits

UPMC is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

At UPMC we provide a total rewards program that is not only market competitive, but fair and provides growth opportunities for all our colleagues.

About UPMC

UPMC is a renowned multinational academic medical centre committed to delivering people-focused care that’s close to home. Reporting to the Materials Management Workstream Lead, this role will provide practical support for general build team activities, data preparation, data entry, validation, testing, documentation, and issue follow-up within the Materials Management Pharmacy workstream. The Junior Analyst will work closely with pharmacy, materials management, and technical team members to help establish accurate pharmacy item and drug catalogue information in the EHR. The role requires a high degree of accuracy, consistency, and focus. It is well suited to a pharmacy technician who understands medication and drug catalogue information and who is interested in applying that knowledge to an EHR implementation environment.

This role is expected to complete assigned work independently, provide clear progress reporting, identify data quality concerns, and escalate questions or issues when required. Training and direction will be provided by senior workstream members, but the successful candidate must be organised, dependable, and comfortable completing detailed, repetitive data activities to a defined standard.

• Support the Materials Management Pharmacy team with general EHR build activities under the direction of senior analysts and the Workstream Lead.
• Enter, update, and maintain pharmacy and materials management data in approved build tools, configuration workbooks, templates, and MEDITECH Expanse environments.
• Support the creation and maintenance of drug stock records, pharmacy items, descriptions, identifiers, units of measure, packaging details, and other assigned data elements.
• Apply approved naming conventions, data standards, and build instructions consistently across all assigned records.
• Complete high-volume data entry accurately and within established work plans and programme deadlines.
• Compare source information against entered data and correct discrepancies before submitting work for review.
• Perform assigned data clean-up, standardisation, de-duplication, and record completion activities.
• Maintain clear status information for assigned build and data tasks, including work completed, items outstanding, questions, and identified issues.

Qualifications & Experience:

Required
• Qualification as a pharmacy technician, or equivalent relevant pharmacy education and experience.
• Practical knowledge of drug catalogues, medication terminology, packaging, and pharmacy item information.
• Demonstrated experience entering, maintaining, reviewing, or validating structured data with a strong level of accuracy.
• High attention to detail and the ability to identify missing, inconsistent, or duplicate information.
• Ability to follow documented instructions, naming conventions, data standards, and quality control processes.
• Ability to organise assigned work, meet deadlines, and report progress independently.
• Working knowledge of Microsoft Excel and confidence using spreadsheets, filters, lists, and structured data templates.
• Clear written and verbal communication skills and the ability to work effectively within a multidisciplinary project team.

Preferred

• Previous experience maintaining a pharmacy drug file, formulary, item master, stock catalogue, wholesaler catalogue, or related reference data.
• Exposure to MEDITECH Expanse, another EHR, a pharmacy information system, an ERP, or a materials management system.
• Experience supporting data conversion, catalogue standardisation, system implementation, testing, or quality assurance activities
• Familiarity with barcode, product identifier, unit-of-measure, pack-size, supplier, or inventory information.
• Experience investigating data discrepancies and documenting corrections or follow-up actions.

jobs.description:

Our ambitions to shape the future of sustainable mobility are powered by our talent. Join us, and get better with every move.

Requirements

A minimum 3 years’ experience in motor underwriting
CIP Qualified and / or an Insurance Graduate
Strong analytical skills and decision-making ability
Knowledge of underwriting rating methods, procedures and reviews
Excellent MS Office skills, in particular excel
Attention to detail and accuracy essential
A highly organized individual with the ability to prioritise and meet deadlines and act on own initiative
Good communication and interpersonal skills, both written and verbal
Team player who will play an important role as part of a specialized team
Innovative and creative with willingness to bring new ideas to improve processes

Desirable

5 years’ experience in motor underwriting

Experience in the design and construction of policy wordings for a range of motor insurance and ancillary covers
MDI qualified or progression towards this
Clear understanding or experience in the motor leasing industry

This role is subject to the Central Bank of Ireland Fitness and Probity Standards (“Standards”) . This role is subject to the Company satisfying itself (as required under the Standards) on reasonable grounds that a candidate complies with the Standards.

With over 3.1 million vehicles managed across more than 40 countries, we provide full-service leasing, flexible subscription services, fleet management services and multi-mobility solutions to customers of all sizes, including large corporates, SMEs, professionals, and private individuals. By leveraging our unique position to lead the way to net zero and further shape the digital transformation of the industry, we are well-positioned to meet the evolving mobility needs of our clients and provide them with the solutions they need to thrive.

Join us on this exciting journey as we continue to enable the transformation towards large scale adoption of sustainable mobility and provide our customers with the solutions they need to succeed. Follow our page for the latest updates, news, and insights.

jobs.description:
A GLOBAL LEADING ASSET MANAGER WITH A DIVERSE & INCLUSIVE CULTURE

As the Global Asset Management business of Prudential, we’re always looking for ways to improve financial services. We’re passionate about making a meaningful impact - touching the lives of millions and solving financial challenges in an ever-changing world.

We also believe talent is key to achieving our vision and are intentional about building a culture on respect and collaboration. When you join PGIM, you’ll unlock a motivating and impactful career – all while growing your skills and advancing your profession at one of the world’s leading global asset managers!

If you’re not afraid to think differently and challenge the status quo, come and be a part of a dedicated team that’s investing in your future by shaping tomorrow today.

At PGIM, You Can!

Location: This role is hybrid, based in our Letterkenny office two days a week.

What you can expect:

As an Investment Analyst, you will play a key role in supporting the onboarding and ongoing management of complex private investments. You will interpret transaction documentation, investigate and resolve data or system discrepancies, and help ensure investments are accurately and efficiently reflected across relevant systems. You will work closely with colleagues and business partners, maintain strong operational controls, and apply accounting knowledge and sound judgement to identify and manage potential risks.

What you will do:

Validation of portfolio and transaction level activity including trades, income payments, corporate actions, and deal restructurings in sub-ledger systems.
Reconcile cash activity to bank, work with bank on discrepancies.
Prepare and verify general ledger entries.
Prepare monthly reconciliations of balances between the accounting system and the general ledger.
Ensure financial statement balances are in accordance with GAAP & STAT principles.
Interface with various clients and business partners.
Prepare data for use in financial statement disclosures.
Provide support for various audits with internal and external auditors.
Prepare reports for our various internal and external business partners.
Work with the Technology team on systems improvements to the accounting system.

What you will bring:

Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Economics, Finance or Business.
Ability to understand and analyze basic accounting principles and financial statements.
Strong written, oral communication, and interpersonal skills.
Good organizational and time management skills.
Strong quantitative and analytical skills.
Works well in a team environment.

*PGIM welcomes all applicants, even if you don't meet every requirement. If your skills align with the role, we encourage you to apply.

What we offer you:

Health Insurance: PGIM Ireland partner with Laya and BUPA to provide health insurance schemes that cover eligible employees day to day medical and hospital expenses.
Annual Leave of 23 days at full pay.
Pension Scheme: Members of the scheme can contribute up to 8% of salary per annum and PGIM Ireland matches contributions up to 8% of salary. Members can also make voluntary contributions to the scheme.
Annual Bonus Programme & Shop LK Vouchers / CleverCards (subject to eligibility): Along with an annual bonus employees are rewarded with Shop LK Vouchers/ CleverCards which are paid tax free.
Life Assurance: fully paid by PGIM Ireland, employees are covered from their start date and beneficiaries are provided with a lump sum of four times an employee’s salary.
Education Assistance: PGIM Ireland have an Education Assistance Programme that reimburses eligible employees for furthering their education.

Prudential Financial, Inc. (PFI) of the United States is not affiliated in any manner with Prudential plc, incorporated in the United Kingdom, or with Prudential Assurance Company, a subsidiary of M&G plc, incorporated in the United Kingdom.

-

PGIM Ireland is proud to be an equal opportunity employer and is committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of applicants’ gender, civil status, family status, sexual orientation, religion, age, disability, race or membership of the traveler community. PGIM Ireland's aim is to hire the best people for the open roles and all appointments will be made on merit.

Any offer of employment made by PGIM Ireland will be contingent on receiving satisfactory references. Applicants should be aware that background checks will be carried out on all candidates offered a position within PGIM Ireland.

jobs.title: Portfolio Analyst/Associate
jobs.description:
PIMCO is a global leader in active fixed income with deep expertise across public and private markets. We invest our clients’ capital across a range of fixed income and credit opportunities, leveraging our decades of experience navigating complex debt markets. Our flexible capital base and deep relationships with issuers have helped us become one of the world’s largest providers of traditional and nontraditional solutions for companies that need financing and investors who seek strong risk-adjusted returns.

Since 1971, our people have shaped our organization through a high-performance inclusive culture, in which we celebrate diverse thinking. We invest in our people and strive to imprint our CORE values of Collaboration, Openness, Responsibility and Excellence. We believe each of us is here to help others succeed and this has led to PIMCO being recognized as an innovator, industry thought leader and trusted advisor to our clients.

Position Description

PIMCO is seeking an analytically minded, technology-curious professional to join its Dublin team as a Portfolio Analyst / Associate. Supporting portfolio management across PIMCO’s European trading rooms, the role combines investment analysis, trading desk support, portfolio maintenance and risk monitoring across a broad range of mandates and products.

The successful candidate will work closely with Portfolio Managers and partner teams across Account Management, Product Management, Legal and Compliance, and the cash desks to monitor portfolio positioning against investment guidelines, benchmarks and model weights.

Strong fixed income knowledge, analytical rigor and technical skills will be key, with responsibility for portfolio studies, performance and positioning analysis, and delivering timely insights to support investment decisions. The role also offers scope to improve how the team works, using automation, data analytics and AI-enabled tools to enhance portfolio management processes and workflows.

With close exposure to experienced Portfolio Managers and PIMCO’s broader European investment platform, this is a strong opportunity for someone looking to deepen their investment expertise while helping shape more efficient, technology-enabled ways of working.

Key Responsibilities

Portfolio Management & Trading Support

Partner with European portfolio management teams to support trading desk activities and day-to-day portfolio maintenance.
Rebalance portfolios to model and target weights, coordinating with the trading and cash desks as required.
Monitor client portfolio position weights and product positioning against client guidelines and benchmarks.
Review and ensure pre- and post-trade compliance, working with Legal and Compliance to resolve potential issues promptly.

Portfolio Analytics & Reporting

Generate studies across a set of mandates or products in accordance with investment guidelines and benchmarks.
Prepare portfolio summaries and monitor portfolio performance.
Conduct performance and attribution analysis, along with other analytics requested by Portfolio Managers.
Create and maintain reports for risk monitoring, highlighting key exposures and changes for Portfolio Managers.

Stakeholder Partnership

Build strong working relationships with Portfolio Management, Account Management, Product Management, Legal and Compliance, and the cash desks.
Communicate analysis, ideas and strategies clearly and concisely to Portfolio Managers, both verbally and in writing.
Work collaboratively across the organization to identify and resolve issues.

Process Improvement & Innovation

Lead and contribute to project work focused on improving portfolio management processes and workflows.
Identify opportunities to enhance efficiency, accuracy and controls through automation, data analytics (e.g., Python, SQL, VBA) and emerging technologies, including AI tools.

Position Requirements

Essential

Degree in finance, economics, mathematics or another quantitative/analytical field from a leading university, or equivalent experience.
Strong technical knowledge of fixed income markets and instruments.
Advanced Excel and Bloomberg skills.
Proficiency in at least one of the following: Python, SQL or VBA.
Demonstrated curiosity about, and experience using, new and emerging technologies and AI tools in your work.
Outstanding analytical and problem-solving skills, with strong attention to detail.
Ability to interact, communicate and build relationships with experienced Portfolio Managers, articulating ideas and strategies clearly, both verbally and in writing.
Ability to work collaboratively across the organization to resolve issues.
Proven track record of working efficiently in high-pressure environments and consistently meeting tight deadlines.

Preferred

Experience in portfolio management support, portfolio analytics, trading support or a related investment role within asset management.
Exposure to performance attribution, risk analytics or investment guideline/pre- and post-trade compliance processes.
Progress toward the CFA or a similar professional qualification.

jobs.title: Private Client Adviser
jobs.description:
About us

At Davy, it’s the unique talents of all our people that have been the foundations of our success for 100 years. As we continue to grow, so do you. Because you are not just part of our team – you are a key player in shaping our future.

At Davy, you are the difference.

Established in 1926, the Davy Group sits at the heart of wealth and capital in Ireland, providing a broad range of services to high-net-worth individuals, self-directed investors, small-to-medium enterprises, credit unions, corporations, and domestic & international institutional investors.

Our culture is shaped around three values, which are at the heart of everything we do: client success, one Davy, and building a proud legacy. Sharing the same goals, we work together to deliver exceptional outcomes for our clients. As part of a team of over 900, you will be encouraged to learn and to grow, both professionally and personally.

About the role

An exciting opportunity has arisen for a Private Client Adviser to join Davy. The Private Client Adviser team supports clients with increasingly complex financial needs who require ongoing financial planning and investment advice to build, protect and transfer wealth. Working with a diverse portfolio of clients, you will help individuals, families and corporates work through bespoke financial planning-led investment, protection and pension journeys.

The successful candidate will:

Build trusted relationships with clients, understanding their financial objectives, personal circumstances and long-term goals.
Convert referral opportunities into new business through effective advice conversations and relationship management.
Deliver holistic financial advice across investments, pensions, retirement and protection solutions.
Provide clear, compliant financial advice and develop tailored financial plans aligned to client needs using Davy’s digital platform and client engagement tools.
Build and maintain a strong pipeline of prospective clients through referrals and lead generation opportunities
Engage and influence to create and grow effective partnerships, both internally and externally, to drive new business performance.
Partner closely with Bank of Ireland, Davy and wider Group colleagues to maximise referral opportunities and deliver joined-up client outcomes.
Direct and manage, formally or informally, others involved in complex processes to ensure ultimate successful delivery of client outcomes.
Make informed, transparent decisions and consider the broader/longer term implications for the benefit of client and business. Engage, direct and manage others in decision making processes, gaining agreement and managing collective work to successful conclusion.
Ensure that all activities and duties are carried out in full compliance with regulatory requirements, Davy’s Risk Management Framework and internal Policies and Policy Standards;
Take ownership for issues that impact clients, leading others where necessary and proactively seeking opportunities to lead business improvement. Identify issues, solve problems and enable breakthrough innovations, as well as incremental improvements to the business and our client service.

What will make you stand out?

You enjoy building long-term trusted relationships and are passionate about helping clients achieve better financial outcomes. You combine strong technical financial planning knowledge with the ability to communicate complex concepts in a simple and engaging manner.
You are client focused and take pride in delivering advice with integrity, professionalism and care. With circa 4+ years’ experience providing financial advice, including, some or all of the following: pensions, investment and protection, either within Ireland or outside of Ireland. Previous experience in a Mifid firm is desirable but not essential.
You are organised and proactive, managing your time effectively while maintaining high standards of administration and compliance. You enjoy building relationships and working collaboratively with colleagues and referral partners. You are curious about economic and product developments and motivated to continue developing your technical knowledge, supported by structured training and ongoing professional development.
You embrace technology and are comfortable using digital planning tools, CRM platforms and client portals to improve client outcomes. You adapt quickly to digital ways of working while ensuring all regulatory and compliance standards are met.
You are naturally curious, commercially minded and committed to ongoing professional development.

You may currently be working as:

An established Financial Adviser.
A Financial Planner or Associate Adviser within a wealth management firm.
A (Senior) Investment or Portfolio Analyst seeking to transition into a client-facing advisory career.
An Adviser within a retail banking, life and pensions or protection business.
A Wealth Management professional supporting advisers and seeking the next step into lead advisory responsibilities.

Degree or Masters level qualification in a business, accounting, law, engineering or related discipline.

Work with the Risk and Resilience function to ensure cyber risks are reflected in the corporate risk register where appropriate.

· Maintain cyber KPIs, KRIs and management dashboards covering risk exposure, remediation, training, vulnerabilities, incidents, supplier assurance and control maturity.

Security Operations

Third-Party and Supplier Security Management

· Coordinate cyber risk assessments for suppliers and third-party service providers.

· Track supplier-related cyber risks, remediation actions, assurance evidence and contractual obligations.

· Support external assurance activities relating to supplier security controls and operational resilience.

Audit and Compliance Support

· Support internal and external audit activities relating to information security, cyber security, resilience and compliance.

Cyber Awareness

· Promote a strong cyber security culture across the organisation by making cyber responsibilities clear and practical.

· Support targeted cyber training for incident response teams, system owners, IT teams, project teams and business stakeholders.

Stakeholder Management, Communication and Reporting

· Strong knowledge of cyber risk management, control assessments, remediation tracking and governance reporting.

· Experience developing, reviewing, implementing and monitoring cyber security policies, standards, SOPs and procedures.

· Experience preparing cyber security reports for senior management, executive committees, audit/risk committees or Board-level governance forums.

· Practical understanding of NIS2, CyFun, ISO 27001, NIST Cybersecurity Framework.

Relevant professional certification such as CISSP, CISM, CRISC, CISA.

BEAUMONT HOSPITAL

(Incorporating St Joseph’s Hospital, Raheny)

Beaumont Hospital, incorporating St. Joseph’s Hospital Raheny, is a large academic teaching hospital 5km north of Dublin City centre. Beaumont Hospital provides emergency and acute care services across 54 medical specialties to a local community of some 290,000 people. In addition, Beaumont Hospital is a designated cancer centre and the regional treatment centre for ear, nose and throat, and gastroenterology, and the national referral centre for neurosurgery and neurology, renal transplantation, cochlear implantation and mechanical thrombectomy.

Beaumont Hospital is the lead Level 4 hospital within the Royal College of Surgeons Hospital Group, which includes Connolly Hospital, Rotunda Hospital, Cavan/Monaghan Hospitals, Louth/Meath Hospitals, and the Royal College of Surgeons. Beaumont Hospital employs approximately 4,000 staff and has a bed complement of 820 beds. Beaumont Hospital is the principal teaching hospital for the Royal College of Surgeons in Ireland.

Beaumont Hospital also enjoys close links with Dublin City University, especially in the area of nurse training, and with other academic institutions in respect of training and research.

St. Joseph's Hospital Raheny, is an acute hospital that provides both medical and surgical in-patient care, day care, outpatient, outpatient physiotherapy and radiology services. A dedicated Care of the Elderly Rehabilitation Unit and a 100 bedded Raheny Community Nursing Unit have also been developed on the St. Joseph’s campus.

Applications are invited from suitably qualified doctors for the following post which is available from 11th January 2027 for 12 months

Completion of your Medical degree in English from any of the following countries: Australia, Canada, New Zealand, The United States of America or The United Kingdom. A copy of your Degree Certificate is the required evidence
