Our partner is looking for a Support Agent (Freelance, Night Shifts) based in Ireland.We are looking for a customer-focused Support Agent to provide reliable, high-quality assistance to users of an international digital learning platform.Working remotely on a freelance basis, you will handle incoming customer inquiries primarily through email.You will help users navigate the platform, resolve issues, and enjoy a smooth experience with its cognitive training tools and educational content.The role combines customer communication, technical troubleshooting, payment-related requests, and collaboration with internal teams.You will also contribute to improving support processes, documentation, and response templates.This position is suited to someone who is comfortable working independently in a fast-paced digital environment.The schedule follows a rotating night-shift pattern to ensure continuous customer support.AccountabilitiesIn this role, you will be responsible for delivering responsive and empathetic customer assistance while helping maintain efficient support operations. Your main responsibilities will include:Handle incoming customer inquiries from users worldwide, primarily through email, providing clear, accurate, and helpful responses. Meet individual and team performance targets, including First Response Time, Resolution Time, and Customer Satisfaction (CSAT). Develop strong knowledge of the platform, its features, and internal support processes to resolve customer issues effectively. Gather relevant information on complex cases and escalate bug reports or other issues to the appropriate technical, product, or legal teams. Coordinate refund requests and process transactions through relevant payment systems. Identify opportunities to improve customer service workflows, contribute to the creation and refinement of response templates, and help test and implement new support tools. Maintain accurate internal documentation and participate in regular one-to-one meetings and team discussions. Work a rotating 2-days-on, 2-days-off schedule, covering night shifts from 20:00 to 06:00. RequirementsThe ideal candidate has an initial background in customer-facing support or sales, strong written English, and the ability to handle customer requests with professionalism and attention to detail. You should also demonstrate the following:English proficiency at B1+ level or above, with strong written communication skills for handling customer inquiries by email. At least 3 months to 1+ year of experience in customer support, technical support, sales (particularly for English-speaking markets), or customer retention. Good technical aptitude and the ability to learn digital products, troubleshoot issues, gather relevant information, and escalate cases accurately. Experience maintaining internal documentation and working with response templates or macros. Strong empathy and a customer-first mindset, with the ability to remain helpful and professional in difficult or sensitive situations. Resilience and the ability to manage a high volume of requests while remaining calm and polite. Adaptability and flexibility when working with evolving processes, new tools, and changing priorities in a fast-paced environment. Excellent attention to detail, particularly when documenting customer issues and preparing escalations. Openness to constructive feedback and the ability to communicate suggestions to colleagues and team leads. Availability to work the required rotating night-shift schedule. BenefitsFreelance working arrangement. Remote work within the eligible locations. A rotating 2/2 schedule, with night shifts from 20:00 to 06:00. Initial training lasting two days, followed by two test shifts. Opportunities to develop customer support, troubleshooting, and digital product expertise. Exposure to an international user base and collaboration with cross-functional teams. How Jobgether WorksWe use an AI-powered matching process to ensure your application is reviewed quickly, objectively, and fairly against the role's core requirements. Our system identifies the top-fitting candidates, and this shortlist is then shared directly with the hiring company. The final decision and next steps (interviews, assessments) are managed by their internal team.We appreciate your interest and wish you the best! Why Apply Through Jobgether?Data Privacy Notice: By submitting your application, you acknowledge that Jobgether will process your personal data to evaluate your candidacy and share relevant information with the hiring employer. This processing is based on legitimate interest and pre-contractual measures under applicable data protection laws (including GDPR). You may exercise your rights (access, rectification, erasure, objection) at any time.We may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of the hiring process, such as reviewing applications, analyzing resumes, or assessing responses and identifying potential inconsistencies or verification signals in application materials based on available information. These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. jobs.description: We help partners understand the changing advertising landscape. jobs.title: Workplace & Technical Operations Generalist
jobs.description: Main MissionThe Workplace & Technical Operations Generalist, Dublin is a hands-on, field-oriented generalist whose core strength is event/AV production, backed by the ability to act as EMEA's remote hands for on-site technical troubleshooting and steady-state workplace operations for the Dublin office.This is a generalist role, not a specialist one. What matters most is genuine curiosity about technology, the ability to pick up new tools and workflows quickly, and comfort working independently and traveling autonomously across Dublin, Paris, and other EMEA officeAbout The Role AV & Event Production (EMEA)Provides hands on AV setup, teardown, and live support for all-hands, offsites, and internal events across Dublin, London, Paris, and other EMEA offices, in person or remotely. Helps coordinate production vendors for larger events (staging, sound, lighting, streaming) region-wide. Maintains and troubleshoots AV equipment and conferencing systems across meeting rooms EMEA-wide, picking up new AV/conferencing tools as needs evolve; no specific platform expertise is required going in. Runs or supports livestreaming/broadcast setup for multi-office all-hands. Builds local know-how so recurring AV/event needs don't require flying in outside support each time.  Remote Hands & On-Site Technical Support (EMEA)Acts as EMEA's "remote hands": travels to Dublin, Paris, and other offices to physically diagnose and fix issues (e.g. a faulty device or cabling problem) so rooms and systems aren't down for weeks waiting on a specialist. Provides on-site support for meeting rooms, network closets, and building-technology touchpoints across EMEA offices. Coordinates with the PREWF infrastructure team on building systems (BMS, access control, smart lighting) rather than owning strategy or configuration decisions. Escalates issues beyond hands-on physical troubleshooting rather than duplicating the helpdesk team's remit.  Workplace & Facilities OperationsActs as a point of contact for day-to-day workplace matters in the Dublin office, including supplies, deliveries, and service providers. Ensures meeting rooms, common areas, and shared spaces are maintained to a high standard. Uses internal tools (e.g. Jira ticketing or similar) to track workplace and facilities requests. Supports basic building maintenance coordination (HVAC, electrical, plumbing) with landlords and vendors; licensed electrical or certified rigging work always goes through a qualified provider. Supports compliance with local health and safety requirements (fire safety, first aid coordination, risk prevention) and helps organize mandatory training and drills.  Project Support, Budget & Continuous ImprovementSupports vendor coordination and project tracking for regional technical and workplace initiatives. Assists with budget tracking for AV, workplace, and technical equipment expenses across EMEA. Identifies opportunities to improve employee experience through better tools and light automation (e.g. Notion-based workflows); curiosity here is valued, deep automation or data ownership is not expected of this role. Assists with small office moves, adds, and changes involving technical systems.  Collaboration & ReportingWorks in close collaboration with the PREWFI EMEA team to ensure alignment across Workplace, Facilities, and Technical activities. Partners closely with Infrastructure and Security on systems, network, and infrastructure projects. jobs.title: Automation & Manufacturing Engineer
jobs.description:
Working within the Operations Engineering team, the *Automation & Manufacturing Engineer* will drive operational efficiency targets (OEE), support new manufacturing project implementations, and optimize automated assets. This role requires a strong blend of hands-on electromechanical troubleshooting and industrial automation literacy. The successful candidate will act as the internal subject matter expert (SME) for machine diagnostics—interrogating PLC code to pinpoint root causes, resolving complex faults locally, and technically managing external OEMs for major software modifications or system upgrades.

*Essential Duties and Responsibilities*

* *PLC Code Interrogation & Diagnostics:* Connect to PLC processors, navigate code, view real-time I/O status, and trace rungs to identify underlying hardware or sequence-of-operation faults.
* *OEM & Vendor Liaison:* Act as the primary technical point of contact for external OEMs; clearly communicate diagnostic findings from the code to facilitate rapid remote support or formal software modifications.
* *Electromechanical Troubleshooting:* Apply systematic root-cause problem-solving to resolve complex mechanical, electrical, pneumatic, and robotic integration issues on high-volume production equipment.
* *Asset Reliability:* Oversee preventative (PM) and corrective maintenance strategies, ensuring all technical documentation, schematics, and CMMS records are kept up to date.
* *Continuous Improvement (CI):* Identify engineering bottlenecks and lead projects utilizing Lean Manufacturing tools to eliminate waste, improve cycle times, and optimize line yield.
* *Project Support & Validation:* Assist in the introduction of new manufacturing lines, participating in equipment commissioning, factory acceptance testing (FAT), and validation protocols (IQ/OQ).
* *Technical Mentorship:* Act as a technical escalation point for shift technicians, delivering targeted training on complex automated systems and managing spare parts critical lists.

*Basic Qualifications & Experience*

* *Education:* *Level 7 or Level 8 NFQ degree* in Automation, Mechatronics, Electrical, Mechanical Engineering, *OR* a *Level 6 Advanced Certificate / Trade Qualification* (e.g., Electrical, Instrumentation, or Fitter trade) paired with extensive automation experience.
* *Experience:* 3 to 5 years of experience in a fast-paced, high-volume manufacturing environment (e.g., Medical Devices, Pharma, FMCG).

*Required Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities*

* *PLC Troubleshooting:* *Strong proficiency in PLC fault-finding and code comprehension* (e.g., Rockwell Automation/Allen-Bradley, Siemens S7/TIA Portal, or Mitsubishi). Must be comfortable uploading/downloading programs, reviewing logic rungs, and forcing I/O safely during troubleshooting.
* *Electrical & Mechanical Expertise:* Strong competency in reading and interpreting electrical schematics, P&IDs, pneumatic circuits, and mechanical drawings.
* *Hardware Proficiency:* Practical experience with servo drives, variable speed drives (VSDs), sensors, vision systems (e.g., Cognex, Keyence), and industrial networks (EtherNet/IP, Profinet).
* *Problem Solving:* Demonstrated ability to perform true root-cause analysis (RCA) under pressure in a high-volume environment.
* *Communication:* Excellent technical communication skills to articulately document issues for internal teams and external OEM engineering partners.

Benefits:
* On-site parking

Work Location: In person

jobs.title: Automation Engineer
jobs.description:
embecta is a global medical device company with a 100-year legacy in insulin delivery and diabetes care. Driven by innovation, purpose, and a commitment to improving lives, we are expanding our portfolio of solutions to serve even more patients, healthcare providers, and communities around the world.


Join a team where technology and innovation drive operational excellence. The Automation Engineer is responsible for developing, enhancing and supporting manufacturing automation systems that improve plant performance, product quality and operational reliability.


Leading automation projects and continuous improvement initiatives, this role delivers measurable improvements in safety, efficiency and productivity while ensuring compliance with regulatory and quality requirements. Acting as a key technical resource, the Automation Engineer provides hands-on engineering leadership and expertise to support manufacturing operations and future growth.


Responsibilities:

  • Design, develop, implement and optimise automation solutions for manufacturing equipment and processes.
  • Lead automation activities associated with equipment upgrades, process improvements and capital projects.
  • Develop functional specifications, design documentation, test protocols and change controls.
  • Support equipment commissioning, validation, qualification and start-up activities.
  • Lead troubleshooting and root cause investigations for complex automation and manufacturing issues.
  • Develop and implement sustainable corrective and preventive actions.
  • Support lifecycle management of automation hardware and software platforms.
  • Collaborate with equipment vendors, system integrators and cross-functional teams during project execution.
  • Analyse equipment and process performance data to identify opportunities for improvement.
  • Ensure automation systems comply with company standards, GMP requirements and applicable regulations.
  • Provide technical coaching and support to Automation Technicians.
  • Participate in Operational Excellence, Lean Manufacturing and continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Support achievement of departmental and site objectives.
  • Any other reasonable duties which may be required by management from time to time


Educational Requirements and Relevant Experience:

  • Degree in Automation, Electrical, Electronic, Mechatronic or related Engineering discipline.
  • Minimum 4 years' experience in an automation engineering role within a manufacturing environment.
  • Experience delivering automation projects from concept through implementation.
  • Experience with equipment commissioning, validation and change management processes.
  • Experience in regulated manufacturing environments desirable.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

  • Strong knowledge of industrial automation and machine control systems within a manufacturing environment.
  • Demonstrated experience programming, modifying and troubleshooting Allen Bradley ControlLogix and CompactLogix PLC systems.
  • Strong knowledge of Rockwell Automation software platforms and manufacturing control architectures.
  • Experience developing, modifying and optimising Cognex Vision System applications.
  • Strong understanding of industrial networks including Ethernet/IP and device integration.
  • Experience integrating automation systems with HMIs, SCADA systems and manufacturing databases.
  • Working knowledge of MES interfaces and manufacturing data collection systems.
  • Experience supporting motion control systems, robotics, machine safety systems and equipment integration.
  • Strong understanding of validation methodologies, software lifecycle management and change control processes.
  • Demonstrated root cause analysis and problem-solving capability.
  • Strong project management, planning and cross-functional communication skills.

The primary focus of this role is the validation strategy for systems incorporating artificial intelligence / machine-learning (AI/ML) components, ensuring these are validated for intended use in line with emerging regulatory expectations, including the draft EU GMP Annex 22 (Artificial Intelligence), Annex 11, GAMP 5 (Second Edition) and the ISPE GAMP Guide: Artificial Intelligence.Alongside this AI focus, the consultant defines and owns the validation strategies and plans that govern how these larger systems are validated and maintained in a validated state. Define validation scope, acceptance strategy, deliverable set, and the leverage of supplier documentation for each system based on risk and criticality. Define the strategy for periodic review, change-driven re-validation, and ongoing validated-state maintenance post go-live. Define the approach to deviation handling, remediation, and evidence standards so validation packages are consistent, defensible and inspection-ready.Key Competencies Deep technical expertise in LIMS — comfortable in the system configuration layer, not just the user interface. Validation mindset: meticulous, evidence-based documentation and zero tolerance for gaps in the validation package. Strong scientific and risk-based acumen — understands the “why” behind analytical methods, laboratory workflows and AI model behaviour, not just the mechanics. Ability to think strategically about emerging regulation (Annex 22) while executing hands-on validation work. Clear, structured technical writing for validation strategies, plans, SOPs and specifications. Collaborative, multidisciplinary approach — works effectively across QC lab teams, IT/data science, quality assurance, and vendors. Self-directed and proactive; manages own workload and flags risks and roadblocks early rather than letting them escalate.

jobs.title: Slot Mathematician (Hard Rock Games)
jobs.description:
What are we building?

At Hard Rock Games, we’re not just making games—we’re crafting experiences that connect people, deliver thrills, and celebrate the spirit of Hard Rock. As the social casino gaming arm of Hard Rock Digital, our teams shape every stage of the journey from concept to launch to live operations, giving our teams the ability to innovate, experiment, and make real impact. With the backing of a globally recognized brand, we combine the agility of a startup with the reach of an entertainment powerhouse. Here, creativity thrives, ideas scale, and careers grow.

We’re looking for passionate creators, builders, and innovators to join us in shaping the future of free-to- play gaming. Let’s play hard.

What’s the position?

Hard Rock Games is hiring a Slot Mathematician to design, model, and validate the math behind our slot games across our game portfolio. You will own the mathematical correctness of every game - from design through player-facing release - ensuring models meet target performance metrics and regulatory requirements.

Key Responsibilities

Design and model slot game math: reel strips, paytables, symbol weights, bonus features, free spins, and jackpots.
Tune models to hit target RTP, hit frequency, and volatility, including multiple RTP variants.
Analyze simpler games directly using data analysis tools; write and validate simulations in code for more complex games.
Playtest game builds and verify that implemented games match the designed model, payouts, and feature behavior.
Produce PAR sheets and comprehensive math documentation for internal review and certification labs (GLI, BMM).
Support regulatory certification across jurisdictions by answering lab and regulator questions.
Partner with game designers early, advising on feature costs in RTP and impact on volatility.
Help build a shared Java codebase of simulators, model libraries and math tools, starting from our existing tools.
Work closely with developers from specification through release to ensure correct math implementation.
Leverage AI tools to prototype ideas, generate code, and explore possibilities - while maintaining full ownership of correctness.

What are we looking for?

3+ years designing math models for slot games with shipped titles in iGaming, Social, or Land- Based environments. Experience in a regulated environment is preferred.
Ability to build and analyze slot models directly using data analysis tools - comfortable performing direct mathematical analysis.
Strong programming and problem-solving skills; Java preferred, but solid Python, C++, or C# is welcome.
Comfort with version control systems like Git and working in shared code repositories.
Strong grasp of probability, combinatorics, and expected-value analysis.
Ability to manually verify, derive, and explain math results. You understand why a model is correct, not just that it runs.
Bachelor's degree in Mathematics, Statistics, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related quantitative field.
Clear communication skills - explaining math concepts to designers, producers, and regulators.

What’s in it for you?

Make a visible impact: you’ll own campaigns and events that shape how millions play. Fast-paced execution + brand heritage: build boldly under the Hard Rock name.

Competitive compensation with flexible vacation and hybrid work.
Be part of a player-obsessed, inclusive team that trusts your autonomy and skills.
Influence product strategies, your post-mortems and insights will steer our roadmaps.

Roster of Uniques

We care deeply about every interaction our customers have with us, and trust and empower our staff to own and drive their experience. Our vision for our business and customers is built on fostering a diverse and inclusive work environment where regardless of background or beliefs you feel able to be authentic and bring all your talent into play. We want to celebrate you being you (we are an equal opportunity employer).

jobs.title: Engineering Graduate
jobs.description:
Location: Waterford, Ireland
Start Date: 1 September 2027
Duration: 23 months | Two 8-month rotations, and 7-month
Working Model: on-site
Working Hours: Full-time
Salary: €41,600 gross per annum
Assessment Centre: January 2027 | In person, Waterford

Your opportunity at Sanofi

Ready to turn your academic knowledge into real-world experience?

Join Sanofi, a global biopharmaceutical company, through our 23-month Graduate Programme in Waterford. Explore three different functions, gain hands-on industry experience and develop the skills to shape your future career.

Our engineers are at the heart of bringing innovative medicines to patients, solving complex challenges and driving continuous improvement across manufacturing operations. This programme offers a unique opportunity to explore different engineering disciplines, contribute to real projects and develop the skills and experience needed to become a future engineering leader.

One programme. Three rotations. A world of experience.

Why explore just one area when you could experience three?

Our structured Graduate Programme takes you through two 8-month rotations, and 7-month, providing exposure to different functions, meaningful projects and opportunities to learn from experienced professionals.

Your rotation journey

Rotation 1: Engineering | Months 1–8

Start your journey in Engineering, where you'll gain an understanding of the technical infrastructure and systems that enable a world-class biopharmaceutical manufacturing facility to operate safely, efficiently and reliably. Working alongside engineering teams, you'll develop practical knowledge of equipment, utilities, maintenance and continuous improvement practices that support the delivery of medicines to patients worldwide.

Gain hands-on experience across Engineering functions including Maintenance, Projects and Utilities.
Support equipment reliability and preventive maintenance activities, helping to ensure safe and efficient manufacturing operations.
Contribute to troubleshooting and continuous improvement initiatives while collaborating with cross-functional teams to solve operational challenges and enhance process performance.

Rotation 2: Operations | Months 9–16

Build on your engineering foundation by moving into Operations, where you'll gain first-hand experience of biopharmaceutical manufacturing and learn how products are produced in a highly regulated GMP environment. You'll work closely with manufacturing teams to understand the processes, systems and controls that ensure the safe and reliable supply of medicines to patients.

Support batch execution and day-to-day manufacturing activities within a GMP-regulated environment.
Develop an understanding of manufacturing processes, SOPs, quality requirements and operational excellence principles.
Gain exposure to Quality, Supply Chain and other site functions, building an understanding of how different teams collaborate to ensure reliable product delivery.

Rotation 3: Engineering Projects & Validation | Months 17–23

Complete your graduate journey in Engineering Projects and Validation, where you'll apply the technical and operational knowledge gained throughout the programme while contributing to projects that support site expansion, equipment implementation and regulatory compliance. You'll gain valuable experience managing complex initiatives and ensuring systems and equipment are fit for their intended use in a regulated environment.

Support engineering projects from planning through execution, collaborating with internal stakeholders and external vendors to deliver project objectives safely, on time and within scope.
Participate in qualification and validation activities, including commissioning, IQ/OQ/PQ execution, documentation review and compliance with GMP requirements.
Contribute to continuous improvement, technology implementation and facility enhancement projects while developing project management, stakeholder engagement and problem-solving skills.

Your development focus

Throughout the programme, you'll develop the technical, operational and leadership skills needed to build a successful career in Engineering within a biopharmaceutical manufacturing environment.

Develop a strong understanding of manufacturing operations, engineering systems and GMP-regulated processes.
Build problem-solving, project management and cross-functional collaboration skills by working with teams across Operations, Engineering, Supply Chain and MSAT.
Gain hands-on experience in continuous improvement, equipment reliability, troubleshooting and operational excellence, while developing the confidence to lead initiatives and drive meaningful business outcomes.

Your growth, our commitment

Your development is at the heart of our programme. Here's what you can look forward to:

Three diverse rotations: Explore different functions and build a broader understanding of the business.
Dedicated cross-functional mentor: Receive guidance from an assigned mentor, with monthly check-ins throughout the programme.
A buddy in every rotation: Get practical, day-to-day support as you settle into each new team.
Hands-on training: Learn directly from experienced colleagues and develop skills through practical experience and training opportunities.

Who we're looking for

We're looking for curious, motivated graduates who are eager to learn, collaborate and explore new opportunities.

To be eligible, you'll need to:

Have graduated within the past two years or be due to graduate before 1 September 2027.
Hold a minimum 2.1 primary degree or a Master's degree in Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Process Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics Engineering or a related discipline.
Have full, unrestricted right to work in Ireland.

Essential skills

Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to identify opportunities for improvement and implement practical solutions.

jobs.description:
DESCRIPTION

Fascinated by the mechanics behind automated systems? Want to master both electrical and mechanical engineering while working with cutting-edge technology? Amazon is the perfect place to launch your career in Mechatronics Maintenance.

As one of the world's most advanced technology-driven companies, we're powered by automation, robotics, and continuous innovation - from robotic arms to complex conveyor networks and smart sensor technology that keep millions of customer orders moving. This apprenticeship gives you the chance to become a multi-skilled maintenance technician across both electrical and mechanical disciplines, with hands-on experience on industry-leading equipment, some of which only exists at Amazon.

Our European Engineering team is fundamental to our operations - they keep vital machinery running around the clock. As an OEM Engineering Technician Apprentice, you'll help maintain a wide range of equipment while upholding Health and Safety best practice, keeping your colleagues safe, preventing downtime, and improving the availability and quality of our equipment.

You'll thrive here if you stay calm when things go wrong and get a real kick out of fixing them. You're hands-on, curious about how machines work, and you understand that keeping production moving is what it's all about. And you don't need to be a qualified engineer to start - what matters most is a practical, problem-solving mindset and a hunger to learn.

A day in the life can involve:

- Carrying out proactive and preventative maintenance
- Carrying out reactive repairs and fault diagnosis in a live distribution warehouse
- Using the latest tools to maximise equipment effectiveness
- Making modifications and upgrades to existing equipment
- Upholding health and safety policies and practices
- Working on continuous improvement projects, and suggesting long-term improvements

Throughout your apprenticeship, you'll build a broad, in-demand engineering skillset, including:

- Fault diagnosis and preventative maintenance
- Mechanical device maintenance, and fluid power systems assembly and testing
- Electrical equipment wiring and testing
- Hydraulics and pneumatics
- Programmable Logic Controller (PLC) operations
- CAD design and 3D printing

Here at Amazon, it's in our nature to learn and be curious. Within this apprenticeship, you'll learn by doing, putting newfound knowledge into practice every day. Our first-class coaching, tailored development opportunities, and challenging, rewarding work will empower you to reach new heights. In subsequent years, you'll undertake on-the-job training in a Fulfilment Centre while concurrently completing your academic training, learning directly from experienced technicians and engineers and gaining exposure to real engineering projects. Alongside invaluable experience, you'll gain a number of externally recognised qualifications.

This role supports our 24/7 operation, so you'll work shifts covering days, nights and weekends - patterns that reflect the real-world schedules of the engineers who keep Amazon operating around the clock.

You'll join a diverse and passionate team of engineers dedicated to driving results and pushing creative boundaries. We value different perspectives and experiences, and we're dedicated to creating an inclusive environment where everyone can thrive. Our employee-led affinity groups - including communities for women in tech, LGBTQ+ employees, and underrepresented minorities - foster a culture of inclusion that empowers us to be proud of our differences. These groups provide community, mentorship, and a platform for your voice to be heard. We're committed to building a workforce that reflects the customers and communities we serve.

We're continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth's Best Employer. That's why you'll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship, and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a well-rounded professional.

Join us and be part of the team that keeps Amazon moving. Apply now and shape the future of technology with us.

jobs.title: Chief Technology Officer
jobs.description:
Overview

We are recruiting a Chief Technology Officer to lead technology across the HIL group and to build the global platform that every Montu market will run on. This role is remote for people located in Ireland.

The mandate is consolidation and delivery. Today each region maintains its own stack, its own roadmap and its own relationship with the central technology function. The decision has been taken to stop funding separate stacks and to make one platform available across every market. Turning that decision into a delivered, adopted reality is the job.

The role is based in Dublin with HILE and carries accountability for HIL Ireland, HIL Australia, HIL UK and any future entity where technology sits. HILE was founded in November 2024 and is the group headquarters. HIL Australia was created in 2026 by separating technology out of Montu Australia, and HIL UK follows by the end of 2026 when the UK technology and product teams transfer in. The group is approximately 78 people today: 18 in Ireland of whom 15 are engineers, around 50 in Australia and around 10 in the UK, with the Australian product team due to move across before year end.

You will have the autonomy to restructure the organisation. Engineering leadership in Australia, the UK and Ireland reports to you from day one, and the shape of the function beyond that is yours to determine.

What makes this role unusual

A platform decision already made, and not yet delivered. The direction is agreed at the founder level. What is missing is the leadership to sequence it, resource it and hold markets to it. Genuine structural authority. Three engineering leaders across three countries report in, product is expected to follow, and you have an explicit mandate to redesign the organisation rather than inherit it. A founder who wants to step back, and a real commercial question attached. HIL is funded by the markets it serves, so defining what they buy and what it costs is part of the role.

What You Will Walk Into

We would rather be straight about the starting position.

Three engineering groups in Ireland, Australia and the UK, at different levels of maturity and not yet operating as one function
A capable platform built in Australia that has not yet been made available to other markets
Germany live on the platform with migration issues outstanding, and internal pressure to revert rather than fix forward
New Zealand growing and waiting on specific platform capability before it can adopt
An in-flight consolidation moving the UK engineering team into HIL, with contracts under review
Markets at different stages of adoption, holding different views on how and when consolidation should happen. The direction is set at the founder level. Building alignment behind it is part of this job rather than something that will be settled before you arrive.

If you want a settled function with a mature operating model, this is not it. If that list reads as the reason to take the job, we should talk.

Key Responsibilities

Global Platform Strategy and Delivery

Own the eighteen month global platform vision and convert it into a sequenced, resourced and costed delivery plan that leadership and the markets can commit to publicly
Make the platform available across all markets and retire duplicate regional stacks, including the migration sequence for Germany, New Zealand and the UK
Set and hold fixed scopes, dates and resourcing so markets plan against technology commitments rather than around them, and take the difficult architectural calls including where to fix forward rather than build bespoke

Operating Model and Engagement

Design the operating model across core platform build, market migration, innovation, day-to-day run and market-employed teams, with clear ownership and funding for each
Define how global teams and regional markets work together across time zones, including the local technical capability each market needs so no market is blocked waiting on another
Move the relationship with markets from ad-hoc requests to scoped, funded deliverables with transparent cost and committed dates, while insulating core delivery from local escalation

Organisation and Leadership

Lead technology across the HIL group, with engineering leadership in Australia, the UK and Ireland reporting in, and product expected to follow
Restructure the organisation as required, including how global and market-based teams are composed and where capability should sit
Complete the in-flight consolidation of market engineering teams into HIL, and raise engineering standards and delivery discipline consistently across all three locations

Commercial and Stakeholder Leadership

Own the HIL cost base, capacity planning and resource allocation across entities, and the value case for the markets that fund it, including how innovation work is budgeted
Build alignment across market leadership on the platform strategy and hold the direction steady while that is worked through, making trade-offs explicit rather than letting them resurface as escalations
Work closely with a technically engaged founder who has already committed to the platform, and take ownership of it so that technology decisions no longer need to sit with him
Ensure technology governance, security, data protection and regulatory obligations are met across every jurisdiction in which the group operates

Ideal Candidate Profile

Experience

Has consolidated multiple regional or business-unit technology stacks onto a single platform and seen it adopted, not only proposed or started it
Has led engineering across multiple countries and significantly separated time zones, ideally including both Europe and Asia Pacific
Has delivered a strategy that senior stakeholders actively disagreed about, and can describe how that disagreement was managed rather than avoided
CTO, VP Engineering or equivalent in a multi-entity business of comparable complexity, with experience of an internal platform that regional businesses consume and

jobs.title: Analog IC Design Engineer
jobs.description:
onsemi is seeking an Analog IC Designer to join its Core Analog IP Development Centre of Excellence in Cork, Ireland. You will design and develop power, clock, monitoring and reset IP for the Treo platform in BCD65 technology, including bandgap references, LDOs, DC–DC regulators, oscillators and PLLs.

Your day-to-day work will focus on transistor-level circuit design, simulation across process, voltage and temperature conditions, layout collaboration and post-layout verification. You will support silicon characterisation and debugging, document design results, and work with product teams to ensure IP meets performance and integration requirements and can be reused across the platform. You will also mentor junior engineers and contribute to delivering designs through validation and into mass production.
Responsibilities
Product Engagement and IP Roadmaps

Contribute to the development of power, clock, monitoring and reset IP in the Treo BCD65 platform.
Engage directly with product-line teams and stakeholders to understand product needs, operating conditions, integration constraints and future requirements.
Translate these needs into clear IP specifications and prioritised development roadmaps for the Core Analog teams, balancing immediate product commitments with longer-term platform requirements.
Evaluate circuit design trade-offs across performance, power, area, robustness, testability and integration complexity.
Champion reusable IP, configurable features and consistent interfaces that support adoption across multiple products while limiting unnecessary customisation.
Communicate design proposals, roadmap priorities and technical decisions clearly through design reviews, presentations and written documentation.

Analog Design and Production Delivery

Design and develop analog IP including bandgap references, low-dropout regulators (LDOs), DC–DC regulators, oscillators, phase-locked loops (PLLs), monitoring circuits and reset functions.
Own block development from specification through transistor-level design, simulation, layout guidance, verification and silicon characterisation.
Verify performance across process, voltage and temperature corners, including mismatch, noise, stability, start-up behaviour and relevant operating modes.
Work closely with layout engineers to address matching, parasitics, isolation, coupling and device reliability, and ensure post-layout performance meets specifications.
Collaborate with product integration, validation, test and product engineering teams to resolve issues and support successful transfer to mass production.
Create clear design documentation, integration guidance and characterisation reports that enable efficient IP reuse and maintenance.

Technical Leadership, Mentoring and AI Adoption

Mentor junior engineers in analog design fundamentals, simulation methodology, design reviews and silicon debug.
Provide technical guidance and constructive design feedback, sharing knowledge and strengthening engineering practices across the Core Analog teams.
Help identify and assess practical opportunities for AI-assisted analog design and layout, including design-space exploration, simulation automation, results analysis, documentation and layout assistance.
Apply sound engineering judgement when evaluating AI-generated outputs, retaining rigorous verification, traceability and protection of confidential design information.
Qualifications
A bachelor’s degree in electrical or electronic engineering, or a closely related discipline, with at least 8 years of relevant analog IC design experience; or a master’s degree in a relevant discipline with at least 4 years of relevant analog IC design experience.
Demonstrated hands-on design experience with bandgap references, LDOs, DC–DC regulators, oscillators and PLLs.
A proven track record of taking several products through the full development lifecycle to mass production, including silicon evaluation, debugging and production support.
Strong analog circuit fundamentals and practical expertise in transistor-level design, simulation, layout-dependent effects and post-layout verification.
The ability to assess product requirements and translate them into robust, reusable analog IP designs.
Experience engaging with product lines and translating competing product requirements into coherent IP specifications, development priorities and roadmaps.
Demonstrated experience mentoring junior engineers and providing technical guidance through design reviews.
Strong communication and presentation skills, with the ability to explain complex technical concepts, present trade-offs and build alignment across engineering teams and product stakeholders.
A solid understanding of how AI can contribute to analog design and layout, including practical use cases, limitations and the need for independent engineering verification.

Desirable Experience

Experience in BCD technologies, particularly BCD65, and analog IP development for mixed-signal platforms.
About Us
onsemi (Nasdaq: ON) is driving disruptive innovations to help build a better future. With a focus on automotive and industrial end-markets, the company is accelerating change in megatrends such as vehicle electrification and safety, sustainable energy grids, industrial automation, and 5G and cloud infrastructure. With a highly differentiated and innovative product portfolio, onsemi creates intelligent power and sensing technologies that solve the world’s most complex challenges and leads the way in creating a safer, cleaner, and smarter world.

https://www.onsemi.com/careers/career-benefits

Job summary

The Senior Validation Consultant is a hands-on, strategy-led technical role responsible for the computer system validation (CSV) of larger laboratory systems — including LIMS, the Lab Execution System (LES) built on LabVantage, and other laboratory systems — within the Quality workstream. The primary focus of this role is the validation strategy for systems incorporating artificial intelligence / machine-learning (AI/ML) components, ensuring these are validated for intended use in line with emerging regulatory expectations, including the draft EU GMP Annex 22 (Artificial Intelligence), Annex 11, GAMP 5 (Second Edition) and the ISPE GAMP Guide: Artificial Intelligence.

Alongside this AI focus, the consultant defines and owns the validation strategies and plans that govern how these larger systems are validated and maintained in a validated state. The consultant brings direct LIMS / LabVantage experience and sets the validation direction for AI-enabled applications while raising the bar of the broader validation framework.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Validation of Larger Laboratory Systems (LIMS and other lab systems) - Lead the computer system validation of larger laboratory systems — LIMS, LES/LabVantage, and other laboratory systems — across their lifecycle.
  • Provide senior CSV oversight for configuration of laboratory platforms to support QC workflows: sample login, testing assignments, instrument integration, specifications management, and results entry.
  • Ensure analytical methods, test plans, and specifications configured within these systems are validated and traceable to approved laboratory SOPs and pharmacopeial methods.
  • Ensure user roles, security permissions, electronic signatures, and audit trail settings are validated in compliance with 21 CFR Part 11 and EU Annex 11.
  • Oversee validation of interfaces between laboratory systems and SAP (QM), MES, instruments, and EDMS.

Validation Strategy & Planning (CSV) - This role centres on defining the validation strategies and plans that govern how larger laboratory systems are validated. The consultant will:

  • Define, author and own the overarching validation strategy and Validation Plans across LIMS, LES, MALDI-TOF, APQR and other laboratory systems.
  • Set the risk-based validation approach in line with the GAMP 5 (2nd Ed.) framework, ICH Q9(R1) quality risk management, 21 CFR Part 11, EU Annex 11, and data integrity / ALCOA+ principles.
  • Establish the structure and standards for the core validation deliverables — User Requirements Specification (URS), Functional Requirements Specification (FRS), Design Specification, Risk Assessment, Traceability Matrix, IQ/OQ/PQ approach, and Validation Summary Reports (VSR).
  • Define validation scope, acceptance strategy, deliverable set, and the leverage of supplier documentation for each system based on risk and criticality.
  • Define the strategy for periodic review, change-driven re-validation, and ongoing validated-state maintenance post go-live.
  • Define the approach to deviation handling, remediation, and evidence standards so validation packages are consistent, defensible and inspection-ready.

Key competencies:

  • Deep technical expertise in LIMS — comfortable in the system configuration layer, not just the user interface.
  • Strong validation-strategy capability: able to define validation approaches and plans for large, complex laboratory systems.
  • Validation mindset: meticulous, evidence-based documentation and zero tolerance for gaps in the validation package.
  • Strong scientific and risk-based acumen — understands the “why” behind analytical methods, laboratory workflows and AI model behaviour, not just the mechanics.
  • Ability to think strategically about emerging regulation (Annex 22) while executing hands-on validation work.
  • Clear, structured technical writing for validation strategies, plans, SOPs and specifications.
  • Collaborative, multidisciplinary approach — works effectively across QC lab teams, IT/data science, quality assurance, and vendors.
  • Self-directed and proactive; manages own workload and flags risks and roadblocks early rather than letting them escalate.

jobs.title: Analog IC Design Engineer
jobs.description:
onsemi is seeking an Analog IC Designer to join its Core Analog IP Development Centre of Excellence in Cork, Ireland. You will design and develop power, clock, monitoring and reset IP for the Treo platform in BCD65 technology, including bandgap references, LDOs, DC–DC regulators, oscillators and PLLs.

Your day-to-day work will focus on transistor-level circuit design, simulation across process, voltage and temperature conditions, layout collaboration and post-layout verification. You will support silicon characterisation and debugging, document design results, and work with product teams to ensure IP meets performance and integration requirements and can be reused across the platform. You will also mentor junior engineers and contribute to delivering designs through validation and into mass production.


  • Responsibilities

Product Engagement and IP Roadmaps

  • Contribute to the development of power, clock, monitoring and reset IP in the Treo BCD65 platform.
  • Engage directly with product-line teams and stakeholders to understand product needs, operating conditions, integration constraints and future requirements.
  • Translate these needs into clear IP specifications and prioritised development roadmaps for the Core Analog teams, balancing immediate product commitments with longer-term platform requirements.
  • Evaluate circuit design trade-offs across performance, power, area, robustness, testability and integration complexity.
  • Champion reusable IP, configurable features and consistent interfaces that support adoption across multiple products while limiting unnecessary customisation.
  • Communicate design proposals, roadmap priorities and technical decisions clearly through design reviews, presentations and written documentation.

Analog Design and Production Delivery

  • Design and develop analog IP including bandgap references, low-dropout regulators (LDOs), DC–DC regulators, oscillators, phase-locked loops (PLLs), monitoring circuits and reset functions.
  • Own block development from specification through transistor-level design, simulation, layout guidance, verification and silicon characterisation.
  • Verify performance across process, voltage and temperature corners, including mismatch, noise, stability, start-up behaviour and relevant operating modes.
  • Work closely with layout engineers to address matching, parasitics, isolation, coupling and device reliability, and ensure post-layout performance meets specifications.
  • Collaborate with product integration, validation, test and product engineering teams to resolve issues and support successful transfer to mass production.
  • Create clear design documentation, integration guidance and characterisation reports that enable efficient IP reuse and maintenance.

Technical Leadership, Mentoring and AI Adoption

  • Mentor junior engineers in analog design fundamentals, simulation methodology, design reviews and silicon debug.
  • Provide technical guidance and constructive design feedback, sharing knowledge and strengthening engineering practices across the Core Analog teams.
  • Help identify and assess practical opportunities for AI-assisted analog design and layout, including design-space exploration, simulation automation, results analysis, documentation and layout assistance.
  • Apply sound engineering judgement when evaluating AI-generated outputs, retaining rigorous verification, traceability and protection of confidential design information.

  • Qualifications

  • A bachelor’s degree in electrical or electronic engineering, or a closely related discipline, with at least 8 years of relevant analog IC design experience; or a master’s degree in a relevant discipline with at least 4 years of relevant analog IC design experience.
  • Demonstrated hands-on design experience with bandgap references, LDOs, DC–DC regulators, oscillators and PLLs.
  • A proven track record of taking several products through the full development lifecycle to mass production, including silicon evaluation, debugging and production support.
  • Strong analog circuit fundamentals and practical expertise in transistor-level design, simulation, layout-dependent effects and post-layout verification.
  • The ability to assess product requirements and translate them into robust, reusable analog IP designs.
  • Experience engaging with product lines and translating competing product requirements into coherent IP specifications, development priorities and roadmaps.
  • Demonstrated experience mentoring junior engineers and providing technical guidance through design reviews.
  • Strong communication and presentation skills, with the ability to explain complex technical concepts, present trade-offs and build alignment across engineering teams and product stakeholders.
  • A solid understanding of how AI can contribute to analog design and layout, including practical use cases, limitations and the need for independent engineering verification.

Desirable Experience

  • Experience in BCD technologies, particularly BCD65, and analog IP development for mixed-signal platforms.

jobs.title: Mixed Signal Verification Engineer
jobs.description:
onsemi is seeking a Mixed Signal Verification Engineer to join its Core Analog IP Development Centre of Excellence in Cork, Ireland. You will verify mixed-signal IP, complex systems-on-chip (SoCs) and digital-on-top subsystems supporting the Treo platform, including power, clock, monitoring and reset functions.

Your primary focus will be developing and executing verification plans and reusable environments that validate interactions between analog blocks and their controlling RTL/digital logic. You will combine analog/digital co-simulation with behavioural and real-number modelling to achieve appropriate accuracy, performance and coverage. Working closely with analog designers, digital designers and system architects, you will identify integration issues, debug cross-domain behaviour and provide clear evidence of verification closure. Hands-on experience using the latest mixed-signal verification tools and flows from major EDA vendors is essential.
Responsibilities
Mixed-Signal Verification Planning and Execution

Develop requirements-driven verification plans for mixed-signal IP, complex SoCs and digital-on-top subsystems, defining scenarios, checkers, coverage goals and completion criteria.
Build and maintain reusable SystemVerilog/UVM-based verification environments, integrating analog models and co-simulation configurations with controlling RTL/digital logic.
Verify analog/digital interactions including register programming, handshaking, status reporting, interrupts, calibration controls and feedback between analog functions and digital control logic.
Develop directed and constrained-random tests for operating modes, start-up, shutdown, reset, power and clock sequencing, fault conditions and recovery behaviour.
Implement assertions, scoreboards and functional coverage to check mixed-signal behaviour, track requirements and identify verification gaps.
Execute regressions, analyse failures, drive coverage closure and document verification results, residual risks and readiness for design release.

Analog/Digital Co-Simulation, Modelling and Debug

Configure and run mixed-signal co-simulations combining transistor-level or behavioural analog blocks with controlling RTL/digital logic at subsystem and SoC level.
Develop, integrate and validate Verilog-AMS and SystemVerilog real-number models (RNM), selecting abstraction levels that balance simulation accuracy, runtime and verification objectives.
Manage analog/digital boundary behaviour, including connect modules, signal disciplines, voltage thresholds, timing, tolerances and model initialisation.
Debug failures across analog waveforms, digital transactions and RTL control sequences; distinguish design defects from modelling, configuration and testbench issues.
Collaborate with analog and digital design teams to correlate models with circuit behaviour and verify power, clock, monitoring and reset functions across relevant operating conditions and process, voltage and temperature corners.
Use current-generation mixed-signal verification tools from major EDA vendors, optimise co-simulation configurations and maintain reproducible simulation and debug flows.

Collaboration, Automation and Methodology

Work with system architects, IP owners and integration teams to clarify requirements, identify cross-domain risks and agree verification responsibilities.
Participate in specification, design and verification reviews; communicate defects, coverage progress and technical trade-offs clearly.
Automate simulation setup, regression execution, results analysis and reporting using scripting and version-controlled workflows.
Improve reusable verification components, modelling practices and documentation, sharing practical knowledge across analog and digital engineering teams.
Qualifications
A bachelor’s or master’s degree in electrical or electronic engineering, computer engineering or a closely related discipline, with 4–8 years of relevant IC verification experience.
Demonstrated mixed-signal verification experience on complex SoCs or digital-on-top subsystems, including co-simulation of analog blocks with their controlling RTL/digital logic.
Hands-on experience using the latest mixed-signal verification tools and current-generation simulation, modelling and debug flows from major EDA vendors such as Cadence, Synopsys or Siemens EDA, with practical proficiency in at least one major-vendor tool suite.
Strong SystemVerilog and UVM skills, including reusable testbench development, constrained-random stimulus, assertions, scoreboards and functional coverage.
Practical experience with analog behavioural modelling and real-number modelling using Verilog-AMS and/or SystemVerilog RNM, including model validation and integration into mixed-signal environments.
A sound understanding of analog circuit behaviour and digital RTL, including power and clock control, reset sequencing, register interfaces and analog/digital boundary effects.
Experience translating specifications into verification plans, debugging cross-domain failures and driving regression and coverage closure.
Proficiency with Linux-based engineering environments, version control and scripting languages such as Python, Tcl or Perl for verification automation.
Strong analytical, communication and teamwork skills, with the ability to work independently on verification tasks and collaborate effectively across analog, digital and system teams.

Desirable Experience

Experience verifying automotive ICs or subsystems, with familiarity with automotive development processes, quality expectations and requirements traceability.
Functional safety experience, including familiarity with ISO 26262, safety requirements, fault injection, diagnostic mechanisms and verification of fault detection and safe-state behaviour.
Experience with power-management, clocking, monitoring or reset IP, including LDOs, DC–DC regulators, bandgap references, oscillators and PLLs in BCD or other mixed-signal technologies.

jobs.description:
onsemi is seeking a Mixed Signal Verification Engineer to join its Core Analog IP Development Centre of Excellence in Cork, Ireland. You will verify mixed-signal IP, complex systems-on-chip (SoCs) and digital-on-top subsystems supporting the Treo platform, including power, clock, monitoring and reset functions.

Your primary focus will be developing and executing verification plans and reusable environments that validate interactions between analog blocks and their controlling RTL/digital logic. You will combine analog/digital co-simulation with behavioural and real-number modelling to achieve appropriate accuracy, performance and coverage. Working closely with analog designers, digital designers and system architects, you will identify integration issues, debug cross-domain behaviour and provide clear evidence of verification closure. Hands-on experience using the latest mixed-signal verification tools and flows from major EDA vendors is essential.


  • Responsibilities

Mixed-Signal Verification Planning and Execution

  • Develop requirements-driven verification plans for mixed-signal IP, complex SoCs and digital-on-top subsystems, defining scenarios, checkers, coverage goals and completion criteria.
  • Build and maintain reusable SystemVerilog/UVM-based verification environments, integrating analog models and co-simulation configurations with controlling RTL/digital logic.
  • Verify analog/digital interactions including register programming, handshaking, status reporting, interrupts, calibration controls and feedback between analog functions and digital control logic.
  • Develop directed and constrained-random tests for operating modes, start-up, shutdown, reset, power and clock sequencing, fault conditions and recovery behaviour.
  • Implement assertions, scoreboards and functional coverage to check mixed-signal behaviour, track requirements and identify verification gaps.
  • Execute regressions, analyse failures, drive coverage closure and document verification results, residual risks and readiness for design release.

Analog/Digital Co-Simulation, Modelling and Debug

  • Configure and run mixed-signal co-simulations combining transistor-level or behavioural analog blocks with controlling RTL/digital logic at subsystem and SoC level.
  • Develop, integrate and validate Verilog-AMS and SystemVerilog real-number models (RNM), selecting abstraction levels that balance simulation accuracy, runtime and verification objectives.
  • Manage analog/digital boundary behaviour, including connect modules, signal disciplines, voltage thresholds, timing, tolerances and model initialisation.
  • Debug failures across analog waveforms, digital transactions and RTL control sequences; distinguish design defects from modelling, configuration and testbench issues.
  • Collaborate with analog and digital design teams to correlate models with circuit behaviour and verify power, clock, monitoring and reset functions across relevant operating conditions and process, voltage and temperature corners.
  • Use current-generation mixed-signal verification tools from major EDA vendors, optimise co-simulation configurations and maintain reproducible simulation and debug flows.

Collaboration, Automation and Methodology

  • Work with system architects, IP owners and integration teams to clarify requirements, identify cross-domain risks and agree verification responsibilities.

  • Strong SystemVerilog and UVM skills, including reusable testbench development, constrained-random stimulus, assertions, scoreboards and functional coverage.
  • Practical experience with analog behavioural modelling and real-number modelling using Verilog-AMS and/or SystemVerilog RNM, including model validation and integration into mixed-signal environments.

jobs.title: Mechanical Engineering AI Trainer
jobs.description:
Mechanical Engineering AI Trainer

*Remote | Contract / Project-Based | $40–$125 USD per hour*

Paro is seeking experienced Mechanical Engineering professionals for remote, project-based AI training opportunities. This work allows engineers to apply their real-world technical expertise to evaluate and improve how advanced AI models perform complex mechanical engineering tasks.

This is not a traditional mechanical engineering position. You’ll use your professional judgment to develop realistic engineering problems, review AI-generated work, identify technical errors and weaknesses, and evaluate responses against professional engineering standards.

What You’ll Do

* Develop challenging, realistic mechanical engineering tasks based on real-world professional workflows.
* Create supporting materials such as drawings, CAD models, load cases, material data, test data, and specifications.
* Evaluate AI-generated calculations, analyses, design reviews, and technical reports.
* Compare AI-generated solutions and identify where reasoning or technical execution falls short.
* Develop worked solutions, acceptance criteria, and detailed grading standards.
* Identify errors involving boundary conditions, units, tolerances, interference, factors of safety, materials, failure modes, and other engineering considerations.
* Contribute across areas such as design, analysis, manufacturing, testing, and validation.

What We’re Looking For

* 2+ years of professional mechanical engineering experience preferred.
* Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering or a related field completed or in progress.
* Hands-on experience in one or more areas such as:
* Mechanical design and CAD
* Structures and materials
* Stress, fatigue, deflection, or failure analysis
* Thermal and fluid systems
* HVAC, pumps, or piping
* Dynamics, vibration, or rotating machinery
* Manufacturing, DFM/DFA, GD&T, or tolerance analysis
* Experience with relevant engineering tools such as SolidWorks, Fusion 360, Onshape, Creo, NX, CATIA, Inventor, FEA/CFD tools, MATLAB, or Python.
* Strong engineering fundamentals and attention to detail.
* Ability to clearly explain technical reasoning and identify why a proposed solution is incorrect.
* Current or recent hands-on engineering experience strongly preferred.
* Professional-level written and spoken English.
* Familiarity with AI/LLM tools such as ChatGPT or Claude.
* Ability to work independently in a self-directed remote environment.

Engagement Details

*Pay:* $40 – $125 USD per hour
*Work Arrangement:* Fully remote, contract/project-based
*Availability:* Approximately 10+ hours per week preferred; additional hours may be available
*Location:* United States, Canada, or the United Kingdom
*Schedule:* Flexible

Assessment & Onboarding

Qualified applicants will be invited to complete an approximately 2–4 hour unpaid skills assessment designed to evaluate technical expertise, attention to detail, and the ability to assess AI-generated work against professional standards.

Assessment submissions must represent the applicant’s own work and may not be completed using AI tools.

Candidates who successfully complete the assessment may become eligible for ongoing paid AI training projects based on expertise, performance, and available work.

If you have hands-on mechanical engineering experience and are interested in applying your expertise to the development of advanced AI systems, we encourage you to apply.

Expected hours: No less than 10.0 per week



Application question(s):
* Do you have general familiarity with AI/LLM tools such as ChatGPT or Claude?
* Are you willing to complete an unpaid, independent technical assessment lasting approximately 2–4 hours without using AI assistance?

Experience:
* hand on mechanical engineering: 1 year (preferred)

Work Location: Remote

jobs.title: Manufacturing Engineer – Digitization, Automation & Lean Transformation
jobs.description:
We are seeking hands-on Advanced Manufacturing Engineers to drive operational transformation across Vertiv's EMEA manufacturing plants.

Combining Industrial Engineering, Lean, digitization and automation, the role will focus on unlocking capacity, improving productivity, stabilising production ramp-ups and delivering measurable business benefits.

This is a hands-on role for someone who enjoys working on the shopfloor, solving problems and turning improvement opportunities into sustainable results.

Location & Travel

The role will initially support 2–3 assigned EMEA manufacturing plants and will require approximately 50% travel across EMEA.

Why Join Us?

  • Play a key role in transforming a rapidly growing EMEA manufacturing network.
  • Work directly with plant teams and senior leadership to deliver tangible operational improvements.
  • Drive projects across Lean, automation, digitization and Industrial Engineering.
  • Have the autonomy to develop and implement solutions that make a measurable difference.
  • Build experience across multiple manufacturing sites and develop your career towards future operational leadership opportunities.

Key Responsibilities

Industrial Engineering & Lean Transformation

  • Lead shopfloor improvement initiatives, including Kaizen, VSM, 5S, standard work and visual management.
  • Drive line balancing, time studies, capacity analysis, labour optimisation, layout and material-flow improvements.
  • Identify bottlenecks, reduce waste and improve productivity, quality and lead times.
  • Support the deployment of Lean Operating Systems and daily management routines across manufacturing sites.

Digitization & Automation

  • Identify opportunities to improve manufacturing through MES, digital work instructions, production dashboards, data acquisition and connected equipment.
  • Identify and support automation opportunities involving robotics, cobots, automated material handling and test systems.
  • Support automation and digitisation projects from business case and concept through implementation, commissioning and handover.
  • Use operational data to improve visibility, decision-making and manufacturing performance.

Ramp-Up & Operational Performance

  • Support new product introductions, production transfers and manufacturing ramp-ups.
  • Drive production readiness, bottleneck removal and process stabilisation.
  • Develop standard work, SOPs and training materials to ensure sustainable process improvements.
  • Track project benefits and work with Finance to validate improvements in capacity, productivity, cost and quality.

Coaching & Continuous Improvement

  • Work closely with operators, supervisors, engineers and plant leadership to implement improvements.
  • Coach and develop plant teams in Lean tools, problem-solving and continuous improvement methodologies.
  • Share best practices and develop standard solutions that can be replicated across the EMEA network.

What Success Looks Like

During the first 12 months, you will be expected to:

  • Complete Industrial Engineering and digital maturity assessments across assigned plants.
  • Deliver measurable improvements in productivity, capacity, quality, cost or lead time.
  • Implement and sustain key Lean management practices.
  • Deliver or develop business cases for digital and automation projects.
  • Establish repeatable improvement standards that can be deployed across other EMEA sites.

Required Qualifications & Experience

  • Bachelor's degree in Manufacturing Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering or a related discipline.
  • 5+ years' experience in Manufacturing Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Operational Excellence, Lean or manufacturing process improvement.
  • Proven experience delivering measurable manufacturing improvements.
  • Strong knowledge of Lean methodologies, including 5S, Kaizen, VSM, standard work, line balancing and problem-solving.
  • Experience in at least two of the following: MES, digital manufacturing, automation/robotics, data acquisition, capacity modelling or Lean transformation.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to translate operational improvements into measurable business benefits.
  • Fluent English and willingness to travel across EMEA.

Preferred Experience

  • Lean Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt, or equivalent experience.
  • Experience in multi-site manufacturing, automotive, high-mix/high-volume manufacturing, greenfield projects or operational transformation.
  • Knowledge of PLC/SCADA, industrial networking, robotics, TPM, simulation or advanced analytics.
  • Experience developing business cases and working with Finance to validate project benefits.

As a Process Development Engineer within our Manufacturing Sciences & Analytical Technology (MSAT) team in Bray, you will provide process engineering expertise and leadership supporting small molecule drug products.

You will play a key role in New Product Introduction (NPI), technical transfers, material qualification, process development and continuous improvement across drug product manufacturing and finished product packaging for our Oral Solid Dosage site.

jobs.title: Rigger / Forklift Driver / Gantry Crane Operator
jobs.description:
Cental is a global supplier of fully designed, engineered, built and integrated modular and skid-mounted solutions for the Data Centre, Utilities, Life Sciences, and Oil & Gas markets. From our headquarters in Carlow, Ireland, we deliver comprehensive solutions for clients worldwide.

Our people are the foundation of our success. With three manufacturing facilities and a talented team of engineers, designers, project managers, and tradespeople, our team manages every detail, ensuring seamless delivery from initial design to final installation. We value teamwork, respect, and continuous improvement, creating a collaborative, innovative environment where everyone can reach their potential.

We also believe in celebrating achievements and recognising effort. From monthly quality and safety initiatives for breakfast treats and local tool vouchers, to company breakfasts, staff BBQs, and occasional outings, we bring people together to enjoy achievements and strengthen our team spirit.

Growth and learning are central to Cental. Whether you’re joining as an apprentice, graduate, or experienced professional, we provide training and development opportunities to help you build a rewarding, long-term career.

If you’re passionate about excellence, innovation, and teamwork, join us and be part of a company that’s engineering solutions and building futures.


Position: Rigger / Forklift Driver / Gantry Crane Operator (Evening shift)

Location: Carlow

Working Hours: 4:30pm – 1:30am


Role purpose

We are looking for a reliable, safety-conscious and experienced Rigger / Forklift Driver / Gantry Crane Operator to join our evening tshift manufacturing team. The successful candidate will support the safe movement, lifting and positioning of steel components, materials and completed modules throughout the factory. Working closely with the evening shift supervisors and production teams, the role will help ensure operations run safely and efficiently.


Key responsibilities

  • Safely operate forklifts and overhead gantry cranes in a busy manufacturing environment.
  • Carry out rigging, slinging and lifting operations involving large steel structures and components.
  • Safely move, lift and position large steel modules and assemblies.
  • Assist with loading and unloading deliveries and organising materials around the factory.
  • Ensure materials and components are delivered to the correct production areas when required.
  • Coordinate with fabrication, fitout and finishing teams to support production requirements.
  • Complete daily equipment checks and report defects or maintenance requirements.
  • Ensure lifting equipment, chains, slings and accessories are inspected and used correctly.
  • Maintain a clean, organised and safe working environment.
  • Follow company health and safety procedures and safe systems of work.


Essential Requirements

  • Previous experience operating forklifts in an industrial or manufacturing environment.
  • Experience operating overhead gantry cranes.
  • Previous experience in rigging, slinging and lifting operations.
  • Relevant and valid forklift and crane operating certificates.
  • Good understanding of lifting safety and load management.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
  • Strong awareness of health and safety procedures.
  • Reliable, punctual and hardworking attitude.


Desirable Experience

  • Experience working with large steel structures or modular buildings.
  • Experience moving heavy and oversized loads.
  • Previous experience in steel fabrication or manufacturing.
  • Knowledge of lifting plans and safe load-handling procedures
