jobs.title: Design Technician
jobs.description:
Overview:

Vision Built a Sisk Company, is a leading offsite construction company delivering high-quality modular and panelised building solutions. Our team combines innovation with practical construction expertise to deliver projects safely, efficiently and to the highest standards.

The Design Technican is a key engineering role within the Building Envelopes and Engineering Services teams. Reporting to a Design Engineer, this role provides support in design, technical assessment and project coordination while developing practical experience and professional engineering skills. The position offers exposure to multi-disciplinary construction projects, design processes and emerging technologies in building envelopes.

Responsibilities:

Design & Techical Support

Assist in preparation of technical drawings, 2D and 3D models and supporting documentation.

Support the review and checking of design information and details for compliance with project specifications and standards.

Assist with material research, product specification and minor design solutions.

Collaborate with senior engineers and technical support staff to ensure design quality and constructability.

Assist in the resolution of minor technical queries from site or project teams.

Project coordination and documentation

Maintain accurate records of drawings, specifications and project correspondence.

Support the assembly and organisation of technical information for project teams.

Assist in coordinating information with contractors, suppliers and design teams.

Support site visits and inspections to gain practical experience and understanding of construction methods.

Development & Continuous Learning

Participate in structured training and CPD programmes to develop technical expertise.

Gain knowledge of building envelope systems, construction standards and design regulations.

Engage with mentoring opportunities to build skills in design, technical assessment and project delivery.

Support capturing lessons learned and best practice for use across projects.

Experience:

Essential

Recent graduate in Civil, Structural, Architectural or related Engineering discipline.
Basic knowledge of building envelope systems and construction principles.
Good organisation, attention to detail and ability to manage multiple tasks under guidance.
Strong communication and teamwork skills, with willingness to learn from senior engineers.
Motivated, proactive and committed to building a career in construction engineering.

Desirable

Familiarity with CAD or BIM software (AutoCAD, Revit) is desirable.
Qualifications:

Essential

Bachelor's degree in civil engineering, Structural Engineering, Architecture or a related discipline.
Commitment to professional development and gaining practical experience in building envelopes and engineering services.

Desirable

Eligibility for graduate membership of a relevant professional body
Additional Information:
Competitive salary
26 days annual leave plus additional company days
Pension and benefits
Unlimited learning and development opportunities
Much more

Our People and Recruitment Commitment

At Sisk Group our people are at the heart of our success. We offer the chance to work with purpose, build a career with no limits and be part of a great team.

All vacancies are managed directly by our Internal Recruitment Team. Unsolicited contact or speculative CVs from unapproved agencies will not be accepted and no introductory fees will apply.

We are an equal opportunities employer. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates regardless of gender, race, ethnicity, disability, age, sexual orientation, religion or any other protected characteristic.

Reasonable adjustments are available during the recruitment process

We know the confidence gap and imposter phenomenon can stop talented candidates applying. You do not need to meet every criterion – your skills and potential matter. Don’t hold back we want to hear from you

All recruitment materials comply with legal and regulatory requirements including the EU Pay Transparency Directive and the Equality Acts UK and Ireland

jobs.title: Customer Success Agent - 9 Month Fixed Term Contract
jobs.description:
About Us

Lanas is igniting healthcare innovation. For nearly three decades, we have connected GPs, pharmacists, specialists, surgeons, and other healthcare professionals with the best technology possible, from trusted everyday systems to new innovative tools that add real value for our customers.

Our technology is used by millions of clinical users in over twenty countries. From core clinical workflows to AI-driven innovation, our products help reduce admin, improve access, drive efficiencies, and support safer, more connected care.

Position:

The Opportunity

We have an exciting opportunity for a Customer Success Agent to join our team on a 9-month fixed-term contract, supporting our GP software systems, HealthOne and HPM.

Reporting to the Customer Success Manager, you will troubleshoot technical issues, resolve customer queries and help customers get the most from our software. You will work with our Development, Hardware Support and Field Engineering teams to maintain service standards and deliver a positive customer experience.

What You'll Own

• Manage customer queries from initial contact through to resolution, ensuring issues are logged, prioritised and followed up.

• Provide technical support for our GP software over the phone and through remote access.

• Investigate hardware and connectivity issues, including PCs, printers, scanners and networks.

• Work closely with colleagues across Customer Success, Development and Hardware Support to resolve complex issues.

• Support testing of software updates and new releases, reporting potential issues to the Development Team.

• Coordinate with Field Engineers when issues require on-site support.

• Keep customers informed throughout the resolution process, maintaining clear and professional communication.

• Identify ways to improve the customer experience and highlight relevant additional software functionality or modules.

Requirements:

What We're Looking For

• Previous experience in customer support, IT support or a technical role is an advantage; graduates with strong technical aptitude are welcome.

• Good IT skills, including familiarity with Windows environments and basic troubleshooting.

• An understanding of databases, particularly SQL, would be beneficial.

• Strong problem-solving skills and a methodical approach to investigating issues.

• Excellent communication skills and a professional, customer-focused telephone manner.

• Ability to manage multiple queries, prioritise work and take ownership through to resolution.

• A positive, flexible attitude, willingness to learn and commitment to working well with colleagues.

Other information:

What We Offer

At Lanas, you can expect challenging projects, real ownership, continuous learning and professional development, and the opportunity to contribute to technology that directly improves patient care. Our benefits include:

• Company matched pension scheme.

• 22 days annual leave, increasing annually up to 26 days (pro rata for the contract duration).

• Working abroad opportunities – up to 20 working days per year, subject to eligibility.

• Flexible working.

• 2 paid CSR Volunteering/Charity Days and 1 Wellbeing Day per year, subject to eligibility.

• Enhanced maternity and paternity benefits, subject to eligibility.

• Employee Assistance Programme, wellbeing supports and webinars.

• Annual leave purchase scheme, subject to eligibility.

Lanas is an equal opportunities employer.

jobs.title: Structural Simulation Engineer
jobs.description: ResponsibilitiesThe Structural Simulation Engineer will support the structural design and development of Liebherr container cranes through Finite Element Analysis (FEA) and simulation activities. The primary focus of the role will be the assessment and optimisation of crane components and structures using Ansys, including both static and transient/dynamic simulations.The successful candidate will also have the opportunity to develop skills in multi-body dynamics modelling and control system simulation using MATLAB/Simulink and Simscape Multibody, working closely with structural, automation and control engineering teams.Key Elements of the Role:Responsibilities shall include, but are not limited to the following: Perform structural analysis of crane components and assemblies using the Ansys suite of software. Conduct static, nonlinear and transient dynamic simulations to support product development and verifi-cation activities. Evaluate structural strength, stiffness, fatigue performance and dynamic behaviour of crane structures and mechanical systems. Prepare, review and interpret finite element models, simulation results and technical reports. Support the development and validation of simulation methodologies and best practices within the de-partment. Collaborate with design engineers to improve component and system performance through simulation-led design. Develop and maintain simplified and detailed simulation models for complex mechanical systems. Support the modelling of crane mechanisms using MATLAB/Simulink and Simscape Multibody. Collaborate with automation and control engineers to understand the interaction between mechanical systems and control algorithms. Contribute to the development of simulation tools, automation workflows and engineering processes us-ing Python, Ansys APDL and VBA. Work with CAD models generated in PTC Creo and prepare geometry for simulation activities. Constructively collaborate with the simulation engineering community within MCC and the broader Liebherr Group.Qualifications, Requirements & Experience The successful candidate will hold a third-level qualification in an engineering discipline – preferably L9 or L10. A strong interest in engineering simulation, numerical methods and analytical problem solving. Knowledge of Finite Element Analysis principles is essential. Experience with Ansys Mechanical or similar FEA software is desirable. Knowledge of structural mechanics, strength of materials and dynamics. Exposure to transient or dynamic analysis methods would be advantageous. Experience with MATLAB/Simulink, Simscape Multibody or similar modelling environments would be advantageous. Experience with CAD software, particularly PTC Creo, would be beneficial. Basic programming skills are desirable, with Python considered a significant advantage. Demonstrated aptitude for learning new software tools, simulation techniques and engineering methodologies.What We Offer Competitive Salary Paid overtime End of Year Bonus Pension Scheme Service Pay Early finish on a Friday 21 days annual leave + Length of service days Company Fixed Days Subsidised canteen Sports and Social Club Retailer Discounts Life Assurance Refer a friend Scheme Maternity Pay Educational assistance Career Progression OpportunitiesPlease note, CV's will not be accepted directly by email.We do not require the assistance of recruitment agencies for this role.#LCCHave we awoken your interest? Then we look forward to receiving your online application. If you have any questions, please contact Jennifer Connolly.One Passion. Many Opportunities.The CompanyLiebherr Container Cranes Ltd. is one of the world's leading manufacturers of ship to shore cranes, rail mounted gantry cranes and rubber tyre gantry cranes. From its base in Killarney, Ireland, the company designs, builds and exports container cranes worldwide. Founded in 1958 as the first Liebherr factory outside of Germany, today, container cranes manufactured by Liebherr in Ireland are renowned for their quality, longevity and productivity.LocationLiebherr Container Cranes Ltd.KillarneyIreland (IE)ContactJennifer Connollyjennifer.connolly@liebherr.com

jobs.title: NPI Quality Engineer III
jobs.description:
By living according to a common set of values, we create a culture that unifies, embraces the uniqueness we all bring to the company, and positions Integer for long-term success.

At Integer, our values are embedded in everything we do.

Customer

We focus on our customers’ success

Innovation

We create better solutions

Collaboration

We create success together

Inclusion

We always interact with others respectfully

Candor

We are open and honest with one another

Integrity

We do the right things and do things right

What you’ll do in this role:

The primary purpose of this job is to apply intensive and diversified knowledge of engineering principles and practices to New Product Introduction (NPI) projects. The following are expectations:

• Ensure Integer internal and external customer expectations are met or exceeded. You Identify and evaluate procedures to ensure the production of quality product.

• Develop new and unique approaches to complex problems and can advance technology beyond previous achieved levels.

• Apply engineering concepts to resolve acute or chronic problems.

• Conduct studies to understand capability for process and/or measurement systems. Provides management with technical guidance as required.

• Identify and develop appropriate documentation for process improvement and project implementation.

• Maintain liaison with individuals and units within or outside the organization with responsibility for acting independently on technical matters pertaining to their field.

• You adhere to Integer’s Values and all safety, environmental, security and quality requirements including, but not limited to: Quality Management Systems (QMS), Safety, Environmental and Security Management Systems, U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) regulations, company policies and operating procedures, and other regulatory requirements.

NPI Support:

• You will support regulatory and agency inspections, audits, investigations, and inquiries regarding the control and assessment of product design and manufacturing quality.

• You will develop new test methods including design and manufacture of new tooling, fixtures, and templates.

• Carry out testing and validation of new test methods including gage R&R studies and statistical analysis of data through software packages such as Minitab.

• Update test method procedures and process standard operating procedures as required.

• Provide technical input into root cause analysis. Generate investigation reports within KPI metrics and timelines and route for approval. Participate and provide technical input on cross functional NPI team reviews.

• You will review procedures, protocols, reports, and other documents related to test method development, process testing and process validation which may be associated with new product introduction.

• Lead a Cross Functional Project Team, providing support and expertise for NPI. Participate and provide technical input in line with the product development process (PDP) and associated procedures.

• Ensure compliance at all stages of product development process (PDP).

• Support planning execution of risk management activities per ISO14971.

• Carry out periodic reviews of internal and external standards and identify potential gaps which require action.

• You will lead continuous improvement projects.

• You will assist with product transfers.

• You will perform work on technical projects where you will follow Integer’s standard quality management and production system methodologies to investigate opportunities for product and process improvements.

• You are expected to collaborate with others in the exchange of information, ask questions and regularly check for understanding in support of your development as an engineer.

Create Test Methods:

• You will lead the generation and completion of protocols and reports for test method validations.

• You will interface with Manufacturing Engineers to review processes for new products and coordinate process validations and capability studies. Recommends process monitoring devices where applicable.

• You will develop various inspection techniques and procedures to ensure product integrity to design specifications. Responsible for the writing, approval and implementation of Incoming, In-Process and Final Inspection procedures.

Support Non-Conforming Material Process:

• You will ensure that the disposition of non-conforming materials meets all necessary procedures and assure adequacy of corrective actions to prevent re-occurrence.

• You will participate in plant CAPA activities, including analysis of data and trends in complaints, supplier quality, nonconforming material, training effectiveness, and root causes analysis.

• You will apply standard data analysis practices and observe products and processes to establish root cause for product and process failures or to support the justification for improvements to products and processes.

Support Site Quality Activities:

• You will support internal quality audit activities, as applicable. • You embed Quality– “I own Quality.” You are a standard bearer for Quality in everything we do at Integer, by assuring adherence to our Quality Management System (QMS), supporting to corrective and preventive actions investigation and implementation, and contributing to the successful attainment of our quality KPI’s and journey to 5 Sigma.

• You may perform other duties as needed and as directed by your line of supervision.

Support Integer’s Manufacturing Excellence and Market Focused Innovation Strategies:

• Strategy Alignment through Site Hoshin Plans, Quality Plans, Validation master plans, associated quality improvement imperatives, and regular updates to QA RA weekly and monthly metrics, supporting the walk to 5 sigma.

• Leadership of Sustained Change ensuring customer change notifications are initiated and completed, as necessary, and supporting continuous improvement activities as required.

jobs.title: Infrastructure & Engineering Graduate Pathways
jobs.description: Job DescriptionAs a daa Infrastructure Graduate, you will help deliver the infrastructure that keeps Ireland connected to the world. From expanding airfields and terminals to delivering major civil engineering and sustainability projects, you will contribute to some of Ireland's most significant infrastructure developments across Dublin and Cork Airports. Working in a live operational environment, you will gain exposure to complex projects that support future growth, enhance connectivity, and improve the passenger experience.Graduates will join the Early Careers Community, a network of interns, apprentices, and second-year graduates, offering opportunities to learn, collaborate, and build professional connections across the business.Over this two-year fixed-term contract, you'll work within our Infrastructure team, contributing to major projects across Dublin and Cork Airports, including airfield and terminal expansions, civil engineering works, transport infrastructure, and sustainability initiatives.Whether you are contributing to airfield developments, terminal expansions, transport infrastructure, or sustainability initiatives, you will play a meaningful role in projects that have a lasting impact. If you are passionate about engineering, innovation, and creating infrastructure that connects people and businesses around the world, the daa Infrastructure Graduate role offers the perfect foundation for an exciting and rewarding career.ResponsibilitiesAs a daa Infrastructure Graduate, you will continue to build expertise within your specialism, gaining hands-on experience in areas which may include project delivery, strategy, advisory services, contracts, programme controls, governance, health and safety, quality assurance, and technical services. Working in a live operational aviation environment, you will collaborate with consultants, contractors, and stakeholders across the business, contributing to capital projects that are shaping the future of Ireland's aviation infrastructure.Areas You May Gain Exposure IncludesCivil Airfield Development - Contributing to major airfield infrastructure projects, including Ireland's first airport runway underpass, while developing your technical and problem-solving skills on complex engineering challenges.Piers & Terminal Development - Supporting the design and delivery of terminal and pier developments that enhance capacity and create a world-class passenger experience.Access & Connectivity Improvements - Working alongside Planning and Strategy teams on projects that improve airport accessibility, strengthen connectivity, and support long-term growth.Sustainability & Safety - Helping ensure safety and sustainability are embedded in every stage of infrastructure development, supporting daa's environmental ambitions and future-ready infrastructure goals.QualificationsDo you have what it takes? RoleWe’re looking for ambitious graduates ready to shape the future of infrastructure. To succeed in these entry level graduate roles, you should:Hold (or be expecting) a 2.1 degree or higher in Civil/Mechanical or Electrical Engineering, Construction Management, Architecture, Quantity Surveying, or a related Construction discipline.Demonstrate a strong understanding of engineering, construction, or infrastructure principles gained through your studies or project work.Bring strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to evaluate information and make sound decisions.Be naturally curious and motivated, with a desire to learn, develop, and take on new challenges.Demonstrate adaptability, with the ability to thrive in a dynamic and evolving environments.Show an innovative mindset, seeking opportunities to improve processes, challenge conventional thinking, and solve problems creatively.Exhibit learning agility, embracing feedback, and continuously developing new skills and capabilities.Be strong collaborators, building effective relationships and working successfully across teams and stakeholders to achieve shared goals.Align with daa's values and purpose, sharing our commitment to enabling business, connecting lives, and building a sustainable future.What We Are Offering You?As a daa Infrastructure Graduate, you’ll enjoy a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your growth, reward your impact, and help you thrive - professionally and personally. From global exposure to wellbeing perks, this programme is your launchpad to a standout career in aviation infrastructure.Programme Benefits IncludeCompetitive salary with a performance-related bonus to reward your impactA structured development pathway, including a 12-week Engineers Ireland-accredited Airport Planning & Design course, alongside expert-led knowledge-sharing sessions throughout the year.Exposure to major infrastructure and capital projects, giving you the opportunity to contribute to projects of varying scale, complexity, and strategic importance.Hands-on experience with industry-leading technologies, including BIM, GIS and cloud-based project delivery platforms used across large-scale infrastructure programmes.The opportunity to build technical expertise in civil and construction engineering, project planning, design coordination, and site delivery.A strong foundation for professional accreditation, supported by experienced mentors, continuous learning opportunities, and real-world project experience.#IND

jobs.title: Experienced Analog IC Designer
jobs.description:
onsemi is seeking an experienced Analog IC Designer to join its Core Analog IP Development Centre of Excellence in Cork, Ireland. You will develop power, clock, monitoring and reset IP for the Treo platform in BCD65 technology, combining hands-on circuit design with substantial architecture involvement and cross-product-line technical engagement.

This role extends well beyond individual block delivery. You will help shape platform-level analog IP architectures, translate product-line requirements into actionable IP roadmaps for the Core Analog teams, and champion IP reuse across the platform. You will also mentor junior engineers and guide designs from concept and specification through silicon validation and mass production.


  • Responsibilities

Architecture, Product Engagement and IP Roadmaps

  • Play a leading technical role in defining architectures for power, clock, monitoring and reset IP in the Treo BCD65 platform.
  • Engage directly with product-line architects, design teams and stakeholders to understand product needs, operating conditions, integration constraints and future requirements.
  • Translate these needs into clear IP specifications and prioritised development roadmaps for the Core Analog teams, balancing immediate product commitments with longer-term platform requirements.
  • Drive architecture trade-offs across performance, power, area, robustness, testability and integration complexity.
  • Champion reusable IP architectures, configurable features and consistent interfaces that support adoption across multiple products while limiting unnecessary customisation.
  • Communicate architecture proposals, roadmap priorities and technical decisions clearly through design reviews, presentations and written documentation.

Analog Design and Production Delivery

  • Design and develop analog IP including bandgap references, low-dropout regulators (LDOs), DC–DC regulators, oscillators, phase-locked loops (PLLs), monitoring circuits and reset functions.
  • Own block development from specification and circuit architecture through transistor-level design, simulation, layout guidance, verification and silicon characterisation.
  • Verify performance across process, voltage and temperature corners, including mismatch, noise, stability, start-up behaviour and relevant operating modes.
  • Work closely with layout engineers to address matching, parasitics, isolation, coupling and device reliability, and ensure post-layout performance meets specifications.
  • Collaborate with product integration, validation, test and product engineering teams to resolve issues and support successful transfer to mass production.
  • Create clear design documentation, integration guidance and characterisation reports that enable efficient IP reuse and maintenance.

Technical Leadership, Mentoring and AI Adoption

  • Mentor junior engineers in analog design fundamentals, architecture evaluation, simulation methodology, design reviews and silicon debug.
  • Provide technical guidance and constructive design feedback, sharing knowledge and strengthening engineering practices across the Core Analog teams.
  • Help identify and assess practical opportunities for AI-assisted analog design and layout, including design-space exploration, simulation automation, results analysis, documentation and layout assistance.
  • Apply sound engineering judgement when evaluating AI-generated outputs, retaining rigorous verification, traceability and protection of confidential design information.

  • Qualifications

  • A bachelor’s degree in electrical or electronic engineering, or a closely related discipline, with at least 15 years of relevant analog IC design experience; or a master’s degree in a relevant discipline with at least 11 years of relevant analog IC design experience.
  • Demonstrated hands-on design experience with bandgap references, LDOs, DC–DC regulators, oscillators and PLLs.
  • A proven track record of taking several products through the full development lifecycle to mass production, including silicon evaluation, debugging and production support.
  • Strong analog circuit fundamentals and practical expertise in transistor-level design, simulation, layout-dependent effects and post-layout verification.
  • Substantial architecture experience, with the ability to assess system-level requirements and translate them into robust, reusable analog IP solutions.
  • Experience engaging with product lines and translating competing product requirements into coherent IP specifications, development priorities and roadmaps.
  • Demonstrated experience mentoring junior engineers and providing technical leadership through design and architecture reviews.
  • Strong communication and presentation skills, with the ability to explain complex technical concepts, present trade-offs and build alignment across engineering teams and product stakeholders.
  • A solid understanding of how AI can contribute to analog design and layout, including practical use cases, limitations and the need for independent engineering verification.

Desirable Experience

  • Experience in BCD technologies, particularly BCD65, and analog IP development for mixed-signal platforms.
  • Experience with supply and voltage monitoring, power-on reset, brownout detection and power or clock sequencing.
  • Experience defining reusable IP portfolios, configuration strategies and integration requirements across multiple product families.
  • Practical experience with scripting, design-flow automation or evaluation of AI-assisted engineering tools.

jobs.title: Ombudsman for Children
jobs.description: Job title: Ombudsman for ChildrenEmployer: Office of the Ombudsman for Children Location: DublinClosing Date: 3pm, Thursday, 26 November 2026Salary: €159,524Overview:The Ombudsman for Children will be appointed under the Ombudsman for Children Act, 2002. The Act provides that the Ombudsman for Children is independent in the performance of his or her functions and is accountable to the Oireachtas. The appointment of the Ombudsman for Children is made by the President of Ireland. The primary objective of the Ombudsman for Children is to promote and safeguard the rights and welfare of children. Information on the work performed by the Ombudsman for Children, the main issues that have arisen, various publications including annual reports and the Ombudsman for Children Act, 2002 can be obtained on the website of the Ombudsman for Children http://www.oco.ie/.The first Ombudsman for Children was appointed in December 2003 and the office of the Ombudsman for Children was established in 2004. The 2002 Act was amended in part by the Ombudsman (Amendment) Act 2012. The 2012 Act relates in the main to the Office of the Ombudsman, rather than the Ombudsman for Children. However, the remit of both has been significantly expanded with effect from 1st May 2013. The bodies within the remit of each Ombudsman and the process for changes to their remits have been largely aligned.The OCO is one of the national public authorities with obligations under EU law protecting fundamental rights, including the right to non-discrimination, in relation to certain high-risk uses of AI systems.The Ombudsman for Children is also an ex-officio member of the Advisory Board outlined in Part 14, Chapter 4 of the International Protection Act 2026, relating to the governance and accountability of the Chief Inspector of Asylum Border Procedures and which consults with, guides and advises same. Functions:The main functions of the Ombudsman for Children are: To promote the rights and welfare of children, including:giving advice to the Government on how to develop policies and services for children, encouraging public bodies, schools and voluntary hospitals to have policies and practices that respect children's rights, collecting and sharing information about children's rights and welfare, telling the public (including children and young people) about children's rights and welfare issues and explaining how children's rights and the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child can be better respected and protected,making people (including the Government) aware of children's rights issues that children themselves are concerned about, sharing information and ideas with the Ombudsman for Children in other countries,creating ways to consult regularly with groups of children; To undertake, promote or publish research relating to children's rights and welfare; To monitor, review and advise on legislation, including: giving advice on how any proposed legislation will affect children; looking at laws relating to children's rights and welfare and how they work; looking at the Ombudsman for Children Act from time to time and making suggestions on whether parts of it should be changed; To examine and investigate complaints made by, or on behalf of, children. Following investigation, the Ombudsman will, where appropriate, issue recommendations to the public body concerned to improve its processes and procedures for dealing with children; To report annually on the operation of the Office; To attend before Oireachtas Committees; and To manage the administration of the Office of the Ombudsman for Children and associated resources.The closing date for receipt of completed applications is 3pm on Thursday, 26 November, 2026.We are committed to a policy of equal opportunity and encourage applications under all nine grounds of the Employment Equality Act.

Your Role: Qualified Person

As Qualified Person, you will oversee the technical review and certification of veterinary medicinal product batches released for the European market. Based in Elanco’s Dublin office, you will also manage the quality system for the Elanco Ireland Marketing Authorisation Holder and Importer entity, ensuring compliance with applicable pharmaceutical regulations, European Union Good Manufacturing Practice and Good Distribution Practice requirements.

Your Responsibilities:
Conduct technical reviews and certify European finished-product batches in accordance with Regulation 2019/6, Regulation (EU) 2025/2091 and applicable EU Good Manufacturing Practice requirements, including Articles 39 and 40.
Manage quality documentation and act as the primary contact for the European Manufacturing and Quality organisation regarding European batch releases, service-quality indicators, deadlines and follow-up actions.
Assess critical deviations with relevant stakeholders and support recall decisions, including participation in management notification processes and product-related governance meetings.
Maintain and improve the Elanco Ireland quality system by preparing and approving procedures, work instructions, site master file content, Qualified Person declarations and other product-supporting quality documents.
Manage change controls, deviations and self-inspections for the Elanco Ireland entity, support audits and inspections, communicate potential market issues to authorities, and share knowledge of European Union pharmaceutical quality expectations across the organisation.

What You Need to Succeed (minimum qualifications):
Qualified Person status for veterinary medicinal products in accordance with Regulation 2019/6 and applicable veterinary Good Manufacturing Practice requirements.
A minimum Master’s degree in a relevant scientific discipline.
At least two years of experience in a Quality department within a pharmaceutical site, or equivalent.
Demonstrated knowledge of pharmaceutical regulations, Good Manufacturing Practice and Good Distribution Practice.
Working knowledge of Microsoft Office, Veeva and SAP.

What will give you a competitive edge (preferred qualifications):
Experience with veterinary medicinal products and European batch release activities.
Practical experience managing quality systems, including change controls, deviations and self-inspections.
Experience supporting regulatory authority inspections, audits or market issue notifications.
Experience preparing quality documentation such as procedures, work instructions, site master file content or Qualified Person declarations.
Experience working with cross-functional European quality organisations and communicating quality information in English.

Additional Information:
Location: Dublin, Ireland.

Your opportunity at Sanofi

Ready to turn your academic knowledge into real-world experience?

Join Sanofi, a global biopharmaceutical company, through our 23-month Graduate Programme in Waterford. Explore three different functions, gain hands-on industry experience and develop the skills to shape your future career.

Quality Systems & Compliance is at the heart of delivering safe, effective, and compliant healthcare products to patients worldwide. This programme offers graduates the chance to build expertise in quality management, problem-solving, and regulatory excellence while making a tangible impact on product quality and operational performance.

One programme. Three rotations. A world of experience.

Why explore just one area when you could experience three?

Our structured Graduate Programme takes you through two 8-month rotations, and 7-month, providing exposure to different functions, meaningful projects and opportunities to learn from experienced professionals.

Your rotation journey

Rotation 1: Quality Systems & Data Integrity | Months 1–8

Start your journey in Quality Systems, where you'll gain an understanding of GMP compliance, data integrity principles, and quality documentation processes that help ensure the safe and reliable manufacture of healthcare products.

Support the Data Integrity Quality Improvement Programme (QIP) through quality systems, documentation, and compliance activities.
Conduct routine GMP and data integrity checks, helping to identify and address quality issues while ensuring proper documentation practices are followed.
Assist with technical writing, document management, CAPA follow-up activities, and initiatives that strengthen inspection readiness and continuous improvement across the site.

Rotation 2: Compliance | Months 9–16

Build your expertise in Compliance, working closely with teams responsible for maintaining inspection readiness and ensuring adherence to GMP and regulatory requirements.

Participate in internal audits and compliance assessments, helping identify opportunities for process improvements.
Support inspection readiness activities by reviewing documentation, tracking actions, and coordinating with operational teams.
Monitor SOP compliance and contribute to initiatives that strengthen quality culture and regulatory adherence across the site.

Rotation 3: Advanced QMS & Compliance Projects | Months 17–23

In your final rotation, you'll take on more ownership through strategic quality and compliance projects, applying the knowledge and skills developed throughout the programme.

Lead or support complex CAPA investigations, identifying root causes and implementing sustainable corrective actions.
Coordinate audit activities, working with stakeholders to prepare documentation, track commitments, and support successful outcomes.
Contribute to cross-site quality initiatives, such as QMS harmonization projects, process improvements, or compliance enhancement programmes with regional or global impact.

Your development focus

Throughout the programme, you'll develop knowledge and practical skills to support your future career in Quality Systems and Compliance, building the expertise required to ensure products, processes, and quality systems meet the highest regulatory and operational standards.

Develop a strong understanding of quality management principles, regulatory requirements, GMP compliance, and Quality Management Systems (QMS) within a highly regulated industry.
Strengthen cross-functional collaboration, communication, project management, and stakeholder engagement skills through exposure to diverse teams and business processes.
Build expertise in risk assessment, problem-solving, root cause analysis, CAPA management, auditing, and continuous improvement methodologies to support effective decision-making and operational excellence.

Your growth, our commitment

Your development is at the heart of our programme. Here's what you can look forward to:

Three diverse rotations: Explore different functions and build a broader understanding of the business.
Dedicated cross-functional mentor: Receive guidance from an assigned mentor, with monthly check-ins throughout the programme.
A buddy in every rotation: Get practical, day-to-day support as you settle into each new team.
Hands-on training: Learn directly from experienced colleagues and develop skills through practical experience and training opportunities.

Who we're looking for

We're looking for curious, motivated graduates who are eager to learn, collaborate and explore new opportunities.

To be eligible, you'll need to:

Have graduated within the past two years or be due to graduate before 1 September 2027.
Hold a minimum 2.1 primary degree or a Master's degree in a relevant discipline such as Quality Assurance, Pharmaceutical Sciences, Biological Sciences, Chemistry, Biotechnology, Microbiology, Engineering, or a related Life Sciences field.
Have full, unrestricted right to work in Ireland.

Essential skills:

Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to assess risks and identify effective solutions.
Excellent communication and collaboration skills, with the confidence to work across diverse teams and stakeholders.
Strong organisational and project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
High attention to detail and a commitment to quality, compliance, and continuous improvement.

Desirable qualifications:

Previous internship, placement, research, or work experience within a regulated industry such as pharmaceuticals, biotechnology, medical devices, or healthcare.
Knowledge of Quality Management Systems (QMS), GMP requirements, or regulatory compliance pr

jobs.description:
At U.S. Bank, we’re on a journey to do our best. Helping the customers and businesses we serve to make better and smarter financial decisions, enabling the communities we support to grow and succeed in the right ways, all more confidently and more often—that’s what we call the courage to thrive. We believe it takes all of us to bring our shared ambition to life, and each person is unique in their potential. A career with U.S. Bank gives you a wide, ever-growing range of opportunities to discover what makes you thrive. Try new things, learn new skills and discover what you excel at—all from Day One.

As a wholly owned subsidiary of U.S. Bank, Elavon is committed to building the platforms and ecosystems that help over 1.5 million customers around the world to achieve their financial goals—no matter what they need. From transaction processing to customer service, to driving innovation and launching new products, we’re building a range of tailored payment solutions powered by the latest technology. As part of our team, you can explore what motivates and energizes your career goals: partnering with our customers, our communities, and each other.

We actively uphold transparent and fair hiring practices that support individual opportunity, inclusive culture, and career mobility across all levels of our organisation.

We offer meaningful opportunities for growth, a culture of inclusion, and a strong commitment to transparency and integrity in everything we do.

Job Description

The Human Resources team supports employees throughout their career with U.S. Bank, from recruitment and onboarding through to learning, & development, talent, employee relations, total rewards, organisational change and HR risk. Our goal is to create an environment where our people and our business can thrive.

Based in Cherrywood, Dublin you will join our HR team on a 18 month Graduate Programme designed to give you broad exposure to Human Resources, with a particular focus on project and programme management.

You will work alongside HR colleagues and business stakeholders, supporting projects that help deliver our People strategy and wider business priorities.

Through a combination of hands-on experience, structured development and exposure to different areas of HR, you will build both your HR knowledge and project management capability.

What you'll learn and experience

During the programme, you will have the opportunity to:

Support the planning and delivery of HR projects and programmes from initiation through to implementation.
Develop project plans, track milestones, actions, risks and dependencies.
Coordinate meetings, workshops and project activities involving colleagues across HR and the wider business.
Gather and analyse people data to help measure progress and support decision-making.
Prepare project updates, presentations and communications for a range of stakeholders.
Support change management and communications activities to help embed new HR initiatives.
Build relationships with stakeholders across different HR functions and business areas.
Identify opportunities to improve HR processes and the employee experience.
Take increasing ownership of project activities as your knowledge, confidence and experience develop.
Complete a CIPD qualification as part of the programme, supporting your professional development and building your knowledge of HR best practice.

What we're looking for

We're looking for someone who is curious about people, business and how projects can drive change. You don't need to start the programme as an HR or project management expert. We'll support you in developing those skills.

You'll ideally bring:

An degree/masters in HR, Business/Management, Psychology or another relevant discipline.
A strong interest in developing a career in Human Resources and project management.
Good organisational skills and the ability to manage multiple priorities.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Confidence working with data and presenting information clearly.
A collaborative approach and an interest in working with different teams and stakeholders.
Curiosity, initiative and a willingness to learn.
Good working knowledge of Microsoft 365, particularly Excel, PowerPoint, data analysis
Available to start on the 1 Feb 2027

What you'll gain

By the end of the programme, you'll have developed practical experience of delivering HR projects, managing stakeholders, using data to inform decisions and supporting organisational change, alongside a broad understanding of how different HR functions work together to deliver a People strategy.

 Few more details

18 month fixed term contract
Location: Cherrywood. The role offers a hybrid / flexible schedule, which means there's an in-office expectation of 3 or more days per week and the flexibility to work outside the office location for the other days.
Ideally graduated in 2025 or 2026 with 1 year or less experience.
This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship. Candidates must have the right to work in Ireland.

Accessibility

Total Rewards

U.S. Bank is committed to fair, equitable, and transparent compensation practices in line with local regulatory and legal requirements. Our total rewards approach is designed to attract, retain, and support top talent while ensuring equal pay for work of equal value.

We offer a market-competitive compensation package that includes:

Clearly defined salary ranges aligned with industry benchmarks and internal equity standards.

Performance-based incentives for eligible employees (as defined by relevant plan rules), awarded through transparent, objective criteria that recognize both individual and company performance.

Inclusive equitable benefits that are accessible to all employees and focused

If you’re an undergraduate looking for a 12 month placement before you head back to university for your final year, we’d love to hear from you. If you’re in your last year at university or have already graduated, head back to the careers website to find other roles across the business.

Job Description

What you’ll need

Whether your degree is in Fashion Design, Graphic Design or Textile Design – you'll show us a creative portfolio that we wish was ours. You’ll want to drive newness every single time, and you’ll thrive from meeting deadlines and shifting priorities. Of course, you’ll be happy to handle your own projects with the support of others, whether you’re hand-drawing or working directly on the Mac.

If you’re a creative multitasker who can put their ideas across to others, and you have working knowledge of Adobe Creative Cloud, Illustrator, Photoshop, and InDesign, the Primark placement in Design is the perfect fit for you.

What you’ll do

You’ll help research and design a commercial range, from considering new techniques and fabrics, to finding out about, and then adapting the latest trends into Primark handwriting. It’s your chance to create typographically strong graphics and prints alongside our Design team and develop garment shape design.

You’ll gain an understanding of our products over time, but there will be detail too — you’ll follow briefs carefully, track amends and prepare design files for meetings with suppliers and more.

Qualifications

Why should you apply?

In Primark, we’ve always said everyone’s invited and we’re committed to making everyone feel safe and comfortable to be themselves. We believe that a diverse, inclusive, and accessible environment elevates us all, and enables creative ideas and collaboration to flourish. Because when we work together, we can accomplish so much more.

And yes, this place moves fast, and it’s growing even faster but we’re committed to providing the best, and most socially and environmentally ethical fashion that’s affordable for everyone. Primark Cares is our commitment to reducing fashion waste, halving our carbon footprint, and improving the lives of the people who make our products.

This placement has real impact, you could even see the results of your work, out on the shop floor! Make your CV look amazing and if you wow us, there could be a permanent job up for grabs when you graduate.

Isn’t it time you put theory into practice? We think so. Apply now for a Primark placement and start owning your journey.

Additional Information

About the placement

You don’t watch from the sidelines around here — you get stuck in. Through hands-on experience and responsibility from the get-go, you’ll gain a vast insight into how our business works and contribute to it from day one. Inspiring, supportive colleagues will make you feel welcome and valued. And we’ll also help you to develop your skill set and grow your potential through supported learning with on-the-job training, masterclasses, and an assigned buddy.

Before applying, please ensure that if you are offered a place on the programme, it has been approved by your university or educational institution.

Closing date: Friday, 6th November 2026. We reserve the right to close the application window early should we receive sufficient applications

jobs.title: Civil / Structural Engineer
jobs.description:
Location: Cork, Little Island
Employment Type: Permanent
Date Posted: 05/Nov/2026
Civil / Structural Engineer

About Us

Arcadis is the worlds leading company in sustainable design, engineering, and consultancy for natural and built assets. With over 36,000 professionals in 70+ countries, we are united in improving quality of life and solving the worlds most complex challenges.

Location/s: Based in our Little Island, Cork offices.

Role description:

Reporting to the CSA Department Manager, the Civil / Structural Engineer will be a member of the CSA Department supporting the delivery of civil and structural design services for major pharmaceutical and industrial clients. The role will have a predominantly civil engineering focus, with primary responsibility for underground drainage, underground electrical and utility services, site development works and drainage impact assessments. The Civil / Structural Engineer will also undertake structural engineering design and support structural project delivery as required.

The successful candidate will work as part of multidisciplinary project teams, taking responsibility for civil engineering deliverables from concept, planning, basic design, detailed design, tender and construction. The post-holder will be expected to deliver and manage their own design scope, coordinate inputs from other disciplines and deliver technically robust solutions to agreed programme and quality requirements.

The Civil / Structural Engineer will work closely with Architects, Structural Engineers, building services engineers and other discipline teams to ensure civil and structural designs are coordinated, compliant and suitable for construction. The post-holder is expected to demonstrate the Arcadis Core Values at all times.

Key Responsibilities

Interface with client design teams, local authorities, utility providers and project stakeholders as required.
Take responsibility for the delivery of civil engineering design scope within agreed budget and programme.
Prepare engineering calculations, drainage impact assessments, reports, specifications, schedules and design documentation.
Design foul, surface water and process drainage systems, including gravity and pumped systems, attenuation, flow control and SuDS measures.
Design and coordinate underground water mains, electrical ducting, utility corridors and other buried services, including clash avoidance and interfaces with foundations and external works.
Prepare site development designs including roads, pavements, levels, earthworks and external works drainage.
Undertake structural design and assessment work, including reinforced concrete and structural steelwork, foundations, equipment supports and modifications to existing structures.
Coordinate surveys, ground investigation information and utility records, and identify design risks or information gaps.
Lead or contribute to technical, constructability, safety and compliance reviews.
Support planning, statutory consent and BC(A)R compliance activities where required.
Coordinate design activities with architecture, structural, process, mechanical, electrical and other disciplines.
Identify and communicate technical issues that may impact quality, cost or schedule.
Attend and contribute to design, client and site meetings as required.
Undertake site visits during construction and support the resolution of requests for information and technical queries.
Contribute to the continuous improvement of departmental procedures, checklists and technical guidance.
Promote Arcadis Behavioural Standards and Equality, Diversity & Inclusion.

Minimum 5 years post-graduate design experience, with a predominantly civil engineering background. Experience in the industrial, pharmaceutical, life sciences or similarly regulated sectors is preferred.

A third-level qualification in Civil Engineering or Civil / Structural Engineering.

Chartered Engineer status or membership of a recognised professional body is preferred, ideally MIEI.

Why Arcadis?

We can only achieve our goals when everyone is empowered to be their best. We believe everyone's contribution matters. Its why we are pioneering a skills-based approach, where you can harness your unique experience and expertise to carve your career path and maximize the impact we can make together.

Youll do meaningful work, and no matter what role, youll be helping to deliver sustainable solutions for a more prosperous planet. Make your mark, on your career, your colleagues, your clients, your life and the world around you.

Together, we can create a lasting legacy.

Our Commitment to Equality, Diversity, Inclusion & Belonging

Were dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone thrives. Through six ED&I workstreamsAge, Disability, Faith, Gender, LGBT+, and Racewe foster innovation by embracing diverse perspectives.

Join Arcadis. Create a Legacy

jobs.title: Customer Insights Analyst – 12 Month FTC
jobs.description:
Tech that takes you places

We’re CarTrawler, the global travel tech company behind seamless connections between people, places and possibilities. From powering car rental to creating smarter ways to move, we make travel smoother for millions worldwide. Our culture is built on curiosity, collaboration and craic where every idea counts and every journey matters. Ready to make an impact? Let’s go places together.

CarTrawler’s Customer team champions travellers and partners alike. We create experiences that are simple, seamless and human whether supporting customers directly or collaborating with partners to improve every interaction. By listening, analysing and acting with empathy, we ensure that our service not only solves problems but builds lasting loyalty.

Your Journey starts here!

Turn data into insights that make a real difference to our customers and our business. Joining our Customer Insights team on a 12-month fixed-term contract, you’ll take ownership of key reporting and analysis, helping teams understand performance, uncover opportunities and make confident, data-driven decisions. You’ll create intuitive reporting that enables colleagues to explore data independently, while using emerging AI capabilities to make our insights smarter and more proactive. It’s a role with plenty of scope to collaborate, experiment and develop your skills as our approach to analytics and AI continues to evolve.

What you’ll do as a Customer Insights Analyst
Turn data into action by analysing complex datasets and translating your findings into clear, practical insights that improve customer and business performance.
Own and evolve key reporting, maintaining and improving dashboards while developing new automated and self-service reporting that helps teams make better decisions.
Partner with teams across the business to understand their challenges, define reporting requirements and provide the insights they need to operate effectively.
Build confidence with data by sharing your expertise through training and workshops, helping colleagues interpret insights and use data effectively in their day-to-day decision-making.
Support forecasting and forward-looking analysis, helping teams move beyond understanding what happened towards identifying what could happen next.
Explore the potential of AI, testing emerging technologies and developing AI-enabled insights, alerts and workflows that improve efficiency and support smarter decision-making.
What you’ll bring to the team
2–3 years’ experience working with data and analytics, with examples of turning analysis into meaningful insights and business outcomes.
Strong data analysis skills, including advanced Excel or Google Sheets capabilities and a working knowledge of SQL, alongside the curiosity and confidence to learn new tools.
Experience creating clear, engaging data visualisations, ideally using Tableau or a similar reporting and visualisation platform.
Confidence working with complex datasets from multiple sources, with an analytical mindset and a structured approach to investigating and solving problems.
An interest in AI and automation, with some exposure to generative AI tools or large language models and an appetite to explore how they can improve reporting, analysis and workflows. Experience with Python or R would be a welcome bonus, but isn’t essential.
A collaborative and proactive approach, with strong communication skills, the ability to manage competing priorities and an openness to different perspectives and new ideas.

Go on, give it a go!
We know that looking for a new job can feel a bit daunting but don’t let a touch of imposter syndrome hold you back. Even if you don’t tick every box, we’d still love to hear from you! Apply today to stay connected.

At CarTrawler, we’re proud to be an equal opportunities employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for everyone. No matter your background, identity, or life experience, if you’re passionate about what you do, you’ll be welcomed here.

Hybrid Working & Eligibility: Our hybrid working policy requires employees to work onsite at our CarTrawler Dublin office a minimum of 2 days per week.

Applicants must have an existing right to work in Ireland without the requirement for employment permit sponsorship to be considered for this role.

We may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of the hiring process, such as reviewing applications, analyzing resumes, or assessing responses and identifying potential inconsistencies or verification signals in application materials based on available information. These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. If you would like more information about how your data is processed, please contact us.

jobs.title: Trainee Merchandiser – Placement Student
jobs.description:
Company Description

Trainee Merchandiser — Student Placement Year

Because you’ll make the difference

Ready to own your career in an ever-growing fashion hub? Then take on a Primark placement starting in Summer 2027. This is your chance to grab valuable experience in a global company that truly feels like a family. You’ll have real projects with real autonomy. You’ll get to know incredible experts who make our fashion a reality. And you’ll gain off-the-scale exposure, making a huge impact for our customers and your future. Want it? Then own it on our undergraduate placement programme.

Because you matter

People are at the heart of what we do, so it’s essential that we provide you with the right environment to perform at your very best. We offer benefits that put you first:

Pay rate: Generous EUR 30,000 salary
Development: A 12 month development programme which kicks off with our Freshers Week
Balance: Our ‘Your Day, Your Way’ approach means you can finish up at 2pm every Friday if you’ve done your 37.5 hours that week
Discounts: Use your in-store colleague discount across our fabulous range
Support: Explore our well-being initiatives and Employee Assistance Programme, Let’s Talk. As well as mentorship to get the most out of your year
Holiday: Enjoy 27 days holiday on top of the Bank Holidays

And if you need to relocate to Dublin for the role:

We’ll support you with opening a bank account and registering for tax and social security in Ireland.
Not sure where to live? Primark will help with finding accommodation for the year.

About you

If you’re an undergraduate looking for a 12 month placement before you head back to university for your final year, we’d love to hear from you. If you’re in your last year at university or have already graduated, head back to the careers website to find other roles across the business.

Job Description

What you’ll need

You have a genuine connection and interest in numbers and figures, an eye for detail and a real awareness of timelines — even when the pressure is on. You’ll use your curiosity to get to know our network of professionals and drive excellence. You won’t be short of initiative either. In fact, you’ll be happy to handle your own workload with the support of others. If you’re studying Fashion, Business Management, Accounting, Economics, Mathematics or a Commercial based degree, the Primark placement in Merchandising is the perfect fit for you.

What you’ll do

After induction, you’ll get stuck into sales and stock monitoring, solving data inaccuracies, and producing analysis reports. You’ll learn about a department by doing real work with your teams on tasks and projects.

You’ll strengthen relationships and share your ideas at team meetings, grow what you know at masterclasses, and have regular catch ups with your assigned buddy and line manager to support your development. So when you present to your Director at the end of your placement, you won’t be short of things to say.

Qualifications

Why should you apply?

In Primark, we’ve always said everyone’s invited and we’re committed to making everyone feel safe and comfortable to be themselves. We believe that a diverse, inclusive, and accessible environment elevates us all, and enables creative ideas and collaboration to flourish. Because when we work together, we can accomplish so much more.

And yes, this place moves fast, and it’s growing even faster but we’re committed to providing the best, and most socially and environmentally ethical fashion that’s affordable for everyone. Primark Cares is our commitment to reducing fashion waste, halving our carbon footprint, and improving the lives of the people who make our products.

This placement has real impact, you could even see the results of your work, out on the shop floor! Make your CV look amazing and if you wow us, there could be a permanent job up for grabs when you graduate.

Isn’t it time you put theory into practice? We think so. Apply now for a Primark placement and start owning your journey.

Additional Information

About the placement

You don’t watch from the sidelines around here — you get stuck in. Through hands-on experience and responsibility from the get-go, you’ll gain a vast insight into how our business works and contribute to it from day one. Inspiring, supportive colleagues will make you feel welcome and valued. And we’ll also help you to develop your skill set and grow your potential through supported learning with on-the-job training, masterclasses, and an assigned buddy.

Before applying, please ensure that if you are offered a place on the programme, it has been approved by your university or educational institution.

Closing date: Friday, 6th November 2026. We reserve the right to close the application window early should we receive sufficient applications

jobs.title: Front of House (FOH), Veterinary Clinic, Full Time
jobs.description:
Location: Greyabbey Veterinary Hospital

Reports to: Lead Vet

Schedule: 40 hours per week

Salary: €29,432.00 to €31, 500 depending on experience

About the role

The ideal candidate will be passionate about customer service and delivering an excellent client experience; you will be the first point of contact for clients and patients at our clinic.

Greet all visitors and welcome them to the clinic

Answer and direct phone calls

Schedule appointments

Checking in patients

Collecting payments

Maintain records as necessary

Manage the receptionist area and assist with admin tasks as needed

Assist Vet nurses and Vets with patient care when necessary

Undertaking additional tasks as may be assigned

About you

Minimum 2 years reception experience (required)

Ideally one-year Veterinary receptionist experience

Ability to maintain a positive attitude

You are highly motivated, hard-working, and a strong team player

You have excellent customer care and communication skills and a genuine commitment to delivering the highest standards of animal welfare and patient care

What’s in it For You… At a Glance

We are proud to support our team members and encourage any interest in further education. In addition to our fabulous teams and supportive environments, we’re proud to offer a benefits package that supports our team’s wellbeing, growth, and families:

Health cash plan

Pension scheme

Gym membership subsidy

Free pet health plan

VCI Registration and VDS Indemnity fees paid

Funded CPD including, allowances, webinar series, new graduate programme, training platform access, and certificate funding

Statutory sick pay

Length of service holidays

Charity paid leave

Maternity/ Paternity benefits

Bike to work scheme

You must be legally eligible to work in Ireland.
